job.name: Android AOSP Device Software Engineer
job.description:
Calling all innovators - find your future at Fiserv. We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title Android AOSP Device Software Engineer

About Your Role Clover, a Fiserv company, is a global leader in point-of-sale platforms powering millions of small businesses worldwide with integrated hardware, software, and payment solutions. The DeviceOS engineering team owns the core platform software running across all physical Clover smart devices and supports global mass manufacturing software pipelines. As a Staff AOSP Engineer based in Sunnyvale, CA, you will serve as the technical authority driving custom Android OS architecture, system framework modifications, low-level platform security, and factory provisioning to deliver a secure, high-performing device experience.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead functional solution architecture, product requirements, and technical designs for custom Android Open Source Project (AOSP) builds across current and next-generation payment terminals.
  • Design, develop, and optimize Android system services, background daemons, and framework-layer components (frameworks/base/) compatible across multiple Android OS versions.
  • Bridge high-level application frameworks with low-level C/C++ native layers, working alongside Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) and kernel teams.
  • Partner directly with global manufacturing partners and test engineers to build, maintain, and optimize factory flashing tools, diagnostic software, and board bring-up daemons to achieve 100% manufacturing yield.
  • Architect platform security workflows, including PKI certificate provisioning, SELinux/SEAndroid policies, and HSM or ARM TrustZone integrations.
  • Responsibilities listed are not intended to be all-inclusive and may be modified as necessary.

Experience You’ll Need To Have

About The Team Consumer Monetization builds the experiences and systems that power how customers purchase and pay for OpenAI products. Our scope spans purchasing flows, payments, subscriptions, and billing, along with the shared capabilities that support new products, offers, and distribution channels.

We own both customer-facing experiences and the underlying platforms that power them. We partner closely with Product, Design, Growth, Data Science, and engineering teams across OpenAI to make purchasing effective and reliable, and new offerings easier to launch and monetize.

The work spans improving conversion, performance, and reliability, building reusable components, and enabling new product launches. You’ll combine product judgment with technical depth to set direction, lead initiatives across teams, and remain hands-on through implementation and delivery.

Approximately 50% of the work will initially be native mobile development, with the remainder across web and product APIs. We’re looking for engineers who enjoy working across the stack and have concrete examples of doing so professionally. Depth in either iOS or Android is required; experience in both is not required.

This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office.

In This Role, You Will

  • Architect and build purchasing and subscription experiences across native mobile, mobile web, and supporting product APIs.
  • Partner with Product, Design, and Growth to identify customer needs, prioritize improvements, and shape technical direction for purchasing experiences.
  • Improve conversion, performance, and reliability through experimentation, product analytics, and customer insights.
  • Develop reusable purchasing components and capabilities that help teams launch and monetize new products.
  • Collaborate with engineering and cross-functional partners to deliver reliable purchasing experiences and support product launches.

job.name: Mobile Engineer (iOS / Android)
job.description:
About The Role The role is for an engineer who owns the mobile experience end-to-end - shipping native and cross-platform features that millions of users interact with daily, on both iOS and Android.

The engineer will work alongside product managers, backend engineers, and designers to solve problems where performance, offline behavior, release velocity, and user experience all matter equally. This is a hands-on build role on a well-funded team shipping to production every week.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and ship user-facing features across iOS and Android using Swift/Kotlin and/or a cross-platform framework (React Native or Flutter)
  • Integrate with REST and GraphQL APIs, handling offline caching, background sync, and retry strategies for unreliable networks
  • Own app performance: profiling startup time, memory usage, render performance, and bundle size; driving measurable improvements release over release
  • Write and maintain automated test suites (unit, integration, UI) and contribute to CI/CD pipelines for builds, releases, and store deployments
  • Monitor production apps using Crashlytics, Sentry, or Firebase; triage and resolve crashes, ANRs, and performance regressions
  • Participate in architecture reviews, code reviews, and technical decision-making on the mobile platform roadmap
  • Collaborate with design and product to implement polished, accessible UI that matches specifications across device sizes and OS versions

What We Are Looking For

  • 3–7 years of software engineering experience, with at least 2 years building and shipping production mobile apps
  • Deep proficiency in Swift/Objective-C or Kotlin/Java; strong working knowledge of iOS (UIKit/SwiftUI) and/or Android (Jetpack Compose) SDKs
  • Experience with mobile architecture patterns: MVVM, MVI, or clean architecture; dependency injection; modular app design
  • Track record of shipping apps to the App Store and/or Google Play, including release management and store review processes
  • Strong debugging and profiling skills using Xcode Instruments, Android Profiler, or equivalent tooling
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience
  • Bonus: Experience with React Native or Flutter, Kotlin Multiplatform, mobile CI/CD (Fastlane, Bitrise, Xcode Cloud), and building for low-connectivity or offline-first use cases

  • Mentor Android engineers on accessibility best practices, run onboarding sessions, and share knowledge broadly (docs, newsletters, external talks).

You're Our Person If...

  • 5+ years Android engineering experience, including Kotlin and Jetpack Compose in a team environment
  • Hands-on expertise with Android accessibility APIs and TalkBack behavior.

Residency All applicants must currently reside in the United States Overview BigBear.ai is seeking an Android Developer to join a mission-focused cyber team supporting critical national security objectives. In this role, you’ll build and sustain custom Android capabilities used by operational teams in fast-moving, real-world environments. You’ll work side-by-side with end users to understand evolving needs, translate them into technical solutions, and deliver reliable tools that perform under pressure. This is a hands-on engineering position with end-to-end ownership from initial design through development, testing, debugging, documentation, and ongoing enhancements where speed, quality, and mission impact matter.

What You Will Do

  • Design and develop custom software tools and techniques for the Android platform
  • Own end-to-end development: requirements, design, implementation, testing, and sustainment
  • Diagnose and debug issues using COTS/GOTS tools and internal frameworks
  • Apply a strong understanding of networking concepts and protocols to tool development
  • Produce documentation needed to operate, maintain, and support delivered software
  • Mentor and guide junior developers to accomplish mission objectives
  • Respond to and solve time-sensitive, real-world cyber problems

What You Need To Have

  • Must have an active U.S. Government Top Secret (TS) clearance, Full Scope Polygraph (FSP), or the ability to obtain one
  • Must have at least 5+ years of experience
  • Experience developing, testing, and debugging in Python and C
  • Experience building UNIX applications using make files (or similar build environments) on mission-relevant platforms
  • Experience developing CNO tools and techniques
  • Strong socket programming and packet-level understanding of IP, TCP, and application-layer protocols
  • Proficiency in tracing execution with debuggers/tools such as WinDbg, gdb, IDA Pro
  • Experience reverse engineering native binaries
  • Experience developing proof-of-concept exploit software
  • Knowledge of OS internals, including topics such as:

+ runtime linker/loader concepts
+ object file formats (e.g., ELF)
+ file system internals (e.g., NTFS, ext2, btrfs)
+ access control mechanisms (MAC/DAC)
+ process/thread APIs, data structures

  • Understanding of modern mitigations (ASLR, DEP, NX), approaches to bypass them, and methods to detect bypass attempts
  • Experience with version control (e.g., git, GitLab)

What We'd Like You To Have

  • Native-level mobile development experience (Android native/NDK or similar)
  • Vulnerability analysis experience
  • Assembly familiarity, preferably ARM
  • Understanding of mobile security protections (e.g., SELinux, application sandboxing)
  • Experience with Objective-C, Swift, C++
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities

Overview of Role:

The AI Forward Deployed Engineer partners directly with business stakeholders to identify high-value opportunities and convert them into secure, scalable and measurable AI solutions. The role combines strong software engineering, generative AI and machine learning capability with stakeholder-facing delivery. It owns the journey from discovery and rapid prototyping through enterprise integration, production deployment, adoption and continuous improvement.

KPIs:

  • Business Impact: Measured value delivered through AI solutions, including efficiency, quality, revenue, cost or risk outcomes.
  • Time to Production: Speed and predictability in progressing priority use cases from discovery and proof of concept to production.
  • Solution Quality and Reliability: Accuracy, relevance, latency, availability, scalability and operational stability of deployed solutions.
  • Adoption and Stakeholder Satisfaction: Active usage, stakeholder feedback and successful integration into business workflows.

  • Prioritized Delivery Roadmap: Create and maintain a roadmap based on business value, feasibility, data readiness, risk and resource needs.
  • Prototypes and Proofs of Concept: Develop rapid prototypes to validate technical feasibility, user value and solution direction.
  • Production AI Solutions: Build, deploy and operationalize selected AI solutions with appropriate security, scalability, reliability and support readiness.
  • Enterprise Integration: Integrate AI capabilities with enterprise applications, identity systems, APIs, data sources and operational workflows.
  • Evaluation and Observability: Establish evaluation, error-analysis, logging, metrics, tracing, usage and cost-monitoring mechanisms.

The role: The Senior Release Engineer is the senior practitioner and standards-setter for Meridian’s Release Engineering function. Environment Operations — Dev & QA

  • Implement and operate Dev and QA environments following CI/CD standard
  • Meet environment parity and promotion criteria by construction; remediate drift findings before they reach the readiness gate
  • Convert recurring environment requests into self-service; measure and report the manual effort retired each quarter

Release Pipeline Support

  • Maintain release-build pipelines for assigned estates within the shared pipeline templates; support release execution to Release & Service Governance’s gates
  • Provide build and environment support during critical release windows as scheduled

Continuous Improvement & Standards

  • Lead improvement initiatives across build and environment practice; pilot tooling with Platform Engineering and produce structured findings for the Sr. Manager

job.description:
Summary Job Description

SAP Private Cloud Operations (PCO) Delivery provides private cloud managed services for SAP applications. The PCO Delivery Technical Operations team is responsible for 24x7 operation of business-critical SAP systems in the cloud. We are looking for a Senior Linux, Cloud & Pacemaker Administrator to support our multinational team across Azure, AWS, Google Cloud and SAP data centers. The role focuses on Linux platform engineering, hyperscaler operations and strong hands-on Pacemaker production support. The administrator will ensure reliable operation of existing high-availability clusters, resolve complex production issues, improve architecture and design, implement new cluster configurations, and develop automation that strengthens service quality and operational efficiency.

Role Information As a Senior Linux, Cloud & Pacemaker Administrator, you will serve as the last line of defense and L3/L4 escalation point for complex Linux operating system, infrastructure, cloud and Pacemaker incidents across public cloud, private cloud, VMware and bare-metal platforms. You will identify and correct design weaknesses, remove single points of failure, standardize Linux and cluster operations, and automate repetitive activities. The role is accountable for stability, security, resilience, high availability and recoverability of environments running business-critical customer systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Operate Linux-based SAP infrastructure across Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, SAP data centers, VMware and bare-metal environments in a global 24x7 model.
  • Administer Pacemaker production clusters, including resources, constraints, quorum, fencing/STONITH, failover behavior, maintenance, upgrades, and recovery.
  • Troubleshoot high-impact Linux, Pacemaker, cloud, and infrastructure incidents; perform root-cause analysis and drive corrective and preventive actions.
  • Review cluster designs, resolve architectural weaknesses, implement new high-availability configurations and validate controlled failover and recovery scenarios.
  • Manage Linux lifecycle activities including installation, configuration, upgrades, patching, hardening, performance tuning and vulnerability remediation.
  • Administer hyperscaler compute, identity, availability zones/regions, load balancing, monitoring and security controls supporting critical workloads.
  • Troubleshoot networking, including TCP/IP, routing, VLANs, VPNs, VPC/VNet, NAT gateways, firewalls, security groups, load balancers and hybrid connectivity.
  • Operate DNS and related infrastructure services such as LDAP, NTP, and proxy services, including name-resolution dependencies affecting hosts, clusters, and SAP workloads.
  • Administer storage and network storage, including block and file storage, S3, Cloud Storage, NFS, multipathing, mounts, capacity, performance, and storage-related failover issues.
  • Improve resilience and high availability through redundancy, failure-domain awarene

job.name: Software Development Manager, Mobile App Foundations
job.description:
Description How would you like to lead a team whose work reaches hundreds of millions of customers and every engineer who builds for the Amazon Shopping app? Our organization builds the foundational services, frameworks, and tools behind the Amazon Shopping experience on iOS and Android. As a Software Development Manager, you will lead a team of engineers building the core capabilities that feature teams across Amazon use to ship quickly and safely.

The engineers on our team have a wide range of skills, and we want your passion for mobile to make the team even stronger. We raise the bar on the mobile shopping experience by building the frameworks, services, and code that thousands of developers across Amazon depend on. We think in terms of frameworks, not features, and we care about stability, scale, and performance more than trying new technology for its own sake.

About you: You are a technical leader who wants to grow your passion for mobile. You like building systems that other teams can take on once and get value from without extra work. You're comfortable getting into the details of architecture, operational metrics, and incidents to find root causes. You hold a high bar for quality while keeping your team unblocked and shipping. You enjoy managing a team and helping engineers grow, and you earn trust with partners by turning unclear, cross-team problems into clear plans with owners and dates.

About us: We're changing the way customers shop on mobile. Along the way we'll face hard, interesting problems that no one else has seen. We rely on our camaraderie, diversity, and strong culture to find solutions that challenge our first assumptions, to make hard decisions, and to deliver something better than what we started with.

If you want to build the foundation that the Amazon Shopping app runs on, we'd like to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

You will lead, hire, and develop a team of software engineers. That means setting clear expectations, coaching engineers as they grow, and building a strong bench of technical talent. You will own the technical direction and roadmap for the foundational mobile services and frameworks used across the Amazon Shopping app. You'll also drive architecture and design decisions that balance scale, reliability, performance, and developer experience.

You will put operational excellence first. You'll define the metrics that matter, keep the on-call rotation healthy, and invest in automation that removes recurring operational work. You'll hold a high bar for engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, and good testing practices.

job.name: Principal Engineer
job.description:
The Principal Engineer is the most senior individual contributor in the System Platform Team. This is not an architect-in-an-ivory-tower role - it is a hands-on technical leadership position where roughly 60% of time is spent writing production code and 40% on cross-cutting technical responsibilities: architecture, technology evaluation, design reviews, and mentoring. The expectation is that when the team runs into its hardest technical problem, the Principal is the one who unblocks it - not by delegating, but by pairing or by writing the solution.

Over the course of the year, the Principal intentionally rotates across different engineering domains - developer experience, release engineering, data and messaging, incident and compliance tooling. This breadth is deliberate: by the end of the year, the Principal has deep firsthand knowledge of the full platform codebase, which is what makes their architecture reviews, technology decisions, and mentorship credible across all areas.

The Stack You Will Work On

  • A Java/Spring Boot microservices platform (GreyMatter) running on GKE, backed by Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, and MinIO/S3
  • An Erlang/OTP real-time robot-control system (Butler Core) running on GCP VMs, using Mnesia, EMQX (MQTT broker), and Cowboy HTTP
  • A hybrid CI/CD setup spanning GitHub (mono-repo for 19 platform services) and Bitbucket (legacy/firmware repositories), with Jenkins, Spinnaker, ArgoCD, Nexus, Terraform, and Ansible
  • Kafka-based event streaming with Avro schema contracts and Redis for payload management
  • An internal context-retrieval server that surfaces runbooks, tickets, deployment history, and architecture docs as LLM-queryable tools
  • An incident management platform (evaluating commercial tools vs. in-house) with a custom compliance evidence layer for SOC2/ISO audits
  • A home-grown Just-In-Time access portal covering GKE, GCP IAM, Kafka ACLs, SQL, Mnesia, and config management, integrated with Google Workspace SSO.

Responsibilites Architecture & Technical Direction

  • Lead cross-team architecture reviews - help the team make large technical decisions, document trade-offs, and land on durable solutions
  • Own build-vs-buy decisions: evaluate commercial tools against in-house alternatives with documented analysis, and live with the consequences
  • Define and enforce engineering standards across the whole team: schema conventions, observability patterns, security postures, secrets hygiene, API design
  • Review system designs across every engineering area the team works in - not just the area you are currently contributing to
  • Partner with the Associate Director on technical hiring: contribute to interview design, loop calibration, and leveling decisions

Hands-On Engineering

job.name: Engineering Manager, Endpoint Sensor - CTIO (Hybrid)
job.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

*About CrowdStrike Falcon (Endpoint Security)* CrowdStrike Falcon Endpoint Security is a two-component security product.

One component is the “sensor”: an agent installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon cloud. The sensor processes thousands of events per second to provide deep visibility into operations on the endpoint, and performs rich correlation and computation to identify malicious events and block malicious activity.

The other component is the cloud: it aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network, correlates malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

*About The Team:* The CTIO (Chief Technology Innovation Officer) team at CrowdStrike defines and executes on the company's technology vision and strategy, driving innovation, and overseeing the development and evolution of the Falcon platform. We deliver cutting edge innovation for our sensor across Windows, macOS and Linux. We ensure that CrowdStrike maintains its position as a technology leader by fostering engineering excellence, aligning technical capabilities with business objectives, and anticipating emerging threats and market trends.

*About The Role:* As an Engineering Manager, you'll lead a team working on user-mode security architecture on Windows, where reliability, performance, and resource footprint all matter.

job.name: Head of Information Security
job.description:
ABOUT WAY

Way is building the AI, data, and infrastructure layer for the experience economy.

As artificial intelligence automates labor and people reclaim time, the shift toward spending on experiences over things only accelerates. Way sits at the center of that shift as the platform, intelligence layer, and curated marketplace on which experiences are created, distributed, and sold.

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Austin with offices in Paris and San Francisco, Way built the category of experiences in hospitality from the ground up, during a pandemic that had shut the industry down. Leading global travel, retail, lifestyle, and hospitality brands leverage Way, including Hyatt, Hilton, Alaska Airlines, Aspen, Piaget, and countless others.

Way’s position is layered by design: a proprietary data network built on millions of experiential data points, the system of record for experiential operations, an e-commerce layer embedded directly into partners’ customer journeys, and a marketplace through Partner Exchange, where brands across hospitality, travel, lifestyle, and retail co-create and co-sell experiences with one another. Every brand that joins makes the network more valuable to every brand already on it.

That combination of data, workflow, distribution, and network effects is not something that can be vibe-coded into existence. It compounds. It is what positions Way as the durable infrastructure for the experience economy regardless of how the technology landscape evolves.

Way is backed with $22m in capital from Tiger Global and strategic family offices and angel investors. The company has mid-8 figures of ARR from a global enterprise customer set, with outstanding growth and efficiency metrics.

THE ROLE

Way is hiring a Head of Information Security to lead security across the product, the cloud environment, and the company.

The world’s leading hotel brands, airlines, and loyalty programs trust Way with guest and member data. You’ll be accountable for protecting it, and you’ll be the person those partners speak to about security.

You’ll report to the COO, work hands-on, and partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Operations. This is a build role. You’ll set the program, choose the partners, and do much of the work yourself.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

job.name: Security Engineer, Security for Employee and Legal Systems (SEALS)
job.description:
Description The Security for Employee and Legal Systems (SEALS) team protects Amazon's enterprise HR and Legal applications. Millions of Amazonians use these systems to review their pay, manage their benefits, update their personal information, and handle confidential legal matters. Protecting that data is the core of what SEALS does, and the customers who depend on us are the people who work here.

The applications we protect are increasingly built with GenAI, and many of them now embed GenAI features and agentic workflows of their own. That shifts the security work. You will threat model LLM-backed applications, assess risks such as prompt injection, insecure model output handling, and over-broad agent permissions, and secure transitive authentication as agents act on behalf of users. You will also use GenAI to scale your own delivery, from automated code review to detection authoring.

SEALS delivers ambient security. Builders get security feedback while they write code, at commit time, so risks are caught and fixed during development. As a Security Engineer on SEALS, you will be an embedded partner to your builder teams and own the security outcomes for your domain.

Strong candidates bring depth in application security: threat modeling, architecture and design reviews, secure code review, and hands-on remediation. You will contribute autonomously within the team, deliver risk reduction across the full lifecycle, and mentor peers, while seeking guidance from managers and technical leaders on the hardest tradeoffs.

Key job responsibilities

  • Own the security outcomes for your assigned SEALS builder teams and the HR and Legal applications they run.
  • Threat model GenAI and LLM-backed applications, covering risks such as prompt injection, insecure output handling, data leakage through model context, and excessive agent authority.
  • Secure agentic workflows, including transitive authentication and scoped authorization as agents act on behalf of users.
  • Author and refine automated detection rules that catch risks at code commit and give builders a fix they can accept immediately.
  • Use GenAI to scale delivery across your domain, including AI-assisted code review, detection authoring, and triage.
  • Drive paved-path adoption (Secure CDK Blueprints, automated patching, standardized authorization, transitive authentication for agentic workflows) so preventable issues do not occur.
  • Hunt for risk the tooling missed through adversarial analysis and manual secure code review in Java, Python, and JavaScript, then turn each escape into a new detection.
  • Provide security architecture guidance and lead the security outcomes of design reviews for your team and customers.
  • Prioritize remediation by business impact, and escalate to leadership when a builder wants to accept a launch-blocking risk.
  • Communicate security outcomes clearly, in writing and verbally, to security and service team leadership.

job.name: Senior Corporate Trainer
job.description:
Module 1: Cloud and AI Foundations on Google Cloud

Goal: Give everyone the same technical starting point on Google Cloud (GCP) and its AI tools.

What you learn

  • Core GCP services: compute, storage, networking, IAM
  • Managed services vs. custom infrastructure
  • Vertex AI, pre-built models, AutoML and custom training
  • Working in Vertex AI Workbench notebooks

Activities

1. Set up the lab, connect to BigQuery, run a sample query and review IAM roles.
2. In pairs, map where Hartford India sits on an AI maturity scale. The results feed the capstone.

Outcome: A working Vertex AI environment, a shared vocabulary and an AI maturity map.

Module 2: GenAI, Embeddings and RAG

Goal: Learn how large language models connect to company data like policies, claims and underwriting guidelines.

What you learn

  • How a GenAI app is built: model, prompt, retrieval and response
  • Embeddings: "water damage", "flood loss" and "pipe burst" are grouped by meaning
  • RAG with BigQuery Vector Search for grounded, auditable answers

Activities

1. Build a GenAI app with no retrieval and judge its answers.
2. Build a full RAG pipeline on Hartford-style documents and compare grounded vs. ungrounded answers.
3. Diagnose three faults (poor chunking, embedding mismatch, missing grounding instruction) and fix them.

Outcome: A working RAG pipeline and the ability to spot why RAG fails. The Claims Intelligence Assistant is scoped as a real use case.

Module 3: Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Systems

Goal: Build agents that decide, use tools and act, using Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK).

What you learn

  • What makes a system agentic: tools, memory, planning, execution
  • Multi-agent setups on Agent Engine
  • Production concerns: speed, reliability, fallback and cost
  • Four design patterns: orchestrator-specialist, pipeline, parallel fan-out, human-in-the-loop

Activities

1. Build a Policy Lookup Agent with two tools and test where it fails.
2. Build a Claims Triage system: an Intake Agent sorts claims as standard or complex, and a Coverage Assessment Agent gives a preliminary decision with a confidence score.
3. Choose the right design pattern for three Hartford use cases.

Outcome: A deployed multi-agent system and the skill to question agentic proposals.

Module 4: Agent Evaluation and AI Economics

Goal: Learn to check whether an agent works and what it costs to run.

What you learn

  • Five evaluation checks: task completion, tool choice, output quality, speed under load, how failures happen
  • Cost drivers: model usage, embeddings and retrieval, extra agent steps, infrastructure
  • Build vs. Buy decisions for AI tools

Activities

job.name: Site Reliability Engineer
job.description:
Trackunit is a fast-growing company and a leading supplier of IoT solutions, operating out of many offices worldwide. Trackunit specializes in digital solutions that connect machines, people, and systems in the global construction industry. The construction industry is the least digitalized industry of all. This lack of digitalization has left construction far behind a global economy on the rise and placed the industry as one of the least productive industries too.

We are looking for a Site Reliability Engineer who wants to run and protect the platform that every Trackunit service is built on, keeping it secure and available for the developers and customers who depend on it. You join the North America half of our SRE team, which works with colleagues in Europe to cover the platform around the clock. This is a mid-level role, and we prefer London, Canada as location, with applications welcome from across Canada.

Keep the platform running and secure. What you run is the foundation for everyone else at Trackunit: our main customers are the Trackunit developers, who build every service on top of it. You see the effect of your work quickly, and you help shape how the platform grows as we prepare it to run in different parts of the world.

With locations in the hearts of London, ON and Kitchener, ON we offer you a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations or remotely from anywhere in Ontario. No relocation assistance is offered for this position.

The Site Reliability Engineer position is currently open at Trackunit . The base salary hiring range for this role is $80,000–$110,000 CAD per year , depending on experience and qualifications.

Once in the role, successful candidates will have the opportunity to progress through the full salary range based on performance and development over time. This range reflects base salary only and does not include additional elements of our total rewards offering, such as our remote work policy, health benefits, retirement savings, and other rewards.

What’s in it for you?

  • Own a foundation, not a feature. Everything else at Trackunit is built on what you run.
  • See your impact quickly. Vulnerability scores and insights move fast, often by the next day, and other teams thank us for the changes we make for them.
  • Work next to security. You work closely with our dedicated security team, from the SRE side, on the platform everyone builds on.
  • Bring your ideas. The SRE team is often the first to propose a change or new automation, and you are encouraged to bring ideas to the table.
  • Grow in a global team. Colleagues across Europe and North America, formal ladders for promotion and improvement, regular one-to-ones with open feedback, and flexibility in how you work.

Who are you ideally? You are an infrastructure engineer with a security mindset who thinks in systems, and who cares that things stay safe and highly available.

job.name: Développeur(se) en fiabilité de site

MaintainX is a leading mobile-first work execution platform for industrial and frontline teams. More than 15,000 customers , including McDonalds, Michaels, Cintas, Redimix, and U.S. LBM, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 16 million managed assets and 92 million completed work orders. In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining Autodesk Operations Solutions , the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations. Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours. Nous recherchons un·e développeur(se) en fiabilité des sites (SRE) pour contribuer à améliorer la fiabilité, l’observabilité et l’autonomie des développeurs chez MaintainX, alors que nous faisons évoluer notre plateforme.

Dans ce rôle, vous collaborerez étroitement avec les équipes de développement produit et plateforme afin d’améliorer la stabilité, la résilience et la préparation opérationnelle de nos services. Vous travaillerez aux côtés des équipes pour concevoir la fiabilité dès le départ, définir clairement les responsabilités ainsi que les standards, et développer des outils partagés permettant aux équipes d’exploiter leurs services en toute confiance.

Vous contribuerez également à des initiatives à l’échelle de l’entreprise qui définissent l’approche de MaintainX en matière d’ingénierie de la fiabilité, notamment les standards d’observabilité, les pratiques de gestion des incidents et les indicateurs de santé des services, en aidant l’organisation à adopter des pratiques éprouvées de l’industrie à grande échelle.

Ce poste convient particulièrement à un·e développeur(se) qui aime travailler de manière transversale, influencer l’orientation technique grâce à de solides pratiques de développement, et transformer les principes de fiabilité en systèmes concrets, évolutifs et pérennes.

  • Participer à l’évaluation du niveau de maturité des services et formuler des recommandations aux équipes de développement
  • Collaborer avec les équipes de développement afin de mettre en place les meilleures pratiques en matière d’observabilité
  • Permettre aux équipes de développement de gagner en autonomie dans le déploiement, le soutien et l’exploitation de leurs services et de leur infrastructure
  • Encadrer et accompagner les développeurs sur les pratiques de fiabilité, en mettant l’accent sur leur autonomie

We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Device Trust Platform team , the group responsible for the lower-level platforms that power 1Password Device Trust and that will, over time, underpin Device Security and the broader 1Password security platform. These systems ingest, process, and store a high volume of telemetry from the devices our customers depend on. Our customers expect this to work with Tier 0 reliability: the services this team owns are always on, and when something fails, it fails over without anyone noticing.

This is an end-to-end team responsible for the data pipelines, storage systems, and infrastructure that keep the product reliable at scale, as well as the application code that runs on top of them. You will lead a group of senior and staff engineers who are already deep in this architecture, and you will grow the team over time, adding engineers as the platform's scope expands and onboarding new hires into a team with high operational standards.

You will be responsible for the resiliency and reliability of our applications. That means owning availability targets, incident response, capacity, and the architectural decisions that keep a multi-region system honest. It also means running a healthy engineering team: planning, design reviews, career growth, and hiring. The role reports to the Senior Manager, Engineering for Device Trust.

Job Title SRE1(Linux System administrator) Job Description The Linux System Administrator is responsible for day-to-day administration, maintenance, and support of Linux-based systems. This role focuses on system stability, patching, monitoring, and incident resolution while following established standards and procedures.

  • Install, configure, and maintain Linux servers (RHEL/Ubuntu/Rocky/CentOS), both physical and virtual.
  • Manage core services: SSH, DNS, DHCP, NTP, LDAP/SSSD, postfix, NFS/SMB, systemd, and cron management.
  • Apply patches and kernel updates; maintain package repos (yum/dnf/apt).
  • Monitor system health and performance (top, iostat, sar, vmstat, netstat; or via Prometheus/Zabbix).
  • Implement backup/restore routines (e.g., Veeam/Bacula/NetBackup); test recoveries.
  • Manage storage (LVM, mdadm RAID, multipath, iSCSI/FC) and filesystems (ext4/xfs/btrfs).
  • Harden hosts per baseline (CIS/STIG), firewall rules (iptables/nftables/firewalld), SELinux/AppArmor.
  • Write basic automation/scripts (Shell script; optionally Python, Ansible playbook) for routine tasks.
  • Respond to incidents; perform root cause analysis; document runbooks and SOPs.
  • Support users/dev teams with environments, permissions, and troubleshooting.

Required Skills

  • Solid understanding of Linux OS fundamentals.
  • Experience with systemd, networking, storage, and filesystems.
  • Package management, log analysis (journalctl, syslog).
  • Storage and filesystem management; backup fundamentals.
  • Familiarity with monitoring tools (i.e. Nagios)
  • Basic virtualization (VMware/KVM/Nutanix) and/or container basics (Docker).
  • Basic scripting skills (Shell script); version control (Git).
  • Understanding of security best practices: SSH keys, PAM, auditing (auditd).
  • Ability to follow procedures and work under supervision.

Educational Background And Working Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT, or related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 3-5 years administering Linux(Rocky/RHEL/Ubuntu) in production.
  • Certifications (nice-to-have): Red Hat RHCSA, CompTIA Linux+, LPIC-1.

Salary Range CAD $75000-$100,000

  • Develop predictive models and machine learning systems to better understand market behavior and identify trading opportunities
  • Analyze large-scale market and order-flow data to uncover signals, evaluate hypotheses, and improve trading performance
  • Build and test statistical and stochastic models for pricing, forecasting, and risk management

What You’ll Get: You’ll join a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and excellence, surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem-solvers. job.name: Production Engineer, Facilities
job.description:
About Fluidstack We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply! How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.
  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.
  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.
  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.
  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Production Engineering Team Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Scaling the systems which make the physical plant observable and operable as one fleet. Building the telemetry, alarm, topology, and health systems that allow operators and automations to see the true state of power, cooling, and environmental infrastructure across every site.
  • Turn facility incidents into a closed repair loop. Automate the path from detection and diagnosis through maintenance, remediation, validation, and return to service so failures do not disappear into handoffs between software, engineering, vendors, and site operations.
  • Bring new sites and equipment into production safely at construction speed. Build repeatable readiness gates, commissioning signals, staged deployments, canaries, and rollback mechanisms for a fleet growing by multiple sites at once.
  • Keep operators ahead of power and cooling risk. Build capacity views, safeguards, anomaly detection, service-health reviews, and operational tooling that identify problems before they affect customers.

job.name: Senior Software Engineer, Infrastructure
job.description:
Courier Health is on a mission to solve one of the biggest and most meaningful opportunities in healthcare: reinvent how people living with chronic and rare diseases are supported.

We are building the future of patient engagement for life sciences companies. Our software is leveraged by biopharma companies to support patients in their complex journey from diagnosis to initiating and remaining on therapy to achieve optimal health outcomes.

Come Build with Us

We're a NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We’re an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. If that sounds like your kind of place, we think you'll love it here.

The Opportunity

Courier Health is at an inflection point. We exist to get patients faster, better access to life-saving therapies, and every one of those patients depends on infrastructure that is reliable, secure, and ready to scale. The platform our engineers build on determines how quickly we can ship for our customers and how quickly patients feel it. This role owns that.

You'll design, deploy, and evolve our serverless-first AWS platform (Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, AppSync, and Aurora) along with the multi-account architecture, CI/CD pipelines, and guardrails that let every engineer move fast and ship with confidence. It's a rare combination: deep technical ownership at an early-stage company, in a domain where the stakes are real. If you're motivated by the opportunity to have an outsized impact on not just your company, but the healthcare industry at large, this is the role.

What You'll Build

A serverless platform that scales with our growth. Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge, AppSync, and Aurora are the core of what you'll operate and evolve. You'll keep it fast, reliable, and secure as our customer base and data volumes grow and provide the architectural guidance that helps teams build systems worthy of it.

Guardrails that make the right thing the easy thing. You'll own our AWS multi-account architecture: account hierarchy, Service Control Policies, and IAM Identity Center. You'll build and maintain the CI/CD pipelines and broader developer platform that make compliant-by-default the path of least resistance for every engineer on the team.

Observability and security we can stake the mission on. We work in healthcare so system health isn't optional. You'll implement and manage the monitoring and alerting that keep us ahead of problems, and proactively identify and address security vulnerabilities and infrastructure risk with an automation-first mindset that scales hardening without slowing delivery.

Set the architecture, roadmap, and acceptance criteria by which multi-thousand-GPU clusters are declared production-ready, and establish the performance bar (collective bandwidth, job goodput, model FLOPs utilization) that every cluster must clear before and after customer handover. Establish technology and product direction in collaboration with other tech leads, managers, and senior leadership.
  • Run and instrument real AI workloads as a diagnostic instrument. Stand up and execute distributed training and inference jobs — open-source and customer-representative models — across thousands of accelerators to validate cluster behavior under genuine load rather than synthetic proxies alone, and translate what those runs reveal into fleet-wide fixes.
  • Lead deep diagnosis of large-scale cluster failures and performance regressions, isolating root cause across the full stack: GPU and NIC firmware, PCIe/NVLink topology and NUMA placement, InfiniBand/RoCE fabric health, congestion control and routing, storage and data-loader throughput, scheduler placement, and framework/communication-library behavior. Serve as the final escalation point for the hardest slow-job and stalled-job investigations.
  • Design and build the validation and burn-in systems that qualify nodes, racks, and full pods at scale — NCCL/RCCL collective sweeps, HPL/HPCG and MLPerf-style benchmarks, thermal and power soak tests, straggler and flapping-link detection — and automate them so that qualification is a repeatable pipeline, not a manual campaign.
  • Drive cluster optimization end to end, tuning fabric configuration (adaptive routing, QoS and congestion control, SHARP in-network reduction, rail and topology-aware placement), collective communication libraries and algorithm selection, GPUDirect RDMA and storage paths, and host-level settings (huge pages, IRQ affinity, CPU governors, MIG and driver configuration) to convert raw hardware into delivered throughput.
  • Partner with Infrastructure, Platform, SRE, and customer-facing teams to translate operational and customer performance needs into durable engineering solutions, and to feed diagnostic signal back into provisioning, remediation, and capacity workflows.
  • Build production-grade Python systems and performance too

job.name: Lead, Engineering Backup
job.description:
Engineering Manager, Atlas Infinite Backup

New York City

MongoDB powers mission-critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, recoverable, and fast to access. Atlas Infinite is our next-generation cloud-native architecture that decouples compute from storage, and its storage layer continuously backs every cluster up to cloud object storage. The Atlas Infinite Backup team builds the systems that turn that stream of data into something customers can trust: point-in-time recovery, retained snapshots, fast restores, disaster recovery, and backup storage that stays affordable as clusters grow to hundreds of terabytes.

We are hiring an Engineering Manager to lead this team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who takes the responsibility of durably storing and recovering customer data seriously, is comfortable with the economics of large-scale storage, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users.

About The Atlas Infinite Backup Team The team is part of MongoDB's Backup and Object Storage Services organization and works hand in hand with Storage Layer Services, the disaggregated storage layer behind Atlas Infinite. We own the object storage tier: everything that happens to a cluster's data after it leaves the hot path and lands in cloud object storage. Because backup is a property of the storage layer rather than a separate agent copying files, the team works on the storage engine's write path, data layout, and lifecycle as much as on backup features.

The team's responsibilities include:

  • Continuous backup of log and page data to object storage, and the indexing that lets a cluster's full history be located and read efficiently
  • Point-in-time recovery, snapshot retention, and restore for clusters at the scale of 100+ TB per shard, including cluster-level and collection-level restore
  • Compaction and garbage collection of the object store so that retained history costs what it should and no more
  • Cold data: serving and tiering infrequently accessed collections and indexes directly from object storage
  • Metering and billing for backup storage, including the model that decides what customers pay for retained snapshots and point-in-time recovery
  • Disaster recovery and compliance capabilities for Atlas Infinite, such as cross-region protection, retention policies, and data lifecycle guarantees
  • Operating these services in production across many cells and regions: observability, on-call, capacity, and cost

What you'll do

You will lead the development of an AI agent that can autonomously investigate production incidents, identify likely root causes, create safe mitigation plans, and execute them while humans supervise and can intervene. You will improve the agent's accuracy, autonomy, and real-world impact, while identifying other opportunities to apply agentic systems across incident prevention, detection, mitigation, observability, and infrastructure operations. This may include improving the agent's architecture, context, and tooling, or adapting foundation models through fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, distillation, pruning, and inference optimization.This is an applied engineering role, not a research position. The ideal candidate combines deep infrastructure expertise with sound judgment about when and how to apply AI to production problems, a long-term technical vision, and the ability to move quickly from an ambitious idea to a production system operating safely at Meta scale.This is also a deeply hands-on senior IC role. You will personally prototype, build, evaluate, and ship AI systems, working directly in the code and with production data. A central challenge is creating systems that improve from experience: learning from outcomes, identifying their own failure modes, testing changes, and safely increasing their effectiveness over time.

job.name: AI Systems Engineer, Codex Agents
job.description:
AI Systems Engineer - Codex Core Agents About The Team The Codex Core Agents team builds the agent harness that turns model capability into real-world action. We own the systems around the model: prompting and interpreting model outputs, executing actions safely in real environments, and feeding production experience back into better models and better agent behavior.

This team sits close to research and works across the stack: harness, model interaction, inference, sandboxed execution, orchestration, evals, production reliability, and the performance envelope around tokens, latency, cost, capacity, and quality. The harness is open source and increasingly part of how models are trained and evaluated, making this one of the highest-leverage layers in Codex.

About The Role We’re looking for engineers to build the AI systems that make Codex agents dependable in production. The ideal candidate is an agent-systems builder: hands-on across low-level systems and ML workflows, able to debug Codex behavior end to end across the harness, model behavior, inference/runtime stack, GPU fleet, and product surface.

You’ll work with research, infrastructure, and product to design agent harness capabilities, run experiments and ablations across the model + system prompt + harness stack, build frameworks for assessing production agent performance, and turn messy failures into durable improvements.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and build the core agent harness and execution loop that lets Codex agents interpret model outputs, use tools, execute code, and complete long-horizon tasks safely.
  • Build sandboxing, isolation, orchestration, state, and workflow infrastructure for agents operating in real development environments.
  • Develop evaluation, experimentation, and debugging systems that distinguish harness issues, model behavior, inference/runtime issues, and product failures.
  • Run ablations across prompts, model-facing interfaces, context construction, tool-use strategies, and harness behavior to improve solve rate, reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Improve observability, profiling, and diagnostics across the agent stack, from backend systems to inference, GPUs, and fleet capacity.
  • Work closely with research to make the harness trainable, measurable, and useful for improving frontier agentic models.
  • Build shared primitives that make Codex faster, safer, more reliable, and easier for other teams and open-source users to build on.

job.name: Site Reliability Engineer (Starlink)
job.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SITE RELIABILITY ENGINEER (STARLINK) At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to 9M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for the world’s best engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

As a Site Reliability Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges that improve our ability to fully utilize the hardware we have deployed. Our goal is to provide customers with the best possible satellite internet experience, often providing under-served communities with affordable, life-changing broadband internet access.

Aerospace experience is not required for success here - rather, we look for smart, motivated, and collaborative site reliability engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a truly inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.

Responsibilities

  • Upgrade existing distributed systems to become sharded and geo-redundant in multiple data centers
  • Advance existing deployment, monitoring, and alerting infrastructure to support a multi-region environment
  • Manage petabyte scale bare metal compute clusters
  • Closely collaborate with engineers across all programs to create highly operable, scalable, and maintainable products
  • Engage throughout the whole software development lifecycle of services -- from inception to design, deployment, operation, and iterative refinement
  • Focus on performance bottlenecks and performance improvement techniques

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems/IT, or an engineering discipline and 1+ years of professional experience in systems administration, site reliability engineering, or DevOps; OR 3+ years of professional experience in systems administration, site reliability engineering, or DevOps in lieu of a degree
  • 1+ years of professional experience with Linux operating systems

This role involves debugging, performance design and optimization, and working on containerized solutions using Docker. Experience with FastAPI, Python, and React front-end is essential.

  • Lead and mentor an 8-10 person engineering team, fostering a collaborative and innovative environment.

  • Write clean, scalable, and maintainable code in Python and React.

  • Drive end-to-end execution: design, build, test, deploy, and run in production.
  • Be accountable for how the product handles consumer data: privacy, retention, access, and compliance obligations including India’s DPDP Act.
  • Communicate status, risk, and bad news early and clearly to stakeholders.

job.name: QA Specialist / SDET
job.description:
Quality engineering for a specification-driven world

At Bosenet, software is increasingly built through a cycle of Understand → Specify → Design → Delegate → Generate → Review → Test → Validate → Improve . Requirements are written as structured specifications and significant parts of the implementation are produced with AI coding agents — which changes what testing means. Quality can no longer be inspected in at the end of a sprint; it starts at the specification, where ambiguity is cheapest to remove and where a sharp question from a tester prevents an entire class of defects.

We are looking for a hands-on QA specialist who is comfortable in the room when specs are being discussed, who designs their own test strategy rather than executing someone else's, and who is evolving towards an AI-native development lifecycle (AIDLC).

What you will do

  • Own the test strategy, methodology and quality approach for your products and integrations — you define it, you are not handed it.
  • Take part in specification and design discussions, and ask the questions that expose ambiguity, missing acceptance criteria, unstated assumptions and edge cases before code is written; push back where a specification is not testable.
  • Design and maintain automated suites with Playwright and/or Selenium — functional, regression, cross browser and end-to-end — plus API and integration automation for REST services, microservices, event driven workflows and SaaS integrations.
  • Run sharp exploratory and risk-based manual testing where automation is not the right instrument.
  • Wire tests into CI/CD pipelines so quality signals arrive continuously, not at release time.
  • Review AI-generated code and AI-generated tests critically — correctness, coverage gaps, silent assumptions, and tests that pass without proving anything.
  • Use AI assistants and agents for test design, test data, coverage analysis, failure triage and test maintenance, while keeping quality judgement under human control.
  • Drive defects to root cause, and cover non-functional quality: performance, security-relevant behaviour, accessibility, reliability and observability.
  • Communicate quality status, risk and release readiness clearly to engineers, architects and international customer stakeholders.

What we are looking for

  • Minimum 7 years of hands-on professional testing and QA experience on real, delivered software.
  • Demonstrable ownership of test strategy, test design techniques and methodology — not only test execution.
  • Strong automation experience with Playwright and/or Selenium : framework structure, locator strategy,

synchronisation, parallel execution and flake control.

  • Solid programming ability in at least one automation language (Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python or C#), and practical API testing experience (REST, JSON, auth, contract testing).

Read the full description

other the truth, and everyone here stays close to the infrastructure that makes AI work.

The Role This is a career-level SRE role for someone who wants to own systems, not just watch them. You'll take

real surface area: the automation and tooling other engineers depend on, and the reliability of

production services running AI and GPU workloads at scale. You'll sit in the incident rotation, and you'll

be expected to make the systems you touch quieter over time.

What You'll Do

  • Build and own the automation and tooling that keeps the platform running; treat operational toil as

a bug to be fixed, not a fact of life.

  • Define and maintain SLOs, SLIs, and the dashboards that make service health obvious at a glance.
  • Take point during incidents; troubleshoot under pressure, drive root cause analysis, and run post-

incident reviews that actually change the system.

then fix them at the source.

  • Partner with Engineering, Networking, and Infrastructure teams to raise the reliability bar across the

stack.

  • Improve availability, scalability, and efficiency through code, not manual effort.

What You'll Bring

  • 3-6 years in SRE, systems engineering, or software engineering, including time running production in

a data center or cloud environment.

  • Strong programming skills (Python, Go, or similar) and a genuine bias toward automating the work

away.

  • Solid command of Linux, networking fundamentals, and distributed systems.

asked.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with AI or GPU workloads, or high-performance computing (HPC).
  • Familiarity with high-performance networking (InfiniBand, RDMA).
  • Kubernetes, plus virtualized or bare-metal environments.

On-Call and Pace

A quick note on the shape of the job. This role sits close to production, so there is an on-call rotation,

and some weeks are busier than others. We share it fairly, and we treat every page as a signal worth

acting on rather than just an interruption. The goal is to make the systems quieter over time, so each

rotation asks less of the person carrying it. If you take ownership of what you run and like leaving it in

better shape than you found it, you'll do well here.

job.name: Site Reliability Engineer
job.description:
Who We Are

AI is changing how software gets built. Code production is becoming a commodity. The focus is shifting from writing code to specifying, orchestrating, verifying, and governing change – and the toolchain is the new constraint.

We are at the center of this shift. We build Develocity, a toolchain observability and intelligence platform used by some of the world's leading software organizations – Netflix, Airbnb, Spotify, SAP, major global banks, and hundreds more. Develocity helps software teams achieve delivery excellence through deep observability, build and test acceleration, and AI-powered intelligence across the entire toolchain – with support for Gradle Build Tool, Apache Maven™, sbt, npm, Python, and Bazel.

We are an AI-native company. AI is not a feature we're bolting on – it's central to how we work, how we think about our product, and where we're heading. Develocity encodes a decade of build and test expertise into a context engineering layer: the ground truth AI agents need to change code safely, and the governance to attribute and gate that change at machine speed. Trust, evidence, and explainability are at the core of everything we build.

We have partnered with the Apache Software Foundation, the Commonhaus Foundation, the Micronaut Foundation, and other OSS projects such as Spring, Quarkus, Kotlin, JUnit, AndroidX, and many more to bring the values of Develocity also to the OSS Community.

Our Values

Seek to Understand: Everything starts with listening and understanding, and we strive to understand different viewpoints, problems, and motivations. Before we take action, we ensure we truly grasp the challenges, perspectives, and goals.

Know the Why : We approach our work with a clear sense of purpose, ensuring every step is deliberate and focused. We take meaningful action with urgency, but never at the expense of thoughtful consideration.

Innovate & Iterate : We embrace challenges and are not afraid to try new things, even if they might fail. With deep understanding and a clear purpose, we can develop creative and bold solutions to tackle challenges.

Own the Outcome: We are empowered to take initiative and we maintain transparency in our work and its outcomes. When we execute, we take responsibility for our decisions, measure the success of our innovations, and learn from the results.

Who You Are

We're building a new SRE team and looking for founding members to help shape how we operate. You'll be responsible for the reliability, performance, and availability of Develocity instances serving paying customers, open-source projects, and public-facing services, plus supporting infrastructure like artifact registries.

job.name: DevOps Engineer
job.description:
About The Role The role owns the infrastructure that keeps production systems running at scale - Kubernetes clusters, CI/CD pipelines, and the observability stack that surfaces problems before customers notice them.

You will work directly with software engineering teams to build reliable deployment paths, drive down incident response times, and turn manual operational work into automated, repeatable systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain Kubernetes-based infrastructure on AWS, including cluster provisioning, autoscaling policies, and capacity planning
  • Build and optimize CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, with automated testing, canary deployments, and rollback strategies
  • Define infrastructure as code using Terraform, managing environments across multiple AWS accounts with peer-reviewed change processes
  • Own observability tooling - Prometheus, Grafana, and distributed tracing - building dashboards and SLO-based alerting that reduce noise and improve signal
  • Lead incident response for production outages, run blameless postmortems, and drive remediation work to completion
  • Harden security posture across the platform: IAM policies, secrets management with Vault, network segmentation, and container image scanning
  • Partner with development teams on service reliability - capacity reviews, load testing, and cost optimization across cloud spend

What We Are Looking For

  • 3–7 years of experience in DevOps, SRE, or infrastructure engineering roles supporting production systems at scale
  • Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production - deployment, debugging, RBAC, and cluster operations
  • Strong proficiency with Terraform and at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred), including networking (VPC, ALB/NLB, Route53)
  • Solid scripting and automation skills in Python, Go, or Bash; experience building internal tooling
  • Demonstrated experience with monitoring and alerting systems (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog) and incident management practices
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
  • Bonus: Experience with service mesh (Istio/Linkerd), GitOps workflows (ArgoCD/Flux), Kafka or other event streaming platforms, and SOC 2 compliance work

job.name: Site Reliability Engineer
job.description:
About The Role The role sits on a platform reliability team that keeps high-scale production infrastructure running - Kubernetes clusters, distributed services, and the observability stack that makes failures visible before users notice.

The team treats reliability as an engineering discipline, not an ops function: SLOs drive priorities, automation replaces toil, and every incident feeds back into architectural improvements across the fleet.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the reliability of core production services - defining SLOs/SLIs, building error budgets into release decisions, and driving remediation when budgets burn
  • Design and maintain Kubernetes infrastructure at scale, including cluster provisioning, autoscaling policies, and GitOps-based deployment workflows (ArgoCD, Terraform, Helm)
  • Lead incident response for production outages: triage, mitigation, postmortems, and follow-through on actionable action items
  • Build and evolve the observability stack - Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and distributed tracing - so engineers can debug issues in minutes, not hours
  • Automate away recurring operational toil by writing tooling in Go or Python that encodes runbooks into self-healing workflows
  • Partner with product engineering teams on capacity planning, load testing, and resilient system design before features ship

What We Are Looking For

  • 3–8 years of experience in SRE, DevOps, or infrastructure engineering, including at least 2 years running production systems at significant scale
  • Deep hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production - operating, debugging, and hardening clusters, not just deploying to them
  • Strong infrastructure-as-code skills with Terraform; comfort managing cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) at multi-region scale
  • Proficiency in at least one systems language: Go, Python, or Bash for tooling and automation
  • Demonstrated incident management experience and a track record of blameless postmortems that changed how systems were built
  • BS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience; deep understanding of Linux internals, networking (DNS, TCP/IP, load balancing), and distributed systems failure modes
  • Bonus: Experience with service mesh (Istio/Linkerd), chaos engineering practices, cloud cost optimization, or contributing to open-source infrastructure tooling

Inspire is a unique assessment service that supports the transition of internationally educated health care professionals into the global work force.

The British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (“BCCNM”) is the college empowered under the Health Professions Act to regulate the practice of all licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, registered midwives, registered nurses, and registered psychiatric nurses in British Columbia. Regulation helps to protect the public by ensuring that professional care or service received by the public is competent, ethical, and meets the standards that society views as acceptable.

As western Canada’s largest health profession regulator, we believe a diverse and inclusive team enriches our efforts to protect the public. We welcome applications from all who reflect of the communities we serve, and especially encourage Indigenous Peoples and members of equity-seeking groups to apply. We believe diverse perspectives and experiences bring both innovation and better outcomes to the work we do and the decisions we make.

BCCNM’s commitment to Indigenous Specific Anti-Racism BCCNM is committed to working with Indigenous Peoples and health system partners to support Indigenous-specific anti-racist practices in the health system. As the largest health regulator in Western Canada, BCCNM has the opportunity to influence the health professionals we regulate, as well as the broader health-care system, to break the cycle of racism, and improve health outcomes for Indigenous Peoples. BCCNM has pledged to become culturally safe and anti-racist, and to support the health professionals we regulate to do the same.

What We Offer You We promise to provide you with rewarding work that challenges you. You will be part of a passionate team contributing to our important mandate of protecting the public. As a member of the team, you can expect to be working in a collaborative, team-based environment, and treated in a respectful and professional manner.

job.name: Software Engineer, Developer Relations
job.description:
**Position: Software Engineer, Developer Relations - Apple Arcade

Location: Cupertino, CA (Hybrid) Duration: 12+ Months

Job ID:** 180001

**Pay Rate: $85/hr - $89/hr

Job Overview:**
Apple Arcade is a family-friendly subscription gaming service on the App Store featuring 150+ games with no ads or in-app purchases across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro. Our catalogue includes hits like Madden NFL '27 Arcade Edition, Balatro+, Hello Kitty Island Adventure, and Sneaky Sasquatch.
This role will place you at the technical center of our developer community, working shoulder to shoulder with the studios that build for Arcade. You will be the engineer other engineers come to, and you will represent Apple as the face of Apple Arcade engineering for our game development partners.

Description In this role, you will build deep technical expertise in an Apple-provided framework that Arcade partner studios integrate into their titles, and you will use that expertise to support those studios directly. That means owning the integration documentation and sample code, building tooling and test plans that prove an integration is correct, and rolling up your sleeves to debug alongside a partner when something does not behave the way the API promised.
You will serve as the primary engineering point of contact for partner developers through office hours, direct correspondence, and hands-on support. When issues come in, you will triage them, separate partner-side integration mistakes from genuine framework bugs, and file well-reproduced reports back to the framework's engineering team. Recurring pitfalls should not stay tribal knowledge, so you will turn them into documentation, self-serve tooling, and feedback that shapes the framework's own roadmap.
Because many Arcade titles are built in Unity, you will also build and maintain a Unity plug-in wrapper around the framework to make adoption dramatically easier for those studios. This is a hybrid developer-relations and partner-engineering role rather than a heads-down feature-building role, and it is a good fit for someone who is energized by unblocking other developers at scale. The API surface will continue to evolve while you are already supporting early integrations, so comfort with ambiguity matters as much as technical depth.

Minimum Qualifications

Our vision in DGX is to power Intuit's financial system of intelligence through trusted, AI-ready data and experiences that fuel breakthrough customer growth and services adoption. Within DGX, Sales Tech builds the platform and intelligence that powers how Intuit's sellers connect with prospective and existing customers across the full lead-to-cash journey. We are seeking a Senior Staff Software Engineer to be the technical anchor for our lead-to-cash domains: pipeline and forecasting, quoting (CPQ), contract lifecycle management (CLM), and order automation. Intuit has embraced a hybrid working model and this role will be based out of our Mountain View office 3 days per week.

  • Stay deeply hands-on, contributing roughly 40 to 60 percent to development across the software lifecycle, with the remaining time on architecture, technical strategy, and cross-team alignment.
  • Drive the most complex, ambiguous, cross-team technical problems to resolution, spanning multiple domains, and ensure end-to-end quality in both technology and customer experience.
