At Asana, security is foundational to our mission of helping teams work together effortlessly. Our security team protects Asana's employees, users, and customers by proactively addressing threats, ensuring compliance, and fostering a culture of security throughout our product and operations.

As the Security Risk Engineer, you will own Asana's internal security risk management program end-to-end. This is a senior role for someone who goes beyond frameworks and checklists — you will engineer the quantitative and automated foundations that let Asana continuously measure and make confident decisions about security risk. You'll build the systems and processes that make risk scalable, not just the policies that describe it, and serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership.

This role is based in our Vancouver, BC office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements

What You'll Achieve

  • Own Asana's security risk management program: Design and continuously mature a quantitative risk framework — including risk scoring methodologies, likelihood and impact modeling, and risk appetite thresholds — that enables consistent, data-driven risk decisions across the organization.
  • Build and maintain a living risk register: Own Asana's central security risk register, developing KRIs, tracking trends over time, and driving accountability for risk treatment and remediation with business and technical owners.
  • Automate risk identification and monitoring: Design and implement automated data pipelines and integrations that continuously surface security risks — pulling signals from vulnerability scanners, cloud security tooling, SIEMs, and third-party risk sources — so Asana's risk posture is always current and not dependent on manual review cycles.
  • Deliver quantitative risk reporting: Develop executive-level dashboards that communicate security risk in business terms — probability, potential impact, cost of control vs. cost of breach, and residual risk exposure — to inform investment and prioritization decisions.
  • Partner cross-functionally on risk: Act as the primary security risk partner to Legal, Privacy, Finance, and Engineering. Influence security investment decisions and build a culture of risk awareness across the company.

About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.

Detection engineering

  • *Track detection quality as measured quantities* : coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.

Response & automation

  • *Own incident response:* triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.
  • *Build automation that removes toil* from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.

Telemetry & partnership

  • Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship , working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.
  • *Threat hunt proactively across the estate* , converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.

You Should Have

job.name: Principal Systems Engineer, Signal-Path Performance & Modeling
job.description:
About Neurophos The demand for new data centers and AI compute is rapidly outpacing the planet's energy capacity. Digital solutions are hitting a power wall as we approach the physical limits of traditional silicon. Conquering this bottleneck means rethinking the fundamental architecture of inference compute. The industry's current path can't meet the need, so we're taking a different approach.

Instead of traditional electronic circuits, we use silicon photonics and an active, programmable metasurface to perform matrix multiplications at the speed of light. Our optical cells are 10,000x smaller than traditional photonic components, enabling unprecedented density. By using photonics instead of electricity, our chips become more efficient as they scale. This architecture will deliver up to 100 times the energy efficiency of existing solutions while significantly improving performance for large-scale AI inference.

We’ve assembled a world-class team of industry veterans and recently raised a $110M Series A led by Gates Frontier. Participants include M12 (Microsoft’s Venture Fund), Carbon Direct Capital, Aramco Ventures, Bosch Ventures, Tectonic Ventures, Space Capital, and others.

Join us and shape the future of computing!

Location: Austin, TX. Full-time onsite position.

Reports To: Chief Systems Engineer

FLSA Status: Exempt

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly skilled Systems Engineer to own the quantitative, end-to-end performance model of our optical vector-matrix multiplication (OVMM) engine. This role is the technical center of Systems Engineering's performance-modeling focus area: you will lead the end-to-end modeling, analysis, and architectural definition of high-speed communication and signal-processing systems. In this role, you will build and maintain the link and power budgets; quantify impairments and non-idealities across the optical, analog, and digital domains; develop mathematical and behavioral models; define the hardware and algorithmic techniques required to meet aggressive system-level performance targets; and determine how accuracy, throughput, and power trade against one another as the architecture evolves.

You will spend most of your time running system-level simulations and translating them into defensible allocations the rest of the organization can design against. If you have deep communication-theory and signal-processing intuition, are fluent in turning a signal chain into a quantitative model, and want to be the person who can answer "where does the system actually lose its margin," this role will let you define the performance envelope of a first-of-its-kind computing platform.

job.name: Senior FastAPI Developer
job.description:
Who are we?

We build AI tools for firms in legal and professional services: software people use for real work, not demos. We started a few months ago and already have paying clients who rely on what we ship. The team is small and moving fast.

The role

You'll own the backend behind our AI features. That's the APIs, the data pipelines, and the orchestration sitting between our product and the language models doing the work. In practice it means running retrieval over large sets of documents, getting dependable results out of LLMs and their tool calls, streaming responses to the UI, and processing long jobs in the background without things falling over.

It isn't CRUD work. The hard parts here are keeping AI systems accurate and fast with confidential data, at production scale. You'll make architecture calls early and live with them.

Requirements What You'll Do

  • Designing and building the APIs and services our products run on.
  • Working on the AI plumbing: retrieval, orchestration, tool-calling, response streaming, and the evals that tell us whether the output is any good.
  • Keeping async and distributed work reliable: document ingestion, embeddings, and long-running jobs on Redis.
  • Building integrations with the systems clients already use, like email and document stores, and making them hold up under load.
  • Taking data security and isolation seriously, since clients hand us confidential material.

Who You Are

  • At least seven years building backend systems that run in production. Depth matters more to us than the number.
  • You think about how things fail, not just how they behave when everything's fine.
  • You've built real LLM-powered systems, or you're itching to: RAG, tool-calling, agents. You know where they tend to break.
  • You use AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) and use them well. Faster output, but you understand and stand behind every line; you wouldn't approve sloppy AI-written code in review, so you don't ship it either.
  • You're fine in a startup that changes direction. Decisions get made, then revisited.

Experience We Expect With The Stack

  • Python: 6+ years
  • FastAPI: 3+ years
  • PostgreSQL / SQL
  • Redis: 2+ years

Nice to have: RAG or vector search experience; LangChain or LlamaIndex; streaming over SSE, WebSocket or SignalR; Microsoft Graph and email integration work.

Visa Sponsorship At this time, Newcode is unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the applicable country without employer sponsorship.

Benefits Why Join Us?

  • Be a driver of innovation in one of Oslo’s most exciting AI ventures
  • Work with talented peers in a collaborative, high-energy team
  • Shape both product and culture as we grow
  • Flexible, English-speaking environment

job.name: Software Engineer, Backend, Growth
job.description:
About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is building an AI-native platform that changes how Go-to-Market and Product Growth teams create, launch, and improve customer-facing experiences. We are looking for a product-minded backend engineer to help build the infrastructure and services that power modern growth and marketing at Ramp.

The next chapter for this team is to build marketing-led products : intelligent tools that turn strategy into execution, automate complex workflows, and help teams operate across channels with dramatically more leverage.

The team will build across creative production, lifecycle marketing, paid media, account-based marketing, experimentation, incentives, and cross-channel orchestration. Examples include AI-powered systems that produce on-brand campaign assets, automate complex marketing workflows, coordinate audiences and execution, and deliver personalized experiences across email, sales outreach, external channels, and Ramp’s product.

A core part of this mandate is Ramp’s incentives platform. We are building shared infrastructure to safely target, authorize, distribute, redeem, and measure incentives across channels and mediums—including in-app experiences tied to product adoption and growth goals. This requires combining marketer-friendly workflows with governed policies, budget controls, reliable financial operations, and closed-loop measurement.

You will work at the intersection of product engineering, AI, data, marketing, and financial infrastructure. The ideal candidate is a product-minded backend engineer who can translate ambiguous workflows into durable systems. You will build the data models, APIs, integrations, and orchestration capabilities that allow marketers, product teams, and AI agents to safely execute complex work end to end.

What You’ll Do

job.name: Software Engineer I, Fullstack (Search)
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Search has become the default way consumers discover where to shop, compare options, and decide what to buy across platforms like Google, TikTok, and even Klarna. As we build a new Ads business and evolve Marketplace into a best in class shopping experience, improving search is one of our highest leverage investments to create an experience users choose and merchants want to invest in.

What You'll Do

  • With the support of your team, you will work on tasks that contribute to the team's projects and goals.
  • You will work collaboratively and proactively with your team and stakeholders, bringing them along for your work and helping to create visibility and dialog regarding the risks and trade-offs related to your work.
  • You will strike the right balance of speed and quality in your work, ensuring that we hit our business goals while protecting our systems from downtime.
  • You will contribute to a sense of community on your team by engaging in growth and development activities.

What We Look For

  • You have previous work or internship experience working with Javascript/Typescript.
  • You have previous work or internship experience designing, developing and launching backend systems at scale and are experienced using Python or Kotlin.
  • You have mastered taking a simple problem or business scenario into a solution that interacts with multiple software components, and executing on it by writing clear, easily understood, well tested and extensible code.
  • You are comfortable navigating a large code base, debugging others' code, and providing feedback to other engineers through code reviews.
  • Your experience demonstrates that you take ownership of your growth, proactively seeking feedback from your team, your manager, and your stakeholders.
  • You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.
  • This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

Base Pay Grade - J

Equity Grade - 5

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)

USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $130,000 - $180,000

USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $115,000 - $165,000

With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do.

At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits.

The individual will work at the forefront of 5G-Advanced and next-generation wireless technologies. This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys solving complex protocol challenges, developing production-quality software, and collaborating directly with leading wireless technology companies.

You will work closely with customer engineering teams and Keysight R&D to develop, customize, integrate, and optimize software solutions used in the development of next-generation wireless systems. Unlike traditional support or deployment roles, you will actively contribute code, debug protocol stack behavior, build software features, and drive technical solutions that influence both customer products and Keysight technology roadmaps.

This is a highly development-focused role requiring strong software engineering expertise and deep knowledge of 3GPP wireless protocols. Successful candidates will be comfortable investigating issues across multiple protocol layers, performing root-cause analysis, modifying production code, and developing software enhancements that directly address customer and product requirements. You will have the opportunity to influence both customer solutions and future Keysight product capabilities by translating field challenges into product enhancements, software innovations, and new technical approaches.

job.name: Senior Quantum Engineer - Quantum Systems
job.description:
Overview Microsoft Quantum has assembled a talented and diverse international team to create the world's first scalable quantum computing system. Our full-stack approach involves innovations from physics on the quantum plane through the hardware, software, and services needed to operate quantum systems at scale. For more information about the team, see Microsoft Quantum | Homepage .

The Quantum Systems team is looking for a Senior Quantum Engineer - Quantum Systems to help develop the devices, experiments, tools, and engineering methods needed to advance scalable quantum computing. The team designs and builds cryogenic systems, control and readout electronics, measurement instrumentation, software and automation, and supporting mechanical and electrical infrastructure; integrates these subsystems with quantum devices; and characterizes and validates integrated-system performance and reliability in room-temperature and cryogenic environments. As a Senior Quantum Engineer within this team, you will apply engineering and scientific methods, collaborate across disciplines, and turn experimental or simulation results into reliable technical progress.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

Responsibilities This role combines technical depth with hands-on engineering and cross-disciplinary collaboration. Key responsibilities of the role:

  • Design and conduct experiments or simulations, collect and analyze data, report results, and use findings to improve future work.
  • Develop equipment, devices, components, tools, or processes needed for quantum engineering and research.
  • Collaborate across hardware, software, and algorithm teams to understand subsystem requirements and interfaces, troubleshoot system-level issues, and validate integrated system performance.
  • Apply engineering best practices to improve reliability, repeatability, scalability, quality, and performance.
  • Create and maintain clear technical documentation, including methods, results, operating procedures, and guidance that other teams can reuse.
  • Identify technical risks or roadblocks, investigate failures, and communicate recommendations and progress to stakeholders.
  • Uphold safety, security, compliance, and secure-by-design practices in laboratory, engineering, and collaborative work.

Other

  • Embody our Culture and Values

Qualifications Required/Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Physics, Engineering, or related field AND 6+ years experience in industry or in a research and development environment

Do you thrive in fast-paced environments where you can design scalable systems, automate data workflows, and drive innovation through modern cloud technologies? If you enjoy solving complex data challenges and delivering solutions that have direct business impact, then the Worldwide Operations Finance Standardization & Automation (S&A) team has an exciting opportunity for you!

As a Data Engineer in WW Ops S&A, you will design, implement, and maintain scalable data infrastructure, ETL pipelines, and platform services that power enterprise-scale data discovery and analytics.   • Develop and optimize data models, metadata management frameworks, and catalog systems that enable fast, reliable data discovery for thousands of internal customers
  • Build and maintain microservices and APIs (API Gateway, Lambda) that power platform features including search, data ingestion, and cross-service integrations

Reality Labs' Systems Engineering team shapes the hardware architecture of future devices, from VR/MR headsets to AI wearables. As an intern on the team, you'll help turn user experiences and workloads into quantitative hardware requirements across compute, memory, storage, power, and thermal, and contribute to the trade studies that drive silicon and platform decisions. You'll be paired with a mentor and own a scoped project that lands in a real platform definition.This is a 12 week internship.

Hardware Systems Architecture Intern, Performance & Workload Analysis Responsibilities:

  • Translate target use cases into hardware requirements — budgeting compute, memory bandwidth, storage throughput, power, and thermal for experiences such as mixed-reality passthrough, always-on AI assistant, and camera capture
  • Contribute to architecture trade studies comparing SoC, memory, storage, and ISP options against performance, power, thermal, cost, and form-factor limits, using analytical models (e.g. roofline, bandwidth and power budgets) validated against measurements
  • Measure platform behavior under load at the system level using power-rail instrumentation, thermal chambers, and hardware performance counters, and use the data to calibrate models
  • Identify where performance is capped by hardware — memory bandwidth, power delivery, thermal headroom, I/O — rather than software
  • Characterize how requirements shift across product classes, from a tethered or high-power headset to a battery-limited wearable
  • Present findings to silicon, hardware, and product leads, and document results so they can feed into supplier evaluations and next-generation platform definitions

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing a Master's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
  • Coursework or research experience in computer architecture, SoC design, or embedded systems, including memory hierarchy, interconnects, and power management
  • Experience with quantitative modeling and data analysis in C++, Python, or MATLAB
  • Intent to return to full-time degree program after completion of the internship
  • Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field
  • Research or project experience in performance and power modeling, workload characterization, or architectural simulation
  • Hands-on experience with system-level measurement: power-rail instrumentation, thermal characterization, or hardware performance counters and profiling tools

job.name: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Leo - GNC SW
job.description:
Description Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Amazon Leo is an ambitious project that depends on entirely new satellite designs along with all of the ground capabilities needed to operate a large constellation and provide high performance service to end users. Because the constellation will have several thousand satellites serving millions of customers, systems are being designed to be highly autonomous, self-adaptable to the environment, and capable of recovery in the event of problems. The great majority of new equipment and software is being developed and built in-house by our engineering and manufacturing teams.

Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) designs the constellation for good coverage and space safety, and develops the systems that control and maneuver each satellite as they ascend from injection to operational orbits, merge into the constellation flow and station keep relative to neighbors. Every spacecraft is ready and able to maneuver at any time to avoid other satellites or space debris if a close pass threatens.

The navigation system provides precise positioning in real-time and supports forecasting future orbital state, taking into account planned maneuvers and other effects. Guidance, Navigation, and Control also provides cueing to direct the communications systems on the satellite that require accurate pointing in order to achieve high performance.

Key job responsibilities

As a Guidance, Navigation, and Control software engineer, you will develop real-time, embedded software that flies the satellite; ground-based applications that predict orbital state, monitor for potential collisions, and optimize maneuvers; high fidelity modeling and simulation software; and all sorts of infrastructure needed to develop and operate the system. Because GNC is the heart of the satellite flight system, you will frequently be pulled in to help with a broad spectrum of problems standing in the way of satellite integration and test, manufacturing, and even flight operations.

job.name: Senior Security Engineer, Detection & Response
job.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes - from emerging brands to Fortune 500s - use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

What you'll do

There is no MSSP and no tier-1 queue here. Detection & Response engineers own their detections end to end: you write them, you tune them, and your team is paged when they fire. The security team is spread across the globe with a follow-the-sun pager rotation so nobody is paged at 3am local.

The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.

Detection engineering

  • *Build and tune detections across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud* , treating them as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and shipped through the same CI/CD practices the rest of engineering uses.
  • *Track detection quality as measured quantities* : coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.

Response & automation

  • *Own incident response:* triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.
  • *Build automation that removes toil* from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.

Telemetry & partnership

  • Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship , working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.
  • *Threat hunt proactively across the estate* , converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.

You Should Have

job.name: Principal Flight Software Engineer
job.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role The software team at K2 strives to blur the lines between the various types of software development and encourages team members to get into parts of the stack they may not otherwise have experience with. This spectrum includes GNC algorithms (Rust, C++), application software on flight computers (Rust, C++), to embedded software on microcrontrollers (Rust, C++),to operating systems (Rust, C++, C), to HDL programming (VHDL, SystemVerilog), to test systems (Python), and many things inbetween. By doing this, we create a stronger team with more capable engineers. For now, this does not include front-end, artificial intelligence, or machine learning development.

As a part of the team, you will be responsible for the development and verification of the software used to fly some of the largest spacecraft that have ever been flown. You will be able to write mission-critical code that controls propulsion systems, attitude control systems, and power systems to ensure safe and reliable operation of the vehicle. In your first 6 months you will developcore pieces of the software architecture including the strategies for fault tolerance, real-time control, and telemetry downlink. In your first year you will implement larger software systems and begin verifying your code using both software and hardware in the loop simulators. In your first two years you will operate your code on multiple spacecraft, demonstrating robust performance in demanding missions.

The ideal candidate relishes working with large volumes of data, enjoys the challenge of highly complex technical contexts, and, above all else, is passionate about data and analytics. Build and maintain the infrastructure to answer questions with data, using software engineering best practices, data management fundamentals, data storage principles, recent advances in distributed systems, and operational excellence best practices. job.name: Senior Flight Software Engineer
job.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role The software team at K2 strives to blur the lines between the various types of software development and encourages team members to get into parts of the stack they may not otherwise have experience with. This spectrum includes GNC algorithms (Rust, C++), application software on flight computers (Rust, C++), to embedded software on microcrontrollers (Rust, C++),to operating systems (Rust, C++, C), to HDL programming (VHDL, SystemVerilog), to test systems (Python), and many things inbetween. By doing this, we create a stronger team with more capable engineers. For now, this does not include front-end, artificial intelligence, or machine learning development.

As a part of the team, you will be responsible for the development and verification of the software used to fly some of the largest spacecraft that have ever been flown. You will be able to write mission-critical code that controls propulsion systems, attitude control systems, and power systems to ensure safe and reliable operation of the vehicle. In your first 6 months you will developcore pieces of the software architecture including the strategies for fault tolerance, real-time control, and telemetry downlink. In your first year you will implement larger software systems and begin verifying your code using both software and hardware in the loop simulators. In your first two years you will operate your code on multiple spacecraft, demonstrating robust performance in demanding missions.

Our client, a US-headquartered healthcare staffing company, is building its Oracle Cloud HCM team in Pune. They are hiring an Oracle HCM Fast Formula Developer to design, build and support the formulas behind time, absence and payroll for a large US workforce.

This is a hands-on development role. You will turn complex pay, time and leave rules into reliable Fast Formulas, test them thoroughly and support them in production. You will work closely with functional, technical and business teams across India and the US.

The role starts on a 3 to 6 month contract and converts to a full-time position with the client.

  • Good understanding of the software development life cycle, testing and documentation

  • Exposure to Project Portfolio Management (PPM) for billable time
  • HCM Extracts, HDL or OTBI
  • Oracle Cloud HCM certification
  • Bachelor's degree in IT, Information Systems or a related field

  • A clear path to a full-time role after a short contract
  • Deep, specialist work on a large US Oracle Cloud HCM setup

About Turing

Turing is one of the world’s leading AGI infrastructure companies, working with frontier AI labs to accelerate model development through high-quality training data, evaluations, and engineering talent.

About the Role

We’re looking for experienced, hands-on software engineers to help evaluate and improve AI coding models .

Rather than primarily building production applications, you’ll work with coding agents across real-world repositories and assess the quality of their work. You’ll review generated code and agent behavior, determine whether solutions are technically correct, identify failure modes, and create the evaluation signals and feedback used to improve model performance.

Think of the coding agent as another engineer whose work you’re reviewing: Can it understand the task? Did it choose the right approach? Is the resulting code correct, robust, and maintainable? Can you explain precisely where it succeeded or failed?

What You’ll Do:

  • Evaluate AI-generated code and solutions across real-world software repositories
  • Review agent behavior, tool usage, and code changes for correctness and quality
  • Identify technical errors, weak approaches, and recurring model failure modes
  • Compare model outputs and explain why one solution is better than another
  • Create and refine rubrics and evaluation criteria for coding tasks
  • Produce high-quality evaluation and preference data used to improve coding models
  • Build and maintain pipelines and infrastructure supporting data generation, collection, and evaluation workflows
  • Synthesize findings from data work into clear write-ups, updates, and recommendations for the team
  • Collaborate closely with researchers and engineers to translate qualitative judgment into scalable processes
  • Share clear, actionable findings with AI researchers and engineers

What We’re Looking For:

  • 5+ years of hands-on software engineering experience
  • Strong proficiency in Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or another major production language
  • Experience working in substantial real-world codebases
  • Strong code-review skills and technical judgment
  • Ability to clearly explain why an implementation is correct, incorrect, or could be improved
  • Strong written communication
  • Experience using modern LLMs or AI coding tools

Experience with LLM evaluation, coding agents, RLHF, preference data, rubric design, or post-training is a plus, but not required.

  • Start: As soon as possible

job.name: Senior Software Engineer, Search Platform
job.description:
Senior Software Engineer, Search Platform Our vision We are building the next-generation search platform, with a vision to democratize knowledge construction and consumption at Thomson Reuters. The platform consolidates search systems across Thomson Reuters products and services, serving millions of end users, internal agents, and internal search teams, into a fully managed, customizable, sovereign, and self-serve search platform. Job Description The AI Enabled Software Engineering (AIESE) team within Thomson Reuters is seeking Senior Software Engineers to build the core of that platform: the ingestion pipelines that turn content into searchable knowledge, the APIs that serve it to products and AI agents, and the cloud infrastructure that keeps it fast and reliable. Your work is what lets internal teams create, configure, and run search on their own, without waiting on a central team.

This is a full-ownership role. You design, build, test, deploy, and operate production systems at scale. We ship to production constantly, treat delivery friction as an engineering problem to solve, and use AI-assisted development as a primary tool. Senior Engineers here hold design authority within their scope, share expertise across the team, and mentor more junior engineers.

Key Responsibilities Build the platform

  • Design, build, and test platform services across document ingestion, search indexing, and query APIs, using the language best suited to the problem (for example Python, Java, or Go).
  • Build reliable pipeline components that move documents through parsing, chunking, enrichment, and indexing, using proven patterns for retries, dead-letter queues, and idempotent processing.
  • Build self-service platform APIs that let client teams configure search systems, manage index lifecycles, and monitor ingestion health.
  • Design retrieval interfaces for products and AI agents with predictable contracts, explicit latency budgets, and result payloads sized for LLM context windows.
  • Contribute to the move from OpenSearch to Vespa, including schema migrations and zero-downtime index promotion.
  • Instrument retrieval components so offline evaluation and LLM-as-judge grading can compare pipeline versions and measure search quality.

Operate What You Build

  • Take part in the on-call rotation and own incidents in your scope, from triage and root cause to post-mortem and systemic fixes.
  • Add logging, metrics, and distributed tracing to your components, including trace-level visibility into agentic retrieval paths, and help define SLOs.
  • Remove delivery friction wherever you find it: slow deployments, flaky tests, and painful local workflows. Use AI-assisted tools fluently and share what works.

Lead and collaborate

job.name: Senior Full Stack Engineer, People Products
job.description:
Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes. Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements. We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.

About The Business Applications Team The Business Applications org builds and operates the internal systems that keep Thumbtack running at scale: Salesforce-centered workflows, admin tooling, and the integrations that connect teams across the company. We're now expanding that foundation into a broader internal platform for AI-enabled work — shared APIs, reusable integration patterns, and safe, auditable capabilities for business-critical actions. We work directly with the business teams who depend on these systems, turning complex operational needs into software that's easier to run, extend, and automate responsibly.

The challenge Thumbtack’s People team is reimagining how employees and leaders experience People programs—and how the People team operates. Employees get support tailored to their circumstances, managers bring relevant evidence into feedback and team decisions, and People specialists spend less time coordinating processes across systems. We have promising starting points: a People Q&A assistant, personalized insights that help leaders understand their teams, and automations across HR and recruiting systems. You’ll help build what comes next: advisors that bring People expertise and personal context together, experiences that anticipate needs and help people act on insights, and connected workflows that complete work on someone’s behalf.

Making this possible means working with some of the company’s most sensitive information—performance, feedback, org structure, and hiring. Every product must know who the user is, what they’re allowed to see and do, what an AI model may receive, and what gets retained. You’ll own that engineering problem end to end, building on our identity-aware infrastructure as it matures and extending its capabilities to meet the specific needs of People products. You’ll work day to day with People Products & Data, who set product direction and priorities, alongside TPMs, HR systems analysts, data scientists, data engineers, and other partners—while building on and contributing to the Business Applications platform.

What You’ll Do

job.name: Cloud Security Specialist
job.description:
Company Description Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. We believe diverse perspectives help both players and teams thrive. If you’re passionate about innovation and pushing entertainment boundaries, join our journey and help create the unknown!

Job Description As a Cloud Security Specialist at Ubisoft Montréal, you will help development and platform teams design, build, and use cloud infrastructure securely at scale. You’ll create reusable security solutions, automate controls, and work closely with teams to make secure delivery practical.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop infrastructure as code modules and reusable code libraries that help teams design, build, and use infrastructure securely at scale.
  • Partner with project teams to understand their needs and deliver practical, scalable security solutions without unnecessary friction.
  • Integrate infrastructure as code scanning and policy as code into continuous integration and continuous delivery platforms and source repositories.
  • Build secrets management patterns and help teams replace hardcoded credentials and long-lived access keys.
  • Coach development and platform teams on secure delivery practices without slowing their work.
  • Document all implemented security controls and measures.
  • Automate security assessments and reporting on the impact of security controls to support rollout and implementation.
  • Build and maintain security configuration templates and hardening standards.
  • Prototype and validate security improvements and solutions.

Qualifications

  • Hands-on proficiency with GitLab CI or similar tools, Terraform, and CloudFormation, including pipeline configuration and reusable modules.
  • Practical experience with Amazon Web Services (AWS).
  • Understanding of AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM), including roles, policies, OpenID Connect (OIDC) federation, and the risks of static credentials.
  • Familiarity with Checkov, tfsec, Open Policy Agent (OPA), or Trivy, including when to use each tool.
  • Knowledge of Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) platforms such as Tenable, Wiz, Prisma, or similar tools.
  • Proficiency in scripting and automation with Python, Bash, or Go, with an understanding of vendor application programming interfaces (APIs).
  • A collaborative approach to building trust with development teams and making security an enabler rather than a barrier.
  • Understanding of cloud networking, including virtual private clouds (VPCs), security groups, routing, private endpoints, and firewalls.

job.name: Security Engineer, Vulnerability Management
job.description:
About LiveKit LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

About This Role Our customers trust us with audio, video and data belonging to their own end users, so a security failure on our side puts their data and their business at risk. We are hiring a Security Engineer to build and run our vulnerability management and security operations program. Vulnerability management is a core capability for keeping our security posture strong as the platform and the company grow: knowing what we run, finding what is exposed, and getting the right fixes shipped quickly. It also underpins our customer commitments and the compliance programs we are building. Our program is early, and you will shape it. You will join a small Trust team that covers security, IT and compliance, and you will own this program end to end from your first week.

You'll thrive at LiveKit if you

  • think like both a builder and a breaker, and understand security from first principles
  • take an automation-first and pragmatic approach to risk mitigation
  • translate security concerns into engineering action
  • can clearly explain complex technical concepts to others
  • are a fast learner and thrive in ambiguity

What You’ll Do

  • Select, deploy and operationalize scanning tooling across our production assets.
  • Run vulnerability management end to end: triage, severity in our environment, owner assignment, remediation SLAs and reporting.
  • Build engineering-first triage and remediation workflows that fit how our engineering teams already work, and automate the routing and follow-up.
  • Build a remediation dashboard that engineering and leadership read and act on.
  • Automate collection of the vulnerability management evidence our compliance programs depend on, in partnership with our Compliance team.
  • Build automation, including agentic tooling, that removes manual security operations work and keeps pace with engineering growth.

Who You Are

job.name: Senior Application Security Developer
job.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary: This role is available to candidates across Canada, excluding Quebec. If you are local to one of our hubs (Burnaby, Calgary, or Toronto) you will be expected to be in office two days per week for our Anchor Days.

Clio is looking for a Senior Application Security Developer to join the Vulnerability Management Program within the Application Security Team. Vulnerability Management is established as a standing program at Clio, with a clear mission: Vuln0 is the goal, and automation is the path. As a Senior Developer, you will bring solid software development experience combined with deep domain expertise in application security and vulnerability management to architect and build tools that reduce toil, automate vulnerability discovery, drive automated remediation, and partner with product teams across Clio.

In this role, you will help own, operate, and extend the tooling and automation pipeline (including our custom internal security tooling) that powers our vulnerability management lifecycle - covering dependency CVEs, SAST, secret scanning, pentest findings, bug bounty, and infrastructure-as-code. You will work directly with development teams to provide guidance, solve root causes, and remediate vulnerabilities in core codebases.

You will collaborate closely with other subteams across Security and Engineering, helping integrate vulnerability sources, refine triage quality, prove reachability, and enable development teams to drive open vulnerabilities to zero past SLA.

Program Philosophy & Mission

  • Vuln0 is the goal: Vuln0 means zero vulnerabilities open past SLA
  • Automation is the path: We cannot scale the team by adding humans to manually triage and patch. We reach Vuln0 generating fixes automatically, and reserving human effort for complex edge cases. The “Vuln-pocalypse” is here and we need people that can apply tooling to ride this wave. Be excited about solving hard problems the right way
  • Risk-based prioritization: Risk and exploitability determine sequencing so development teams focus on what is reachable and actionable
  • Enforceable SLAs & clear ownership: VM owns the process, tooling, systems, and automation; development teams own resolving their own vulnerabilities with our guidance and assistance

A Day in the Life

Come make an impact every day at Zebra.

Serves as a senior technical resource for cloud security, with primary focus on secure cloud architecture, standardized perimeter controls, Zero Trust access patterns, design recommendations, risk articulation, and secure-by-design guidance across multi-cloud deployments.

job.name: Senior Security Engineer - Insider Threat
job.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About The InfoSec Team The InfoSec team protects Affirm’s systems and data from evolving threats. We manage security risk, monitor vulnerabilities, and enforce protective controls across the company. The team leads incident response, compliance, identity and access management, and employee training. Our goal is to ensure that security is built into every system and decision at Affirm. We maintain a secure, trustworthy environment so the business can operate and grow with confidence.

About The Role In this role, you'll help mature Affirm's insider threat program. You'll build out the controls, detection use cases, and investigative practices that make it work day to day, support insider risk investigations, and partner with Legal, HR, Privacy, and Compliance to keep the program effective, proportionate, and trusted by Affirmers.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the build-out of key insider threat workstreams, from initial design through to day-to-day operation
  • Build out the program's operating mechanics, including investigative standards, playbooks, and the metrics and reporting that show whether the program is working
  • Support insider risk investigations alongside SIRT, bringing insider threat expertise, telemetry and evidence analysis, and written findings and risk recommendations
  • Partner with Legal, HR/Employee Relations, Privacy, and Compliance on case handling and escalation criteria, helping ensure the program respects employee privacy and meets legal and regulatory obligations
  • Threat model Affirm's highest-risk data and systems for insider risk, and partner with detection engineers to turn the results into production detections
  • Own and improve the controls that reduce insider risk, including data loss prevention, endpoint monitoring, secure browser and contractor access controls, SaaS posture management, and access governance, working with system owners to close gap
  • Automate the program's operational load with workflow automation platforms and Python, covering evidence collection, case routing, and reporting
  • Build and expand agentic automations that assist with insider risk triage and investigation, and define which decisions stay with a human

What We Look For

job.name: Senior Supply Chain Security Engineer (East Coast Preferred)
job.description:
About Docker Docker is the platform at the center of how intelligent software gets built. For more than a decade, Docker has helped millions of developers and thousands of organizations build, ship, and run software consistently across any environment. Today, Docker extends that same trust to the AI era. Docker Hardened Images form the foundation agentic code is built on, local and cloud Docker Sandboxes isolate where agents run, and Docker AI Governance sets enterprise-wide policy. Together, they give builders and organizations the confidence to adopt any model, tool, or agent without compromising security, governance, or control.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

The Role The DHI Content team builds and maintains Docker Hardened Images: a catalogue of security-hardened system packages, container images and Helm charts designed to be minimal, up to date and safe to use in security-conscious and regulated environments.

This is a supply-chain and open-source maintainer role rather than a conventional backend engineering role. You will work across upstream OSS projects, package and image definitions, Helm charts, Kubernetes, integration tests, vulnerability remediation and the controls that prove content is ready to publish. The work is broad by design: customers should be able to select hardened packages and images and, where relevant, deploy them through hardened charts without the pieces drifting apart.

We are moving DHI content production towards a machine-first factory. Routine work should begin with a machine-produced change and pass through automated build, test, policy and review controls. Engineers add the most value by handling difficult ecosystems, making security judgements, improving standards and turning repeated human corrections into better tooling. You will use AI-assisted engineering extensively, but remain accountable for the evidence and quality behind every result.

As a Senior Supply Chain Security Engineer, you will own substantial content and improvement work from upstream discovery through release and ongoing maintenance. You will be expected to close the loop on customer and security outcomes, not only submit individual definition changes.

Success in This Role Looks Like You will succeed by becoming a trusted end-to-end owner for hardened content. Within your first year, you should have delivered complex new or updated DHI content across packages, images and Helm charts, improved the factory or its quality gates, reduced recurring manual work and raised the capability of the engineers around you.

job.description:
Change the future with us. We are looking for dedicated and talented people who solve ever-changing challenges, customer needs, and questions from colleagues with clever concepts and creativity. We embrace change and work with curious minds re-inventing the future of work. Join us and let us focus together on what’s truly important: making lives better with new ideas and the latest technology around the world.

About the role: Agentic AI Security Specialist We are seeking an Agentic AI Security Specialist to join Siemens Digital Industries Operations Software at our AI hub in Canada.

You own the security of a product in which software agents read industrial data, consult digital twins, and, within granted authority, act on production systems. Trust is the product's core promise and you make sure that the product can live up to that promise.

The role covers two workstreams with one underlying discipline: keeping autonomous agents contained. First, you are responsible for the security of our own AI-first development: our coding agents work in sandboxes with real tools and real credentials, and no agent may break out, exfiltrate data, or cause damage; our development and demonstration environments must never expose customer data. Second, you are responsible for the security of the product itself: customer agents must remain securely confined to their granted scope, skills must not be able to cause harm beyond their declared effect, and the guardrails must be able to deliver their full protective effect under attack and under failure. The development environment and the customer product are operated separately, but the mechanisms that keep an agent inside its boundaries are the same, and you own them in both.

You hold the full product security mandate: threat models, identity and permission architecture, enforcement at the point where an agent calls a tool or triggers an action, isolation of execution environments, secure supply chain, and security analytics over the traffic the platform generates. You work closely with the data and memory engineer, whose pipelines carry the signals you analyze, with the runtime lead, whose execution model you constrain, with the developer platform engineer, whose sandboxes you harden, and with the governance owners in Europe, who define what the product may do. You are not a compliance function and not a reviewer at the end of the line; you design the mechanisms and verify that they hold.

job.name: DevOps Engineer
job.description:
About OTH Security

At OTH Security, we deliver right-sized security solutions tailored to each client. Our team believes in open, respectful collaboration, and continuous improvement. We believe security should enable our customers.

Intermediate DevOps Engineer

The role

We're hiring a DevOps Engineer for our practice. When a client comes to us to achieve SOC 2, ISO 27001 or a similar standard, the audit work often shows their infrastructure isn't ready. You'll close that gap: building secure, auditable infrastructure with Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD, then handing clients a platform their own teams can run.

This is an intermediate, client-facing role. You'll work on two or three client engagements at a time and take well-scoped projects from assessment to rollout on your own. Our security consultants and senior engineers are on hand for architecture calls and reviews.

Key Responsibilities

  • Assess client cloud environments, CI/CD and Kubernetes setups against SOC 2, ISO 27001 and similar controls, and write up clear, prioritized findings.
  • Build and refactor client infrastructure as code with Terraform: reusable modules, remote state, separate environments and peer-reviewed changes.
  • Set up and harden Kubernetes clusters: RBAC, network policies, pod security, secrets handling and safe upgrades.
  • Build CI/CD pipelines that enforce change management: required reviews, automated tests, security scanning and an audit trail for every deploy.
  • Implement technical controls auditors look for: least-privilege IAM, SSO and MFA, encryption at rest and in transit, centralized logging, backups and vulnerability management.
  • Produce audit-ready evidence and documentation, and work with our compliance consultants and the client's auditors to answer technical questions.
  • Explain technical trade-offs to client engineers and non-technical stakeholders, and keep them updated on progress and risks.
  • Hand over cleanly: runbooks, architecture notes and knowledge transfer so client teams can run what we build.
  • Help turn repeated client work into reusable modules, templates and playbooks for our practice.

Qualifications

Required

  • 3–5 years in DevOps, platform, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • Production experience writing and maintaining Terraform, including modules and remote state.
  • Production experience running workloads on Kubernetes: deployments, services, ingress, config and secrets, and debugging failing pods.
  • Working knowledge of major cloud providers (AWS / GCP / Azure).
  • Experience building CI/CD pipelines with a tool such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or Jenkins.
  • Scripting skills (Bash / Python / Go)
  • Linux, networking (DNS, load balancing, TLS) and container (Docker) fundamentals.
  • Security fundamentals: IAM and least privilege, network segmentation, encryption, secrets management and vulnerability scanning.

Dentsply Sirona develops, manufactures, and markets a comprehensive solutions offering including dental and oral health products as well as other consumable medical devices under a strong portfolio of world class brands.

This role is the enterprise technical owner for the security of three foundational internet-facing services: Domain Name System (DNS), digital certificates and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and Web Application Firewall (WAF). These services define and protect the boundary between Dentsply Sirona and the public internet, and this engineer is accountable for keeping that boundary trustworthy, available, and resilient.

As the build-and-govern owner, the role designs, selects, and stands up these capabilities, then sets the standards and guardrails by which they run. It owns the design, engineering, and continuous improvement of controls across DNS resolution and domain governance, the full certificate lifecycle and enterprise PKI, and web application and edge protection. Day-to-day operation transitions to a partner Infrastructure run-and-maintain function, while this role retains design authority, standards, and risk governance. The engineer partners closely with Infrastructure and Operations, Network Engineering, Cloud Engineering, Product Security, Application Development, and Security Operations to reduce attack surface, prevent outages caused by expired or misissued certificates, and ensure web-facing assets are protected against modern application-layer threats.

Operating with minimal direction, the Senior Engineer leads complex initiatives end to end, acts as the senior escalation point for DNS, certificate, and WAF issues, and serves as a trusted advisor to both engineering teams and security leadership. Clio is looking for a Senior Application Security Developer to join the Vulnerability Management Program within the Application Security Team. Vulnerability Management is established as a standing program at Clio, with a clear mission: Vuln0 is the goal, and automation is the path. As a Senior Developer, you will bring solid software development experience combined with deep domain expertise in application security and vulnerability management to architect and build tools that reduce toil, automate vulnerability discovery, drive automated remediation, and partner with product teams across Clio.

In this role, you will help own, operate, and extend the tooling and automation pipeline (including our custom internal security tooling) that powers our vulnerability management lifecycle - covering dependency CVEs, SAST, secret scanning, pentest findings, bug bounty, and infrastructure-as-code. You will work directly with development teams to provide guidance, solve root causes, and remediate vulnerabilities in core codebases.

You will collaborate closely with other subteams across Security and Engineering, helping integrate vulnerability sources, refine triage quality, prove reachability, and enable development teams to drive open vulnerabilities to zero past SLA.

Program Philosophy & Mission

  • Vuln0 is the goal: Vuln0 means zero vulnerabilities open past SLA
  • Automation is the path: We cannot scale the team by adding humans to manually triage and patch. We reach Vuln0 generating fixes automatically, and reserving human effort for complex edge cases. The “Vuln-pocalypse” is here and we need people that can apply tooling to ride this wave. Be excited about solving hard problems the right way
  • Risk-based prioritization: Risk and exploitability determine sequencing so development teams focus on what is reachable and actionable
  • Enforceable SLAs & clear ownership: VM owns the process, tooling, systems, and automation; development teams own resolving their own vulnerabilities with our guidance and assistance

A Day in the Life

About The Team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems.

About The Role You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions.

You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground.

You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it.

This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required.

In This Role You Will

  • Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria.
  • Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review.
  • Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates.
  • Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence.
  • Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt.

job.name: Senior Security Engineer, Detection & Response
job.description:
About Flexport:

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes - from emerging brands to Fortune 500s - use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

What you'll do

There is no MSSP and no tier-1 queue here. Detection & Response engineers own their detections end to end: you write them, you tune them, and your team is paged when they fire. The security team is spread across the globe with a follow-the-sun pager rotation so nobody is paged at 3am local.

The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.

Detection engineering

  • *Build and tune detections across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud* , treating them as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and shipped through the same CI/CD practices the rest of engineering uses.
  • *Track detection quality as measured quantities* : coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.

Response & automation

  • *Own incident response:* triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.
  • *Build automation that removes toil* from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.

Telemetry & partnership

  • Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship , working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.
  • *Threat hunt proactively across the estate* , converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.

This role is primarily backend on a full-stack team. You'll own the services that make agentic trading feel fast, clear, and trustworthy for millions of customers.

  • Shape agent behavior through prompt engineering, evals, and conversation analysis, partnering with our registered investment adviser on changes to financial advice
  • Improve service reliability, latency, observability, and execution safety, including retry behavior and safeguards against duplicate actions
  • Partner with frontend engineering, product, design, trading infrastructure, and legal/compliance to ship customer-facing capabilities within regulatory guardrails

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with deep backend expertise and a track record of shipping and operating production services
  • Strong experience with API design, distributed systems, data modeling, testing, and debugging production failures
  • Proficiency in Go or demonstrated ability to learn it quickly
  • Experience building production LLM or agentic systems, including tool calling, orchestration, or evaluation
  • Proven ability to take ambiguous projects from zero to production with minimal oversight and sound product and technical judgment
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Role Summary: We're looking for an experienced Principal Engineer to shape the architecture, scalability, and reliability of Cosmo's growing technology platform.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role combining technical leadership with practical engineering. You'll work closely with Engineering Managers, Platform Engineers, and Data teams to design and evolve our cloud-native, connected-device ecosystem.

You'll drive architectural decisions, solve complex technical challenges, establish engineering standards, and mentor engineers across teams.

This is not a purely architectural role. You'll remain actively involved in hands-on engineering, including coding, prototyping, debugging, and implementing critical technical solutions.

Core Responsibilities

  • Architecture & Technical Leadership: Define and evolve architecture across backend services, AWS infrastructure, IoT connectivity, and data integrations. Lead design reviews, establish engineering standards, and guide technical decisions across teams.
  • Backend & Distributed Systems: Design and develop scalable services using Node.js, TypeScript, and NestJS. Build RESTful and GraphQL APIs, event-driven architectures, and reliable integrations using Kafka and modern databases.
  • Cloud & IoT: Design resilient AWS architectures, including AWS IoT Core, MQTT, real-time device connectivity, and cloud-to-device communication. Improve scalability, high availability, failover, and cloud cost efficiency.
  • Reliability & Observability: Improve system performance, security, monitoring, and incident prevention using Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch, dashboards, and anomaly detection. Lead complex technical investigations and architectural improvements.
  • Hands-On Engineering: Contribute directly to critical implementations, code reviews, performance optimization, debugging, and proof-of-concepts.
  • AI & Automation: Explore AI-assisted development, automated incident analysis, intelligent alerting, anomaly detection, and Jira workflow automation to improve engineering productivity.
  • Mentorship & Collaboration: Mentor Platform engineers, lead architectural discussions, document technical decisions, and collaborate across Platform, Data, Mobile, and Firmware teams.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 6-12 months, you'll have established a strong understanding of Cosmo's architecture, helped define technical direction for critical systems, and delivered meaningful improvements in scalability, reliability, and engineering standards.

You'll have contributed hands-on to high-impact initiatives, strengthened cross-team technical decision-making, and helped engineers become more independent and effective.

job.name: Software Developer
job.description:
DRW is a diversified trading firm with over 3 decades of experience bringing sophisticated technology and exceptional people together to operate in markets around the world. We value autonomy and the ability to quickly pivot to capture opportunities, so we operate using our own capital and trading at our own risk.

Headquartered in Chicago with offices throughout the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia, we trade a variety of asset classes including Fixed Income, ETFs, Equities, FX, Commodities and Energy across all major global markets. We have also leveraged our expertise and technology to expand into three non-traditional strategies: real estate, venture capital and cryptoassets.

We operate with respect, curiosity and open minds. The people who thrive here share our belief that it’s not just what we do that matters–it's how we do it. DRW is a place of high expectations, integrity, innovation and a willingness to challenge consensus.

We are looking for a passionate Software Developer to join our team. You will develop critical software that our traders, researchers and engineering teams use to implement and analyze our algorithmic trading strategies. As a member of our team, you will be surrounded by cutting-edge technology and senior technologists providing you with the best possible environment to succeed.

What DRW Montreal Has To Offer You

Faites décoller votre carrière en vous joignant à notre équipe novatrice et diversifiée à l’avant-garde du transport aérien de passagers. Joignez-vous à Air Canada, une entreprise canadienne emblématique à l’avant-garde du transport aérien, alors que nous continuons à façonner la prochaine génération de solutions numériques au sein de la société aérienne. Axé sur la technologie, l’innovation et les solutions basées sur l’IA, ce poste offre une occasion passionnante de mettre au point des solutions qui auront une incidence importante sur nos activités et notre clientèle.

Vous ferez preuve de curiosité, de discernement et d’une approche axée sur les résultats, tout en explorant continuellement la façon dont les technologies émergentes, notamment l’IA générative et les capacités des agents d’IA, peuvent améliorer nos méthodes de conception, de développement, de mise à l’essai et d’exploitation des logiciels.
