job.name: SDET Engineer
job.description:
SDET Engineer

Experience: 7 to 10 years

Employment type: Full-time

About the role

We are looking for an SDET Engineer to test features on distributed systems and keep our product quality high. You will build and run UI automation with Selenium and Python, work closely with development engineers to find the root cause of failures, and track bugs through to closure. If you are hands-on with automation, comfortable with Linux and cloud troubleshooting, and able to work independently, this role is for you.

What you will do

  • Develop and execute manual and automated UI tests to find bugs
  • Make sure automated tests run regularly so regressions are caught early
  • Work closely with development engineers to find the root cause of failures
  • File bugs and track them to closure
  • Fix test bugs and maintain automation scripts
  • Test features on distributed systems

What you should bring

  • BE, BTech, BCA, MCA, ME, MTech or equivalent
  • 7+ years of software QA engineering experience
  • Hands-on UI automation experience with Selenium and Python, including writing, maintaining and running automation scripts
  • Good understanding of manual, functional and regression testing, including test case creation and defect reporting
  • Basic knowledge of Linux, SSH and cloud environment troubleshooting, including log analysis and basic debugging
  • Fundamental understanding of virtualization and hypervisor technologies, preferably Nutanix AHV and VMware vSphere/ESXi
  • Good debugging, problem-solving and analytical skills, with the ability to work independently

Good to have

  • PyTest and API automation, including REST API and integration testing
  • Backend and system testing
  • Performance, stress and scalability testing
  • Docker and Kubernetes
  • Distributed systems and storage/NAS testing
  • CI/CD and observability tools

How to apply

Click Apply or message us on LinkedIn. Please mention your notice period and current location in your application.

Click Apply or message us on LinkedIn. Immediate joiners, please mention your notice period and current location in your application.

job.name: Remote Senior JavaScript Engineer
job.description:
About Us:

Based in San Francisco, California, Turing is the world’s leading research accelerator for frontier AI labs and a trusted partner for global enterprises deploying advanced AI systems. Turing supports customers in two ways: first, by accelerating frontier research with high-quality data, advanced training pipelines, plus top AI researchers who specialize in software engineering, logical reasoning, STEM, multilinguality, multimodality, and agents; and second, by applying that expertise to help enterprises transform AI from proof of concept into proprietary intelligence with systems that perform reliably, deliver measurable impact, and drive lasting results on the P&L.

Ideal Background:

This role is ideal for engineers who have built production systems at companies like Google, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Meta, or similar high-scale engineering organizations. We especially welcome graduates from top computer science programs such as Stanford, MIT, Carnegie Mellon, UC Berkeley, Georgia Tech, and comparable institutions — though exceptional experience and skill always take precedence over pedigree.

Project Overview:

As a Software Engineering evaluator, you will create cutting-edge datasets for training, benchmarking, and advancing large language models, collaborating closely with researchers. This includes curating code examples, providing precise solutions, and making corrections — with a primary focus on Python across backend services, data pipelines, and ML infrastructure, alongside JavaScript (including ReactJS), C/C++, Java, Rust, and Go. You will evaluate and refine AI-generated code for efficiency, scalability, and reliability, and work with cross-functional teams to enhance enterprise-level AI-driven coding solutions.

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?

  • Work on AI model training initiatives by curating code examples, building solutions, and correcting code — primarily in Python, with additional work in JavaScript (including ReactJS), C/C++, Java, Rust, and Go.
  • Evaluate and refine AI-generated code to ensure that it is efficient, scalable, and reliable.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to enhance AI-driven coding solutions against industry performance benchmarks.
  • Build agents and automated verification tools in Python that can verify the quality of code and identify error patterns.
  • Hypothesize on steps in the software engineering cycle (prototyping, architecture design, API design, production implementation, launch, experiments, monitoring, operational maintenance) and evaluate model capabilities on them.
  • Design verification mechanisms that can automatically verify a solution to a software engineering task.

job.name: Software Engineer
job.description:
About Us The world is electrifying. As we plug in more devices and services, we need new ways to connect to power.

The traditional, one-size-fits-all utility approach, with complicated bills and frustrating customer service, no longer works. At Light, we make it easy to get affordable, renewable electricity by embedding power with the products that consumers already use, from the companies they love.

Light's mission is to power a sustainable and abundant energy future for everyone. We do it by making any company able to sell electricity. With Light's utility-as-API platform, companies from automakers and solar providers to real estate and beyond can offer their own, integrated electricity plans.

Imagine purchasing an electric vehicle that includes unlimited home charging, or solar panels that come bundled with any excess energy you might need from the grid. We're building the flexible future where clean energy shows up wherever customers already are.

We're a Series A company based in Austin, TX. We've found meaningful traction and are now investing aggressively in growth. Join us in building the digital energy infrastructure for the next century of power.

The role As one of Light’s early engineers, you’ll build a first-of-a-kind product from the ground up. You’ll play a direct role in architecting and implementing the foundations of our platform, from our core developer API and embedded UI components to grid-facing systems like load forecasting and and behind-the-meter control.

As one of the early members of the team, you’ll help define our culture, making Light a place people come not just for the mission, but work alongside others they admire and enjoy.

You would describe yourself as having:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of delivering impactful solutions.
  • A high degree of product ownership, driven by objectives and outcomes, not just tasks.
  • Experience building robust and elegant solutions to complex problems with an understanding of what it takes to be a technical leader on significant projects.
  • Attention to detail and ability to execute autonomously.
  • Versatility in working across the stack and adaptability to evolving product needs.
  • Experience working at an early-stage startup is a strong plus.
  • The ability to work in person in Austin, TX with the founders and rest of the engineering team.

job.name: Sr. Software Engineer - AI Quality and Productivity
job.description:

The AI Quality and Productivity team in the Product Validation, Safety and Quality IT org is responsible for empowering Quality and Warranty teams by delivering reliable and secure AI-driven tools that streamline workflows, accelerate decision making, surface actionable insights, and unlock measurable productivity gains across the product lifecycle.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will be responsible for developing data intensive and AI-enabled software applications that support Product Development engineering teams. You will work with complex data requirements and deliver solutions using industry standard practices across SQL, Databricks, and modern programming languages such as Java and Python. You will design and build software and data solutions based on detailed requirements and system specifications, with a strong focus on data quality, performance, and reliability.

This role offers the opportunity to advise, coach, and mentor other software engineers while shaping how engineering teams access and use data and AI. You will help define patterns and best practices for SQL, Databricks (DBX), and AI/ML integrations within VEQ and play a key role in ongoing modernization and cloud initiatives.

What You'll Do

  • Design, develop, and maintain data driven and AI-enabled applications and services that support Product Development and Quality teams.
  • Write high-quality, performant SQL (queries, functions, stored procedures) for complex data transformations and modeling across enterprise data platforms (e.g., SQL Server, Oracle, PostgreSQL).
  • Build and optimize data pipelines and workflows in Databricks (DBX) and related tools to support batch and near real-time data processing.
  • Develop backend services and APIs in Java and/or Python that integrate data, business rules, and user workflows into robust, reusable components.
  • Develop enterprise grade applications using Kubernetes/Docker, Quarkus, Java, Angular, PostgreSQL, and other GM approved tools.
  • Partner with data science and AI teams to productionize AI/ML and LLM based solutions, including feature pipelines, inference integrations, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
  • Proactively identify and remediate issues related to code quality, patterns, performance, security, and data correctness, using code quality analysis tools and remediation techniques.
  • Lead or contribute to solution design, including architecture, patterns, and technology choices aligned with GM standards and Statement of Technical Direction.
  • Apply and champion software engineering best practices, including code reviews, automated testing, branching strategies, CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions), observability, and secure coding practices.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (product owners, data engineers, architects, business stakeholders) to refine requirements, define acceptance criteria, and deliver incremental value in an Agile/SCRUM en

job.name: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, Public Sector
job.description:
At Scale, we build the AI systems behind some of the country's most important decisions. On the Public Sector Engineering team, you'll embed directly with U.S. government customers, including the Army, Air Force, Joint commands and Intelligence Community, to build and deploy AI applications that support their most critical missions.

This is a hybrid customer-facing engineering role. You'll sit with the people whose problems you're solving, own delivery from first prototype to production, and ship software that customers adopt and rely on in the field. Model performance matters, timelines are urgent, and ambiguity is the norm. Your work directly shapes what Scale's platform can do for the public sector.

What You'll Do

  • Embed with government customers to understand their mission, scope the problem, and turn it into working software.
  • Own delivery end-to-end: design, build, deploy, and maintain solutions at customer sites, from prototype to stable production.
  • Build robust backend systems and data integrations that connect customer environments to Scale's platform and back.
  • Partner with product and engineering to feed field signals back into the roadmap, so the patterns you build once become capabilities the whole team can reuse.
  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customer stakeholders, guiding adoption and maximizing mission impact.

Required What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, ideally in customer-facing, forward-deployed, or government contexts.
  • Strong production coding in Python and TypeScript (or comparable modern languages).
  • Comfort across the stack, including cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), containers, Linux, and networking fundamentals.
  • Ability to operate independently in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and make sound trade-offs under pressure.
  • An active TS/SCI clearance, or eligibility to obtain one.

Bonus

  • Experience building or deploying systems powered by LLMs or generative models.
  • Familiarity with Node and React, Kubernetes and Docker, and Terraform.
  • Data engineering background covering ETL pipelines, data modeling, and data governance.

Location and travel This role requires significant time on-site with customers. Expect 25% travel with up to 50% travel as necessary, and/or relocation to Washington DC or St. Louis.

job.name: Senior Software Engineer I, Core Objects
job.description:
At Braze, we have found our people. We’re a genuinely approachable, exceptionally kind, and intensely passionate crew.

We seek to ignite that passion by setting high standards, championing teamwork, and creating work-life harmony as we collectively navigate rapid growth on a global scale while striving for greater equity and opportunity – inside and outside our organization.

job.name: Staff Software Engineer - iOS
job.description:
The Company PayPal has been revolutionizing commerce globally for more than 25 years. Creating innovative experiences that make moving money, selling, and shopping simple, personalized, and secure, PayPal empowers consumers and businesses in approximately 200 markets to join and thrive in the global economy.

Turing supports customers in two ways: first, by accelerating frontier research with high-quality data, advanced training pipelines, plus top AI researchers who specialize in software engineering, logical reasoning, STEM, multilinguality, multimodality, and agents; and second, by applying that expertise to help enterprises transform AI from proof of concept into proprietary intelligence with systems that perform reliably, deliver measurable impact, and drive lasting results on the P&L.

Ideal Background:

This role is ideal for engineers who have built production systems at companies like Google, Microsoft, Apple, Amazon, Meta, or similar high-scale engineering organizations. We especially welcome graduates from top computer science programs such as Stanford, MIT, Carnegie Mellon, UC Berkeley, Georgia Tech, and comparable institutions — though exceptional experience and skill always take precedence over pedigree.

Project Overview:

As a Software Engineering evaluator, you will create cutting-edge datasets for training, benchmarking, and advancing large language models, collaborating closely with researchers. This includes curating code examples, providing precise solutions, and making corrections — with a primary focus on Python across backend services, data pipelines, and ML infrastructure, alongside JavaScript (including ReactJS), C/C++, Java, Rust, and Go. You will evaluate and refine AI-generated code for efficiency, scalability, and reliability, and work with cross-functional teams to enhance enterprise-level AI-driven coding solutions.

What Does a Typical Day Look Like?

  • Work on AI model training initiatives by curating code examples, building solutions, and correcting code — primarily in Python, with additional work in JavaScript (including ReactJS), C/C++, Java, Rust, and Go.
  • Evaluate and refine AI-generated code to ensure that it is efficient, scalable, and reliable.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to enhance AI-driven coding solutions against industry performance benchmarks.
  • Build agents and automated verification tools in Python that can verify the quality of code and identify error patterns.
  • Hypothesize on steps in the software engineering cycle (prototyping, architecture design, API design, production implementation, launch, experiments, monitoring, operational maintenance) and evaluate model capabilities on them.
  • Design verification mechanisms that can automatically verify a solution to a software engineering task.

job.description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts. Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

About The Team The Experience Library team is part of the Digital Marketing Technology organization at Salesforce. We build and own a content authoring and rendering platform that powers marketing pages across salesforce.com. Our platform enables marketing teams to create high-quality, localized, and performant web experiences at scale, powering some of the highest-traffic pages in the Salesforce digital ecosystem.

We work across the full stack with a strong frontend focus on building modular component libraries, WordPress integrations, and a robust rendering layer serving global audiences. We embrace a "you build it, you own it" culture, where engineers are responsible for the quality, performance, and reliability of what they ship, from design to deployment and beyond.

Our team is at an exciting inflection point: actively integrating AI into our engineering workflows, running accelerated innovation initiatives, and expanding internationalization support to new global markets.

The Experience We are looking for a highly skilled and experienced Lead Member of Technical Staff (LMTS) to serve as a technical leader and frontend-focused full-stack domain expert on the Page Builder platform. In this role, you will lead the end-to-end architectural design, engineering roadmap, and development of high-impact, enterprise-scale web capabilities powering salesforce.com.

As a technical leader, you will set the engineering standard for the team, foster a culture of technical excellence, drive AI-first workflow innovations, and play a pivotal role in mentoring engineers across the organization.

job.name: Senior Ground Software Engineer
job.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role As a Senior Software Engineer on our Ground Software team, you are responsible for creating the software that is used to build, test, and fly our satellites and customer payloads. You will build upon the mission software platform used to fly K2's Gravitas satellite, developing new capabilities and automation as we scale to support multiple constellations. You will collaborate closely with internal Mission Operations and Flight Software teams to define and implement our overall mission architecture, and you will work with external customers to scope and deliver software that meets their payload needs.

You will have the opportunity to work in exciting, interdisciplinary domains like: satellite command and control, constellation operations, mission automation, radio communications, astrodynamics, and more.

Responsibilities

  • Design and implement software that facilitates the build, test, and operations of K2's vehicles and our customers' payloads
  • Collaborate with Mission Operators and Engineers across the company to identify and scope software solutions to complex technical and business problems
  • Facilitate software design reviews, architecture discussions, and code reviews to align stakeholders on technical direction
  • Work across our stack (Rust backend, TypeScript/Vue frontend) to support development, test, and operations milestones
  • Support internal and external customers in an on-call capacity as your software is used to drive ground test activities and on-orbit spacecraft operations
  • Mentor other engineers to build a strong team culture and software engineering practices

Read the full description

job.name: Mobile Engineer (iOS / Android)
job.description:
About The Role The role is hands-on ownership of the mobile experience - building and shipping native iOS and Android features that users interact with daily, from first launch through long-term retention.

The team ships to production on a weekly cadence. Mobile engineers here own their features end-to-end: architecture, implementation, instrumentation, rollout, and post-release analysis.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build, ship, and maintain native features across iOS (Swift/SwiftUI) and Android (Kotlin/Jetpack Compose) with a weekly release cadence
  • Own feature development end-to-end: technical design docs, implementation, code review, testing, staged rollout, and post-launch analysis
  • Architect for offline-first behavior, deep caching strategies, and resilience on poor network conditions using a combination of local persistence (Room, Core Data, SQLite) and API sync logic
  • Instrument user-facing surfaces with analytics and performance telemetry (Firebase, Amplitude, Sentry), and use that data to drive iteration
  • Improve app performance and stability: cold start time, ANR rates, crash-free sessions, memory footprint, and bundle size
  • Collaborate with product managers, designers, and backend engineers to shape scoped, testable, customer-focused deliverables
  • Contribute to shared mobile infrastructure - design systems, CI/CD pipelines (fastlane, Bitrise/GitHub Actions), automated UI and unit testing

What We Are Looking For

  • 3–7 years of professional mobile engineering experience, with production ownership of at least one app on either iOS or Android (ideally both)
  • Expert-level proficiency in Swift or Kotlin, including modern patterns (coroutines, Combine/Flow, structured concurrency)
  • Hands-on experience with SwiftUI or Jetpack Compose, plus enough UIKit/XML knowledge to maintain legacy surfaces
  • Deep understanding of mobile networking: REST/gRPC clients, serialization, retry/backoff strategies, and API versioning
  • Track record of shipping through App Store and Play Store release cycles, including review processes, phased rollouts, and hotfix paths
  • Strong grasp of mobile architecture patterns (MVVM, MVI, modularization) and dependency management at scale
  • Bonus: experience with cross-platform tooling (KMP, React Native, Flutter), mobile CI/CD ownership, accessibility, or an active GitHub portfolio of shipped apps

job.name: Staff Software Engineer
job.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

The Real Time Operations division at Axon is on a mission to provide the best-in-class situational awareness software to emergency responders in order to make them more effective and efficient in managing life-and-death situations. As a staff software engineer, you will be joining our team focused on building a fast and performant real-time crime center application that can ingest real-time signals from devices at scale, and provide emergency responders with the features and functionality to focus on the most pertinent information for dealing with the situation at hand. You will take the lead for designing and building critical systems across the cloud, web, and mobile to direct first responders to where they are most needed.

You will join forces with device, other back-end, and front end teams to efficiently source realtime geo-located data from devices in the field such as patrol cars, body cameras and drones. You will join forces with communications teams responsible for streaming realtime media feeds and other signals from devices. You will join forces with application, customer and third party teams to ensure our users have other data they need to make tough decisions. You will write code that efficiently brings these data feeds together on a single map, allowing our users to make better decisions, saving lives.

In this role, you will be reporting to director of engineering for the Real Time Operations division. As a technical leader, you will be advising the division on the right long-term technical initiatives to invest in, and act as a force multiplier on the team, working intimately with other senior engineers in the division to guide and grow them. You are a great collaborator and coach, and will mentor our next set of senior engineers.

Your customer empathy and eagerness to understand users and their problems allows you to balance competing business and engineering priorities, helping to steer the team to achieve the best outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Read the full description

job.name: Salesforce Developer & Administrator, Ads Services
job.description:
Description The Ads Services Salesforce Team is looking for a smart, motivated, and hands-on Salesforce Developer & Administrator to own and operate our shared production Salesforce instance. This is a hybrid role that combines technical Salesforce development (Apex, integrations, Lightning) with platform administration (configuration, user management, data quality). You will be responsible for day-to-day operations, new feature delivery, integrations with internal tools and AWS services, and ensuring a smooth experience for business teams across Support, Operations, and Customer Advisory.

You will use your business judgement and technical experience to design and build compelling solutions for hundreds of internal customers in a fast-paced, innovative environment.

Key job responsibilities

  • Manage configuration of Salesforce features including user management, security, custom objects, page layouts, validation rules, workflows, Flows, and Process Builders.
  • Manage Salesforce support requests and escalated administrative needs — provide prompt and complete resolution to technical challenges.
  • Collaborate with product owners and business stakeholders on major project roll-outs, including training and troubleshooting for end-users.
  • Monitor system health and proactively identify opportunities to leverage Salesforce in innovative ways to improve business processes and increase productivity.

Development

  • Design and develop Apex classes, triggers, and batch jobs to support complex business logic.
  • Build and maintain Lightning Components and Visualforce pages for custom user interfaces.
  • Develop and manage integrations with internal tools and AWS services using REST/SOAP APIs.
  • Design and implement MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations to connect Salesforce with AWS, Retail, and Ads platforms — enabling AI-powered workflows across multi-cloud ecosystems.
  • Design, build, and maintain data models and data pipelines for Salesforce — including ETL/ELT processes, data lake integrations, and real-time sync with external systems.

Cross-Cutting

  • Partner with system product owners to deliver tailored solutions that support business requirements and drive tangible business value.
  • Consult with stakeholders on application performance, scalability, and usability.

A day in the life

Most days start off with a team standup. Participate with a 2-pizza cross functional team of PM and SDEs as they discuss the activities for products and services. In this role you will work with business stakeholders to ideate products and features. You will collaborate with engineers of various levels to break down complex problems with real business impact.

Read the full description

job.name: AI Tooling Engineer
job.description:
*🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!* Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops.

As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact.

We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce.

*💻The Role* We're looking for an AI Engineer to build the internal tools, prototypes, and business workflows that put AI into the hands of every team at Whatnot. You'll own ambiguous, cross-org bets end-to-end: finding real problems, shipping working software fast, hardening what works, and scaling how Whatnot gets value out of AI. You’ll partner with Whatnot’s AI Platform and Developer Tools teams to leverage their systems, add new functionality, and find ways to accelerate adoption by non-technical team members.

This is a high-velocity, high-judgment builder role. You've shipped a lot of apps and prototypes—you're someone who can sit with a CX lead or an ops manager, understand their workflow in an afternoon, and have a working prototype in their hands by the end of the week. You create leverage for yourself by building on top of 3rd party tools where it’s advantageous but also know how to navigate lower-level interfaces where necessary. You also operate above any single project: you help decide where the opportunities are, define the reusable patterns and infrastructure others adopt, and raise the bar for how the whole company builds with AI. You move fluidly across the stack (frontend, backend, data, and the AI layer) and are deeply fluent in the current generation of AI tools and the production patterns around them—prompt engineering, RAG, MCP, agents, and evals.

This is not a model-training or research role. You won't be training models—you'll be building the tools, workflows, and integrations that make off-the-shelf AI dependable and useful inside Whatnot's systems and processes.

*✅ What You'll Do*

We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Plaid’s mission is to unlock financial freedom for everyone by making money movement and access to financial data simple and secure. As a Fullstack Software Engineer, you will design and build the systems and experiences that power how millions of people connect to their finances.

You will work across the stack, building scalable backend services and APIs while also crafting intuitive, high-quality frontend experiences that bring those systems to life. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy switching between backend problem-solving and frontend user experience work, and who are excited to grow their impact across both.

You will collaborate closely with product managers, designers, and other engineers to ship products that are reliable, secure, and delightful to use. At Plaid, engineers take ownership early, contribute to architectural decisions, and see their work reach millions of users.

Responsibilities

  • Design & Development: Design, develop and maintain both frontend and backend components
  • Majority Backend Focus (60-70%): Develop APIs and services, focusing on scalability, security and performance.

job.description:
Who we are

Want to make an impact? Join our pack and come work (and play!) with us.

We believe everyone deserves the unconditional love of a pet—and at Rover, our mission is to make it easier to experience that love. Founded in 2011, the Rover app and website connect dog and cat parents with loving pet sitters and dog walkers in neighborhoods across the US, Canada, and Europe. We empower our community of trusted pet sitters and dog walkers to run their own pet care businesses on Rover, with the tools and security of a global company behind them.

Headquartered in Seattle, Washington, we work closely with our teams in Barcelona and remote locations. We have a reputation as a great place to work and are proud to be recognized as a top workplace in our area by respected business publications. We're an agile, fast-growing company, and our leadership comes from some of the world's most respected tech companies.

At Rover, our furry coworkers are just as important as our human ones—and we wouldn't have it any other way. Along with making the joys of pet parenthood more accessible, we're committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming community of pet people—and that starts with our employees.

About The Commerce Platform The Commerce Platform team is Rover's trusted commerce backbone, owning everything from the order lifecycle to the checkout and payout experience—making it effortless, secure, and reliable for anyone to transact on Rover while ensuring financial accuracy, auditability, and regulatory compliance at scale. Our team's responsibilities include:

  • Delivering a convenient, secure checkout and payout experience. We own the integrations with our payment service providers (including Stripe and PayPal), manage KYC verification, ensure PCI compliance, and continually improve the platform by expanding payment offerings, optimizing checkout flows, and improving the bottom line through high-impact projects
  • Owning the end-to-end transaction lifecycle. We maintain orders and line-item data, fees, credits, and promotions, and serve as the source of truth for what gets charged, credited, taxed, and paid out on the platform—including tax calculation and reporting across eligible jurisdictions
  • Ensuring accurate, audit-ready financial records. We run the reconciliation and reporting pipelines that keep month-end close clean and accurate, partnering closely with Rover's Finance & Accounting and FP&A teams as Rover grows internationally and adds new service lines
  • This is a hybrid position that has the minimum expectation to work out of our Downtown Seattle Office two days per week on Mondays and Thursdays. For this reason, candidates must be based in the Greater Seattle Area or willing to relocate

job.name: Frontend Engineer
job.description:
We're building Billy, a personal AI you can talk to, work with, and ask to take action. Our goal is to give people more room for what matters, with support that remembers and makes good use of context across every part of their lives.

We're looking for a frontend engineer to build a web experience that feels clear, responsive, and personal, and to join a team working at the frontier of consumer AI. This is a hands-on role leading frontend development: you'll build most of the interface yourself and own its technical quality.

What you'll do

  • Work closely with our founders and design team to take features from prototype to production across onboarding, chat, voice, and other web app flows.
  • Build beautiful, scalable UI components.
  • Partner with backend engineers to connect typed APIs and handle streaming responses, loading and error states, retries, and reconnects.
  • Test features on desktop and mobile browsers, including keyboard navigation, focus management, and reduced-motion behavior, and debug slow or unreliable interactions.
  • Improve how we build software: notice recurring friction, propose practical solutions, and follow through on improvements to testing, development, and releases.

What you'll bring

  • Experience shipping and maintaining production interfaces with React and TypeScript.
  • Strong HTML, CSS, and browser fundamentals, including responsive layouts, semantic markup, accessibility, and performance.
  • Careful attention to typography, spacing, motion, and interaction details.
  • Experience debugging with browser DevTools and observing how people actually use a feature.
  • The ability to take design direction well, explain tradeoffs clearly, and iterate thoughtfully on feedback.
  • The ability to move work forward independently: spot gaps, propose solutions, communicate important decisions, and carry implementation through to release.
  • Recent, substantial hands-on engineering experience. You should enjoy writing, debugging, and refining code yourself.

Nice to have

  • Experience with streaming interfaces or real-time audio using LiveKit or WebRTC.
  • Motion and 3D experience with GSAP or Three.js.

Our stack

React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, with TanStack Router and TanStack Query, Nano Stores, XState for conversation flows, and ConnectRPC with Protobuf for typed APIs. We use Storybook, Vitest, and Playwright for interface development and testing, LiveKit and WebRTC for real-time audio and streaming, GSAP for animation, and Three.js for 3D graphics.

Why this role matters

A personal AI needs an interface people can understand and trust. The details matter: knowing when Billy is listening, seeing progress while an action runs, and recovering clearly when something goes wrong.

You'll own much of what makes those experiences work, with direct involvement in the product and close collaboration with the people designing and building it.

job.description:
About Opendoor At Opendoor our mission is to tilt the world in favor of homeowners and those who aim to become one. Homeownership matters. It's how people build wealth, stability, and community. It's how families put down roots, how neighborhoods strengthen, how the future gets built. We're building the modern system of homeownership giving people the freedom to buy and sell on their own terms. We’ve built an end-to-end online experience that has already helped thousands of people and we’re just getting started.

About The Role — All Levels *Location We're looking for team members who are enthusiastic about an in-office culture — people who want to build alongside others and not from a distance. This role is based in one of our talent hubs where we welcome everyone 5 days a week with the requirement of Mo, Tu, Th, Fri. Opendoor offers relocation assistance for qualified candidates moving to Miami or Toronto.* You're interviewing for Opendoor, not any specific team. We don't slot you into a team on day one, rather once you're in, we match you to where you'll have the most impact and the most fun.

This isn't a role for everyone. We choose hard mode. We're process-light, high-trust, and we don't put artificial boundaries between you and the work. You'll be expected to understand how your piece connects to the product and communicate at that level. We don't have project managers, we don't have scrum. We do reviews, proposals, demos, and trust.

What We're Looking For *You ship.* You pick the boring solution when boring is right and the novel one when it isn't. You measure twice and cut once, but you also know when "good enough and shipped today" beats "perfect next quarter."

*You think in first principles.* You have opinions on architecture, distributed systems, and the tradeoffs between technologies. You can speak to the constraints, tripwires, and heuristics that come with operating in a complex and high touch environment. You've formed these opinions through your experiences, not from a book.

*You're language-agnostic.* We care about deep expertise, not loyalty to a specific stack. If you've done the most impressive work of your career in a language or framework we don't or haven't used, we want to hear from you.

*You default to AI.* You've already integrated modern AI tools into your daily workflow. You use them to move faster, not as a crutch.

*You communicate well.* You write clear design docs. You give useful code reviews. You push back on bad ideas without making it personal. You can explain a technical tradeoff to a non-technical stakeholder and actually land it.

*You believe in what we're building.* Not hype, conviction. You see the opportunity in what we're doing and you want to be part of finishing it.

A frontier company is not defined by adopting the newest technology first. It is defined by the judgment to translate emerging capabilities into secure, reliable and measurable outcomes. This means framing ambiguous problems, making explicit tradeoffs among cost, reliability and speed, and deciding responsibly with incomplete information. It also means knowing when not to use AI, controlling scope and establishing what must be true before a solution is ready for release.

ISD’s frontier consulting practice brings industry understanding, solution expertise and engineering discipline together. We use AI to strengthen how we explore, design and deliver, while keeping people accountable for decisions and quality. We build early working artifacts, validate them with customers and learn from delivered work rather than self-assessment. Adoption, change and capability transfer begin at the outset, so progress becomes sustained customer value rather than a successful demonstration alone.

Based in the Greater Toronto Area, the Senior Solution Architect in ISD Canada will lead strategic customer engagements, with a particular focus on financial services. The role requires fluency in customer workflows, data and risk considerations before selecting products or platforms. You will partner with executives and customer engineering teams to establish a credible baseline, define success measures and connect architecture decisions to business priorities across the Toronto and Canadian market.

This is both a strategic and a hands-on architecture role. You will guide multidisciplinary teams, maintain full-stack depth and collaborate with specialists to validate critical design choices in working solutions. The ideal candidate will have strong SQL skills, experience with data visualization tools, and basic to intermediate Python knowledge. This role is primarily focused on data exploration, analysis, reporting, and translating data into meaningful insights that support business decisions.

The successful candidate will work closely with data scientists, subject matter experts, and cross-functional teams to understand business needs, identify relevant data, perform analyses, and communicate findings clearly.

Location: Toronto

Work Mode: full-time, hybrid

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform data extraction, exploration, and analysis using SQL.
  • Analyze datasets to identify trends, patterns, and meaningful insights.
  • Develop and maintain dashboards and reports using Power BI, Tableau, or similar visualization tools.
  • Use Python to support data analysis, automate tasks, and generate scripts when needed.
  • Leverage AI-assisted coding tools to support script development, while validating code accuracy and functionality.
  • Translate analytical results into clear, actionable insights and communicate findings to stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to understand business requirements and identify relevant data sources.
  • Prepare written summaries and present analytical findings to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Support basic project planning, including estimating timelines, prioritizing tasks, and meeting deadlines.
  • Work collaboratively with data scientists and other team members to support ongoing analytics initiatives.

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • 4-6 years of experience as data scientist, data analyst o related.
  • Proficiency in SQL, including the ability to extract, query, manipulate, and analyze data independently.
  • Proficiency in Python, with the ability to understand, review, troubleshoot, and validate scripts. Experience using AI-assisted coding tools is an asset.
  • Hands-on experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar dashboarding and reporting tools.
  • Data Analysis: Experience exploring datasets, identifying patterns, interpreting results, and translating findings into meaningful insights
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to summarize complex data and explain findings clearly.
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong attention to detail and analytical mindset.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and subject matter experts.
  • Basic project planning and time-management skills, including estimating workloads and managing deadlines.
  • Curiosity and a proactive approach to data exploration.

job.name: People AI Solutions Designer
job.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Position Summary The People AI Solutions Designer is the builder. Where the People AI Deployment Lead readies HR processes for automation, the Solutions Designer takes that readied work and builds it — rapidly prototyping, coding, and shipping the agents, automations, and lightweight apps that solve real HR problems.

This is a hands-on craft role for someone who moves quickly from problem to working prototype to production. The Designer “vibe-builds” and assembles solutions in low-code and agent platforms and dropping into code where it is faster or better — and partners closely with the Deployment Lead, HR Systems, and McKesson Technology to put durable solutions into the hands of HR. Select solutions may be managed from idea to launch from within HR with limited oversight, and more complex solutions may require a handoff to MT to fully implement.

Key Responsibilities Translate Readied Workflows into Technical Designs (20%)

  • Take defined inputs, outputs, decision points, and ownership and turn them into a concrete solution design or mockup.
  • Make pragmatic build decisions — what an agent handles, what is automated, what stays human — and flag where a process needs more readiness before it can be built.

Build & Prototype Solutions (30%)

  • Build agents, automations, and lightweight apps that solve the HR problems surfaced and readied by process owners across HR & partners within the Workforce Innovation team
  • Rapidly prototype — turn a readied workflow into a working build quickly, favoring momentum and learning over perfection, then refine based on user feedback
  • Build across low-code and agent platforms (e.g., Microsoft Copilot Studio / Power Platform, ServiceNow, Moveworks) and drop into code (Python, scripting, APIs) where it is the better tool.
  • Lead the prototype and build, partnering closely with UX designer for interface designs and McKesson Technology for complex enterprise solutions

Iterate from Real Usage (20%)

  • Pilot solutions with real users, instrument them, and improve based on actual usage and performance.
  • Tune prompts, logic, and integrations to raise quality, reliability, and experience.

Harden, Document & Hand to Operations (15%)

job.name: Senior Backend Engineer
job.description:
Who We Are At Bluehost, we believe all small businesses deserve the opportunity to succeed online. Our mission is to give small businesses the confidence to think big. We're the all-in-one platform for small businesses to grow online with powerful simplicity, premium performance, smart tools and human support.

This role is a part of Bluehost's innovation team, the group building the AI-native backbone of our platform while the rest of the business scales around us. You'll design async, production-grade backend systems that treat AI as a first-class citizen: multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and provider-agnostic LLM integration, all woven into products millions of small businesses depend on. We want a true go-getter who can take an idea from whiteboard to production without waiting to be told how.

What You'll Do & How You'll Make Your Mark

  • Design and scale async REST/WebSocket APIs in Python (FastAPI or similar), using dependency injection, type hints, and clean, vertical-slice architecture
  • Implement multi-agent workflows (sequential, concurrent, and handoff patterns) to route work among specialized LLM agents
  • Integrate multiple LLM providers behind a provider-agnostic layer, enabling A/B testing and cost-aware routing rather than hard-coding a single vendor
  • Build and maintain Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines against vector stores such as pgvector, Chroma, or a managed vector search service
  • Design schemas and evolve data models (SQLAlchemy/SQLModel-style ORM plus migrations) that support both traditional application logic and AI-driven features
  • Instrument services with structured logs, distributed tracing, and cost/latency metrics, holding a real bar for p95 response time under production load
  • Maintain end-to-end CI/CD ownership, lint, type-check, test, package, and deploy, so releases are boring and safe
  • Champion AI across the delivery lifecycle, not just code generation, and set the guardrails the team works inside: how generated code gets reviewed, how provenance and licensing are checked, and what customer data may enter a prompt
  • Move ideas from concept to production fast, with real ownership over architecture and outcomes, not just tickets

Who You Are & What You'll Need To Succeed

job.name: AI Research Engineer (Remote)
job.description:
• Role Title : AI Research Engineer (Remote)
  • Role Type : Full-time
  • Location : Remote

The Role

We are seeking a Member of Technical Staff to help advance the evaluation and development of frontier coding agents. Sitting at the intersection of AI research, software engineering, and model evaluation, you will design the benchmarks, methodologies, and data systems that shape how next-generation coding models are measured and improved.

What You'll Do

1. Design and own evaluation frameworks for coding agents, including benchmark specifications, scoring methodologies, rubrics, and quality standards.

2. Lead end-to-end research initiatives focused on measuring and improving coding model performance across diverse software engineering tasks.

3. Develop high-quality datasets, golden examples, and evaluation protocols that enable reliable assessment of frontier coding systems.

4. Analyze model behavior and failure modes, identifying systematic weaknesses and translating findings into actionable improvements for training and evaluation.

5. Build tooling and infrastructure that support large-scale experimentation, data generation, review workflows, and evaluation pipelines.

6. Establish best practices for coding-agent assessment, ensuring methodological rigor, reproducibility, and measurement quality.

7. Partner closely with researchers, engineers, and applied AI teams to design experiments and evaluate emerging model capabilities.

8. Contribute to technical reports, benchmark studies, and client-facing research initiatives that communicate model performance and insights.

What We're Looking For

1. Strong software engineering background with expertise in Python, C++, or comparable programming languages.

2. 3+ years of experience in software engineering, machine learning, AI research, evaluation, or related technical disciplines.

3. Experience designing, reviewing, or validating technical assessments, benchmarks, coding tasks, or evaluation methodologies.

4. Familiarity with large language models, coding agents, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, or related AI systems.

5. Proven ability to build tooling, automate workflows, and improve technical processes through systematic experimentation.

6. Strong analytical skills with the ability to investigate model behavior and derive insights from complex technical systems.

7. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly articulate technical findings to diverse audiences.

8. Comfortable operating in fast-moving research environments with significant ambiguity and evolving priorities.

Preferred

1. Experience working on frontier AI systems, coding agents, or model evaluation research.

2. Deep interest in understanding how data, evaluations, and feedback mechanisms influence model capabilities.

3. Track record of independently driving ambiguous technical or research projects from conception to execution.

AI/ML Engineer — Learning Systems

Vancouver, BC

  • Remote (Canada)HybridFull-time$160,000 – $210,000 CAD / year

Design the retrieval, generation and evaluation systems that let Nucleus OS teach — grounded, personalized and measurably effective.

The role

Learning is the hardest test for AI: answers must be correct, grounded in an organization's own material, and pitched at the right level for each learner. You'll build the systems that make that happen.

You'll work on retrieval-augmented generation , curriculum and assessment generation, learner modelling and — critically — the evaluation harnesses that tell us whether learners actually got better.

Benefits

Ici, vous pouvez créer un élan qui dépasse notre organisation, développer des compétences de demain et prendre votre carrière en main, et ce, avec du soutien à chaque étape. Notre équipe IA générative et Livraison logicielle aide les clients à moderniser la façon dont les logiciels sont planifiés, conçus, testés, livrés et exploités. Nous conjuguons rigueur de livraison, expertise technique et accélération du SDLC par l’IA pour permettre aux clients d’avancer plus vite, sans compromettre la qualité, la sécurité ni la confiance.

En tant que conseiller principal, développeur en livraison logicielle, vous concevrez et développerez des solutions logicielles de haute qualité, tout en orientant les équipes de livraison et les clients dans leurs décisions techniques. Vous contribuerez à l’architecture, au développement, aux tests, à l’automatisation et au déploiement, en plus d’encadrer des conseillers et d’appuyer les responsables de livraison.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Piloter des volets ou des fonctionnalités techniques de moindre envergure, de la conception à la mise en œuvre.

  • Contribuer à la conception des solutions, à l’estimation, au raffinement du carnet de produit, à la planification des sprints et à la documentation technique.
  • Participer aux revues de code et contribuer à rehausser les normes d’ingénierie, la couverture des tests, la sécurité et la maintenabilité.
  • Tirer parti de façon responsable des outils de livraison assistés par l’IA pour accélérer le développement, les tests, l’analyse et la documentation.
  • Résoudre les problèmes touchant les couches applicative, données, infrastructure et déploiement.

job.name: Principal Engineer, AI-Native Platform
job.description:
■ About BuildBase

BuildBase is transforming how homes get built. Our cloud platform helps homebuilders simplify procurement, run field execution, manage sales and warranty, and make data-driven decisions from first offer to final handover. We have strong traction in Canada and growing momentum in the US.

We’re also changing how software gets built. Our next-generation platform is being built AI-first: autonomous agent teams scope, build, test and ship work alongside our engineers, under human review. We’re looking for someone to lead that shift.

■ The Role

This is a senior, hands-on full-stack role for an engineer who sees AI as the core of how a modern engineering team works, not as an add-on. You’ll own the technical direction of our platform end to end: architecture, application code, cloud infrastructure, reliability, delivery pipelines, and the AI systems that increasingly do the building.

This is not a hands-off architecture role. You’ll design the system and write the code: React front ends, .NET APIs and services, and the SQL beneath them, applying sound architecture and design patterns every day and setting the example for the team.

Reporting to the Director of Engineering, you’ll be their trusted technical partner in setting engineering direction, priorities and standards for the team.

■ What You’ll Do

Build across the full stack

▪ Lead the design and delivery of our next-generation platform, a .NET 10 API and a React/TypeScript front end, running alongside and progressively replacing our established system.

▪ Write production code across every layer: responsive React/TypeScript interfaces, secure RESTful APIs and services in C#/.NET, and well-tuned SQL Server data access and schema.

▪ Apply proven architecture and design patterns (Clean Architecture, SOLID, domain-driven design, dependency injection, well-documented OpenAPI contracts) and make them the team’s default through example and code review.

▪ Design to the AWS Well-Architected Framework across operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.

▪ Make pragmatic decisions in multi-tenant SaaS: data isolation, tenancy-aware design, performance at scale, and safe coexistence of legacy and modern systems on shared data.

Own cloud and delivery end to end

▪ Own our AWS environment (containers, managed SQL Server, object storage, CDN and serverless) and steer it toward simpler, cheaper, more resilient designs.

▪ Build and run CI/CD in Azure DevOps (Repos, Pipelines, Boards) with automated testing, quality gates, zero-downtime deployments and safe rollbacks.

▪ Champion infrastructure-as-code, secrets management and security by default.

Keep production reliable and observable

▪ Bring site reliability engineering practice to the platform: define SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for the client journeys that matter most, and use them to balance feature work against reliability.

Read the full description

job.name: Scientifique de données

job.name: Senior Software Engineer, AI Platform
job.description:
Everlaw is looking for a Senior Software Engineer, AI Platform with experience building and operating AI platform capabilities that power user-facing software in complex ecosystems. Transforming legal tech with software and AI is a full-stack challenge that applies retrieval, vector search, model orchestration, evaluation, and agentic patterns - alongside search, databases, and real-time collaboration - to help our customers find the truth in millions of documents.

We will encourage you to explore our entire system and work with significant autonomy across the stack. If you have deeper experience in areas like RAG pipelines, LLM integrations, or large-scale retrieval pipelines, there will be plenty of opportunities to lean into that expertise. Most of all, we care about finding self-driven engineers who love their craft, write clean software, use the right tools for the job, and avoid dogma.

We’ve built sophisticated technology with a small, talented team; as we grow, we’ve maintained a culture where you’ll own serious capabilities, write great code, learn a huge amount, and have a lot of fun. You’ll work directly with product and platform partners as needed to ship AI platform features that matter.

We build with a high sense of urgency, with respect for the profound opportunity ahead of us, but don’t rely on sprints or made-up deadlines to motivate results; code quality and maintainability are paramount. At our core, we enjoy the creative process of building systems that are reliable, reproducible, explainable, scalable, and secure. We do this by empowering our team members, tackling challenging and complex engineering problems, and providing mentoring, coaching, and comprehensive feedback.

At Everlaw, our mission is to promote justice by illuminating truth . Our company culture is open and vibrant, and we’re committed to the professional growth of our team members, offering an annual learning and development stipend, regular check-ins with managers regarding career goals, and mentoring from staff and principal engineers. If you’re looking for a place that values passion, integrity, thinking big, and a desire to apply your experience while also continuing to learn, we’d love to hear from you.

Think you’re missing some of the skills and are hesitant to apply? We do not believe in the “perfect” candidate and encourage you to apply if you feel you can bring value to our team. This is a full-time, on-site position located in Oakland, California with an expected hybrid schedule of 3 days/week in the office and 2 days/week at home.

Getting started

You will join the TikTok USDS JV - Data Governance and Assurance Engineering team, the architects of the foundational infrastructure managing the end-to-end AI lifecycle. Our mission is to ensure the integrity, security, and compliance of our AI assets through automated frameworks and advanced content assurance standards.

- Recommendation & GPAI Assurance: Architecting auditable recommendation pipelines to ensure content delivery systems meet strict USDS compliance and safety requirements.

Responsibilities
- Automated Safety Evaluation: Design and scale high-throughput evaluation engines to benchmark LLM and Recommendation Model outputs against safety, bias, and accuracy protocols.

Confidential Search — Founding AI Engineer

Seed-stage AI company backed by a top-tier venture firm

About the company

Our client is building an agentic service desk for managed service providers the firms that run IT for small and midsized businesses worldwide, a category representing roughly half a trillion dollars in annual spend. Their AI agents sit alongside human technicians: reading tickets, investigating root causes across the tools MSPs already run on, and executing approved fixes.

The engineering problem is genuinely hard. These agents have to reason through problems no one wrote a runbook for, respect customer policy, carry state across workflows that run for hours or days, and behave predictably inside live production environments. The company closed a seed round from a tier-one venture firm and is now hiring the engineers who will define how the product actually works.

The opportunity

The Founding AI Engineer will own the agent layer end to end — from first prototype through hardened production deployment. The work rotates by nature: one week may go toward teaching an agent to diagnose an unfamiliar failure mode, the next toward building evaluation harnesses that surface where it breaks down, the next toward the tooling and infrastructure that let it act safely inside a customer's stack.

This is a builder's seat, not an architect's. The person in this role will talk to customers directly, help set the roadmap, ship the code, and operate what they ship. They will also help settle the open questions in this category which decisions belong to agents, where humans keep the final call, how agent reasoning gets explained to a technician, and what a genuinely good technician experience looks like. Those standards are unwritten today. This role helps write them.

What the role involves

  • Building and refining AI agents that investigate IT issues, hold context over long sessions, call tools across customer systems, operate within policy, escalate for approval, and recover cleanly when something goes wrong.
  • Standing up evaluation systems that quantify agent quality, surface failure modes, and convert production traces and customer feedback into concrete improvements.
  • Running fast experiments across models, prompting strategies, retrieval, tool design, and agent architectures — then promoting what works into dependable production systems.
  • Engineering the integrations and backend infrastructure that let agents run securely, reliably, and observably through long-lived customer workflows.
  • Working directly with customers to understand their day-to-day, shipping product improvements end to end, and helping establish engineering practices as the team grows.

Who this is a fit for

job.name: Machine Learning Systems Engineer
job.description:
About Us At Archetype AI, we’re building the world’s first physical AI platform to bring artificial intelligence into the real world. Our foundation model, Newton, understands the physical world through objective sensor data and generates real-time insights into complex physical behaviors, from industrial machinery and systems to wearable devices and smart environments.

Formed by a high-caliber team from Google and backed by one of Silicon Valley’s most renowned venture funds, Archetype AI is at Series A and rapidly advancing its technology for the next big leap. This is a unique opportunity to join an exciting, fast-growing AI team based in the heart of Silicon Valley.

About The Role You will own the serving path for Newton and related multimodal models. Much of our inference stack is Rust-native: model nodes in our agent runtime, built on Rust ML stacks (candle, Burn) with custom GPU kernels, plus the routing layer that streams real-time inference to GPU nodes. You will drive GPU utilization, numerical precision, and low-latency serving from the kernel up.

What You’ll Own

  • Build and own model nodes in our Rust inference runtime: loading, warmup, batching, streaming, GPU memory pools.
  • Optimize kernels and the GPU path: custom CUDA kernels, mixed precision, quantization, parity against research.
  • Own inference routing and serving: streaming path API to GPU node, request batching, SLO-backed latency and cost.
  • Productionize research checkpoints: export, compilation, quantization, parity evals, and rollout.
  • Build the observability inference needs: latency histograms, GPU metrics, OOM signatures, replayable traces.

Key Qualifications

  • 6+ years software engineering, several of them in ML systems, inference, or high-performance GPU computing.
  • Has owned a production serving path end to end, not only benchmarked models.
  • Expert in PyTorch with models shipped to production; knows what will be slow before the profiler runs.
  • Strong CUDA or equivalent GPU depth: memory hierarchy, occupancy, Nsight or equivalent profiling.
  • Rust or C++ alongside Python, Linux performance, production ops; ready to work in Rust daily.
  • Works with researchers: can translate an architecture change into serving work.

Nice to Have

  • Rust ML stacks: candle, Burn, or comparable GPU compute in Rust.
  • Custom kernels and compiler stacks: Triton, CUTLASS, TorchInductor, TensorRT.
  • Quantization and mixed precision in production with a numerical-correctness suite.
  • Multimodal, video, embedding or time-series serving, not only decoder-only chat LLMs.
  • High-performance serving stacks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM): continuous batching, paged KV cache.

What You'll Do

  • Design and develop AI assistants using Vertex AI, including model selection, prompt engineering, grounding, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agent orchestration.
  • Build intelligent, multi-step AI agents using the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), designing agent architectures with tool use, sub-agents, callbacks, and session management for complex conversational workflows.
  • Develop and integrate applications using the Google Cloud AI/ML SDKs (Vertex AI SDK for Python, Google Gen AI SDK) for programmatic access to foundation models, embeddings, tuning, and prediction endpoints.
  • Design agentic architectures leveraging ADK's orchestration capabilities including sequential agents, loop agents, parallel agents, and custom agent hierarchies to handle multi-turn, multi-domain use cases.
  • Implement tool and function calling patterns within ADK agents, connecting them to enterprise APIs, databases, and external services to enable grounded, domain-specific responses.
  • Implement responsible AI practices including safety filters, bias detection, guardrails, hallucination mitigation, and content moderation.
  • Architect scalable, production-grade solutions using Vertex AI Agent Builder, Vertex AI Search, Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, and other GCP services.

job.name: LLM / GenAI Engineer
job.description:
About The Role The role sits at the core of an AI product team building LLM-powered systems that ship to production — not demos. This means owning RAG architectures, agentic workflows, fine-tuning pipelines, and the evaluation infrastructure that determines whether a system actually works.

You will work closely with applied scientists, backend engineers, and product leadership to translate ambiguous GenAI problems into reliable, observable, cost-efficient systems serving real users.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and build production RAG pipelines with LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom architectures, including chunking strategies, hybrid retrieval, and reranking
  • Integrate and tune vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, Qdrant) for low-latency semantic search at scale
  • Develop agentic workflows using frameworks like LangGraph or custom orchestration — tool calling, multi-step planning, and guardrails for production reliability
  • Run parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA, DPO) on domain-specific datasets and manage the full training-to-deployment lifecycle
  • Build systematic LLM evaluation frameworks: golden datasets, LLM-as-judge pipelines, regression suites, and hallucination/quality metrics
  • Optimize inference cost and latency across self-hosted open-weight models (vLLM, TGI) and commercial APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic)
  • Ship observable, tested code with strong monitoring — latency, token spend, quality drift — and participate in architecture reviews

What We Are Looking For

  • 3–6 years of software or ML engineering experience, with at least 1–2 years building LLM/GenAI systems in production
  • Deep Python proficiency; comfort with async programming, API design, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure)
  • Hands-on experience with at least one LLM orchestration framework and one vector database in a production setting
  • Practical knowledge of transformer architecture, embedding models, prompt engineering limits, and context-window management
  • Experience fine-tuning or adapting open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) using LoRA/QLoRA and standard training tooling
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field — or equivalent practical experience
  • Bonus: experience with inference optimization (quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache tuning), Kubernetes-based ML infrastructure, or building evaluation/benchmarking platforms from scratch

job.name: Agentic AI Engineer — Healthcare AI
job.description:
Three hundred fifty million Americans rely on a healthcare system whose decision-making has become slow, costly, and adversarial - care delayed by prior authorization and paperwork, claims that misfire, clinical decisions made without the right information at the right moment, and patients who struggle to navigate or afford the care they need. Deloitte has a new AI-first effort, backed by $1B in committed investment, building the reasoning models and agentic systems to rebuild how that system decides - across payers, providers, and life sciences, and for the patients they serve - so that care is faster, fairer, and far less wasteful. This is not AI applied at the margins. It is a ground-up rebuild of the decision-making machinery behind American healthcare, at national scale.

This is an early, well-funded build. You will own agent systems end to end - from architecture through production - and your work ships into live clinical and operational settings within your first months, not into a lab.

As an Agentic AI Engineer, you will design, build, and operationalize the LLM- and SLM-powered systems behind real healthcare decisioning - the reasoning, orchestration, retrieval, memory, and control layers that let intelligent agents operate reliably across the hardest decisions in the industry: clinical reasoning, prior authorization and claims integrity, care navigation, and the operational workflows that run across payers, providers, and life sciences. This is not a prompt-only role. We are looking for builders who think deeply about system behavior, grounding, and reliability where a wrong action has real consequences for patients and the clinicians who serve them.

You do not need a healthcare background. We pair every engineer with clinical and domain experts and teach you the domain - you bring the agentic engineering depth.

We hire on demonstrated depth, not years - the level you join at is determined through our interview process, based on the depth and judgment you demonstrate, not your years in a title.

Recruiting for this role ends on 1/29/2027.

Agent architecture & orchestration

job.name: Sr. Software Engineer II, AI on Sensor – Mac, Linux, or Windows (Hybrid)
job.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

*About The Role:* CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”: a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The sensor processes thousands of events per second to provide deep visibility into operations on the endpoint, and performs rich correlation and computation to identify malicious events and blocks malicious activity.

The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network, correlates malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

This is a Sr. Software Development Engineer II (SDE) role in the CTIO team that is bringing multiple AI-based strategies together into an integrated capability on our next-generation sensor (lightweight agent) across macOS, Linux, and Windows platforms. The Sr. SDEs in the team own the design and development of the features that put AI on the endpoint: operationalizing machine learning models inside the sensor, building the data pipelines that collect, transform and deliver sensor telemetry for model training, evaluation and on-device inference, and integrating those capabilities with the core sensor features. Features will cross-cut most core OS subsystems such as file system, memory, process, and networking, and many are built with shared components across platforms. The team operates under the Agile development principles and ships frequently.
