job.name: Senior Compensation Analyst
job.description:
At YETI, we believe that time spent outdoors matters more than ever and our gear can make that time extraordinary. When you work here, you’ll have the opportunity to create exceptional, meaningful work and problem solve with innovative team members by your side. Together, you’ll help our customers get the high-quality gear they need to make the most of their adventures. We are BUILT FOR THE WILD™.

About The Role The Senior Compensation Analyst supports the design, administration, analysis, and ongoing management of compensation programs across the organization. This role partners with Talent Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, Payroll, Legal, and business leaders to provide data-driven guidance on market pricing, job evaluation, salary structures, incentive programs, compensation planning, and pay-related compliance.

This role requires strong analytical capability, sound compensation judgment, and the ability to translate complex data into practical recommendations. The Senior Compensation Analyst independently manages recurring compensation processes and contributes to broader projects that support competitive, equitable, compliant, and scalable pay practices.

What You'll Do Compensation Strategy & Program Administration

  • Support the design, administration, and governance of base pay, variable pay, and other compensation programs.
  • Manage key components of annual compensation planning processes, including eligibility reviews, data validation, planning tools, statement testing, approvals, communications, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Conduct market pricing, compensation benchmarking, pay range analysis, and internal equity reviews to inform pay recommendations.
  • Maintain salary structures, pay ranges, guidelines, and compensation-related documentation across assigned populations or geographies.
  • Review compensation requests, including new hire offers, promotions, transfers, adjustments, and other pay actions, ensuring alignment with guidelines, budget, internal equity, and market data.
  • Provide guidance to Talent Acquisition, Talent Business Partners, and leaders on compensation policy, offer positioning, pay decisions, and exception processes.
  • Partner with HRIS teams to test and validate compensation-related Workday data, processes, reports, and configuration changes.

Job Architecture & Organizational Design

job.name: Senior Credit Analyst
job.description:
Job Title Senior Credit Analyst

Location: Austin, TX

What You'll Do As a Senior Credit Analyst you'll be primarily responsible to spread, manage and maintain financial background information on present and prospective customers, and develop credit studies for the Loan Officers, Chief Credit Officer and other Executive Management. You'll manage spread assignments, conduct financial analyses, and maintain related records and files. One of your key responsibilities is the preparation of a variety of credit department reports.

  • Responsible for supporting the Credit Administration team in analyzing credit and collateral information to determine risk involved in lending money to customers. Collecting, organizing, analyzing company financials to ensure Bank compliance, and updates the Bank’s systems accordingly. Work directly with clients to resolve compliance issues and operational inquiries.
  • Review client financials and perform sensitivity analysis to evaluate credit risk in connection with Bank structures. Prepare in-depth reports providing plans of action based on qualitative and quantitative research.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Bank groups to execute treasury management products, foreign exchange instruments, derivatives as well as legal documents. Produce loan packages for new and restructured loans.
  • Facilitate reporting and requests on behalf of the Bank with third parties, e.g. field auditors, appraisers, etc. Monitor loan disbursements to ensure compliance with Bank regulations.

What You'll Need

  • 2+ years of related experience in Accounting, Finance or Economics or similar field.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required.
  • Entry level to intermediate knowledge of general banking operations, including deposit operations, loan administration, treasury management and/or other commercial banking products and services.
  • Entry level to intermediate knowledge of applicable regulatory and legal compliance obligations, rules and regulations, industry standards and practices.
  • Entry level to intermediate knowledge and understanding of financial statements and ability to analyze business and financial data.
  • Strong analytical, conceptual, communication, leadership, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to self-motivate and work productively without supervision.
  • Intermediate speaking and writing communication skills.

Compensation: Hourly range for new hires is generally $36.74 - $45.38 for Costa Mesa, CA. Hourly range for new hires is generally $36.74 - $36.74 for Reston, VA. Hourly range for new hires is generally $39.93 - $49.33 for San Francisco, CA. Salary amount is determined by specific job location. In addition, the role may be eligible for annual bonus/incentives earned.

job.name: Supply Planner
job.description:
At YETI, we believe that time spent outdoors matters more than ever and our gear can make that time extraordinary. When you work here, you’ll have the opportunity to create exceptional, meaningful work and problem solve with innovative team members by your side. Together, you’ll help our customers get the high-quality gear they need to make the most of their adventures. We are BUILT FOR THE WILD™.

About The Role The Supply Planner plays one of the most visible and critical roles in ensuring our company has the right products, at the right places, at the right times. A Supply Planner is responsible for developing and executing end-to-end supply plans that ensure product availability, successful new product launches, and optimal inventory performance across assigned product categories. This role serves as a key cross-functional partner to Demand Planning, Sourcing, Product Development, Operations, Logistics, and Commercial teams to translate demand signals into executable supply strategies while balancing service, inventory, and cost objectives.

The position plays a critical role in launch readiness, supply risk management, capacity planning, and lifecycle management, ensuring products are available to support wholesale, direct-to-consumer, and international growth initiatives.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and maintain supply plans for assigned product categories and product portfolios.
  • Monitor inventory health, service levels, safety stock, and projected gaps to proactively mitigate supply risks.
  • Manage purchase order strategy and supplier execution to support demand plans and business objectives.
  • Lead inventory balancing activities across channels, regions, and distribution centers.
  • Evaluate supply constraints and recommend recovery plans to minimize customer and revenue impact.
  • Updates Purchase Orders based on vendor confirmation
  • Identifies products oversold to forecasts and develops contingency plans
  • Provides updated vendor forecasts monthly
  • Lead supply planning activities for new product launches, seasonal programs, and product line extensions.
  • Collaborate with suppliers and sourcing teams to align production capacity with forecasted demand.

Analysis and Reporting

  • Analyze forecast consumption, inventory trends, service performance, and fulfillment metrics.
  • Identify opportunities to improve planning processes, data quality, planning systems, and reporting capabilities.
  • Drive process standardization and supply planning best practices across product categories.
  • Support development of dashboards and management tools that improve decision-making and supply.
  • Reviews exceptions and organizes data to review with Sr. Planner or Manager to resolve.
  • Prepares data and material for daily meetings with Supply Planning Manager.
  • Prepares data and material for monthly SIOP supply review meetings.

Communication

job.name: Project Controls - Engineer III / Lead Engineer - Project Farma
job.description:
The successful candidate will reside in one of Project Farma's primary markets and be willing to travel domestically to meet client project requests. Project Farma’s purpose is to improve patient lives by accelerating the delivery of life-changing therapies. We accomplish this through the successful execution of high-quality life sciences projects across the full project lifecycle. Project Farma (PF) team members collaborate with cross-functional teams to build trusted client relationships, deliver an exceptional customer experience, and contribute to business growth by identifying opportunities and applying data-driven insights to support project planning, cost, schedule, and performance management.

All team members are expected to embody Project Farma’s values by being curious, personable, and unselfish, while maintaining a strong commitment to a Patient Focused and People First mindset.

The Project Controls - Engineer III / Lead Engineer is an advanced individual contributor with demonstrated depth in their technical discipline and a growing record of leading complex workstreams. This role applies strong subject‑matter expertise to solve high‑impact technical and operational challenges, supports technical decision‑making, and contributes to the evolution of standards, methods, or best practices within their area. The Principal Engineer works with a high degree of independence, mentors junior and peer engineers, and partners closely with project and people leaders—while remaining focused on technical delivery rather than formal people management.

Key Responsibilities As a Project Controls Engineer III / Lead Engineer, you will work collaboratively with clients, vendors, contractors, and other Project Farma Team Members to support projects related to biomanufacturing across the entire engineering lifecycle. You will apply your advanced technical skills to meet project team and client needs for developing / maintaining project schedules and monitoring project performance. This work will include interfacing directly with project management, client management and site personnel for the development of detailed integrated schedules. You will be responsible for delivering high quality work, forming and maintaining valuable, long-term relationships with our clients, and continually strengthening your technical and industry knowledge. This position will lead key project controls deliverables including but not limited to:

  • Summary project plans and milestone management reports
  • Detailed project execution schedules
  • Activity tracking and variance reports
  • Budget estimates, project cost reports and forecast trend analysis reports
  • Issue, risks and scenario analysis reports
  • Scope and change management impact analysis reports
  • Comprehensive monthly project status reports

job.description:
We are Indeed Flex. We Help People Get Jobs. Right now, we’re hiring!

We are a tech-first staffing platform that gives workers the freedom to choose their own shifts and businesses the power to hire with a click. We are removing the friction from the traditional agency model and replacing it with speed, transparency, and choice.

We operate with the agility and energy of a high-growth scale-up, but we are backed by the stability and resources of Indeed - the world’s #1 job site. This gives us a unique advantage: the freedom to innovate at speed, with the muscle to dominate the market.

💼 This is an in-office role at the Indeed Domain Tower, five days per week with the option to work from home on Thursdays. A relocation package is available upon moving to Austin and commencing employment.

The Role

The Senior Financial Analyst will join the FP&A Team under the Strategy department and play a pivotal role in driving growth, enhancing profitability, and supporting business transformation. As an individual contributor that operates highly independently with minimal supervision, you will take full ownership of building, enhancing, evolving and running the commercial finance partnership with the US Revenue department and respective FP&A activities and processes.

What you’ll be doing

Business Partnership & Commercial Finance

  • Partner closely with the US Revenue team to provide financial insight and commercial decision support.
  • Support pricing, customer profitability, commercial terms, renewals, and new business opportunities.
  • Develop financial models and scenario analyses to evaluate profitability and support commercial decision-making.
  • Identify opportunities to improve revenue performance and profitability.
  • Develop a strong understanding in cost drivers like payroll taxes and workers compensation insurance.

FP&A, Forecasting & Performance Management

  • Own monthly revenue and gross profit forecasting, with clear visibility into pricing, volume, mix, and cost drivers.
  • Support annual planning, budgeting, and performance management processes .
  • Deliver reporting, analysis, and insights to senior leadership to support decision-making.
  • Reconcile financial and sales data to ensure integrity and improve forecast accuracy.
  • Continuously improve reporting, processes, and governance to drive efficiency and better decision support.
  • Collaborate closely with Accounting and Finance Operations to ensure robust support for the Revenue function.
  • Identify manual bottlenecks in the current FP&A cycle. Design and implement automated workflows to reduce time spent on data manipulation.

Cross-Functional & Strategic Support

  • Partner with Accounting and Finance Operations to ensure a robust month-end close process.
  • Lead or support ad hoc projects and strategic initiatives across Commercial Finance and FP&A.

job.name: GIS Analyst (Entry Level, Hybrid - Austin)
job.description:
Description ICF is growing in the south-central United States, and we need more environmental professionals to share in this growth! ICF is seeking a motivated, early-career GIS Analyst to join our team and provide geospatial information system (GIS) expertise to support environmental services for infrastructure projects throughout Texas and the U.S. As a GIS Analyst, you will turn geospatial information into practical insights that help clients navigate environmental review, permitting, compliance, and planning. You will work with GIS professionals, biologists, archaeologists, planners, engineers, and project managers to deliver reliable information that supports informed project decisions.

This is an entry-level position expected to begin in the Summer 2027. The role is hybrid from our Austin, TX office, with the potential for infrequent, occasional travel in Texas (0-10%). The GIS Analyst will provide GIS services and expertise supporting environmental consulting projects in Texas and across the U.S. by developing, managing, analyzing, and visualizing geospatial data for environmental reviews, permitting, compliance, planning, and infrastructure projects.

Why work for ICF? At ICF you are our raison d'être , a team of environmental experts prizing scientific rigor, regulatory insight, work-life balance, and a commitment to integrity. You will enjoy the diversity of work, entrepreneurial opportunities, and mission of building a more prosperous and resilient world. Whatever you seek, there is a reason so many of our people have stayed with ICF for over 20 years.

On Our Team, You Will

  • Apply your GIS technical expertise to help solve our clients’ toughest compliance challenges, involving Clean Water Act (CWA), Endangered Species Act (ESA), and federal and state laws
  • Build a reliable foundation for project decisions by developing, maintaining, and analyzing geospatial data in ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online, with well-organized geodatabases, clear metadata, and quality checks
  • Communicate complex information clearly and concisely through high-quality maps, figures, tables, web-based products, and data visualizations
  • Help field teams and project managers stay connected by preparing field maps, supporting GPS and ArcGIS Field Maps workflows, and integrating field observations into reliable project information
  • Integrate diverse sources of information to understand wetlands, wildlife habitat, land use, infrastructure, terrain, and environmental constraints
  • Help our team deliver dependable work efficiently by improving spatial analysis workflows and communicating progress, data limitations, and potential issues while balancing project priorities and deadlines
  • Learn and hone your consulting skills working with a variety of talented GIS specialists, biologists, archaeologists, planners, and project managers

job.name: Growth Hacker
job.description:
Company Description SentLogic is an emerging technology company focused on building data-driven products and solutions that help organizations grow efficiently and intelligently. The team values experimentation, rapid iteration, and measurable impact in all initiatives. SentLogic promotes a culture of autonomy, collaboration, and continuous learning, encouraging team members to propose, test, and scale new ideas. The company embraces remote work and relies on modern tools and processes to support distributed, outcome-oriented teams.
Role Description This is a full-time remote role for a Growth Hacker at SentLogic. The Growth Hacker will design and run experiments across acquisition, activation, retention, and referral channels to drive sustainable user and revenue growth. Day-to-day responsibilities include identifying growth opportunities, developing and executing data-informed marketing strategies, analyzing web and product analytics, and optimizing funnels for conversion.   • Familiarity with digital marketing channels such as SEO, paid media, email, and social media is beneficial.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Marketing, Business, Data Analytics) or equivalent practical experience.

At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture and technology to become the best version of you. And we’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.

Service line - Position Title: Credit Finance & Client Reporting (Senior) At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

About Global Delivery Services Global Delivery Services refers to EY's worldwide network of service delivery centres. The GDS team plays an important role in EY’s strategy by ensuring effective support to EY’s growth agenda.

Our journey started in 2002 with approximately 200 people. Today we stand at 80,000+ professionals in ten locations around the world. We operate in Argentina, China, Hungary, India, Philippines, Poland, Sri Lanka, Mexico, Spain and the United Kingdom.

Client service is focused on providing Consulting, Assurance, Tax, Strategy & Transactions, and Knowledge support to our clients around the world. The teams enable account teams worldwide to provide seamless, high-quality, value-added support, helping deliver exceptional client service.

Enablement Services provides cost-effective, high-skilled, and innovative services to support EY’s global and local enablement teams. Markets, BMC, AWS, Finance and Accounting, Risk Management, Procurement, People Shared Services, IT Service Delivery and IT Global Infrastructure services, are among the services offered by Enablement Services.

Our innovation specialists serve the GDS Client Service and Enablement Services teams, along with Service Lines, Core Business Services and Sectors. The team brings the desired environment, technologies and skilled teams together for facilitation, rapid prototyping and innovative thinking. job.name: Assistant Program Manager – Customer Experience & Automation (Kirana Club)
job.description:
About Kirana Club India has over 12 million kirana stores, and most still depend on traditional wholesale markets to source products for their shops.

Kirana Club is changing how these retailers discover, source, and replenish inventory. With 4 million+ kiranas on the platform, we're building a commerce marketplace that connects retailers directly with brands and sellers.

Now part of the Meesho family, we're entering our next phase of growth, with an opportunity to rethink how B2B commerce and fulfilment work at scale.

About The Role We're looking for someone who loves solving problems at their root, building scalable systems, and using technology to make things work better.

As we scale, thousands of retailers interact with our platform every day — placing orders, tracking deliveries, raising concerns, and requesting resolutions. Our goal is to build a customer experience where things work so reliably that retailers rarely need to contact support.

You'll own initiatives that improve the end-to-end retailer experience by identifying recurring problems, understanding why they happen, and building long-term solutions through better processes, product improvements, and automation.

This is not a traditional customer support management role. You won't be managing support agents or day-to-day ticket queues. Instead, you'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Customer Support to systematically eliminate friction and build scalable customer experience systems.

What You'll Work On

  • Root cause analysis: Deep dive into customer complaints, support tickets, order journeys, and operational data to identify recurring issues and their underlying causes.
  • Process and system design: Build scalable workflows, SOPs, escalation mechanisms, and resolution processes that prevent recurring problems and reduce manual intervention.
  • Automation and AI: Identify opportunities to automate repetitive support workflows, customer communication, refunds, and issue resolution using technology and AI.
  • Customer experience improvements: Work with Product and Engineering to simplify customer journeys, improve self-service capabilities, and proactively resolve issues before customers need to reach out.
  • End-to-end problem ownership: Take problems from identification to solution design, implementation, and impact measurement. Ensure fixes are permanent rather than temporary workarounds.
  • Data-driven prioritization: Quantify the impact of different customer experience problems and prioritize initiatives that meaningfully improve customer satisfaction, retention, and operational efficiency.

Some of the problems you might work on include reducing delivery-related complaints, automating refund and claims workflows, improving NDR resolution, and designing better customer communication systems.

What We're Looking For

job.name: Assistant Program Manager - Catalog (Kirana Club)
job.description:
About The Role Kirana Club (a Meesho company) is India's largest kirana community, and our commerce business is scaling fast. We need many times more sellers, SKUs and categories than we have today: the right ones, at the right price, reliably in stock.

You'll own the highest-impact problems across supply, catalogue and category. Most of them are 0→1: spot the problem in the data, build the first version by hand, prove it works, then scale it through product and automation. You'll work in a lean team with a high bar for talent and a direct line to leadership, where one sharp person changes the trajectory of the business.

What You'll Do You will work on super high impact problem statements across supply, category, catalogue, pricing

  • Scale supply. Redesign how sellers join, list and go live, and push towards self-serve so supply can grow 10x without the team growing 10x.
  • Catalogue as a growth lever. Retailers only buy what they understand. You own listing quality, attributes, images and pricing accuracy, and you measure how they affect conversion.
  • Shape what we sell. Turn retailer demand signals into a clear plan: which categories, brands and SKUs to add, and where we're thin or overpriced.
  • Seller growth. Find out why some sellers take off while others stall, whether it's price, range, stock reliability or visibility, and build what moves them up.
  • Fix problems at the root. When the same issue shows up across sellers, build the template, validation or process that stops it for good.
  • Build new playbooks. Launch new categories, seller types or regions from scratch, then hand over a playbook that scales.
  • Work with product. Turn operational noise into crisp problem statements, and co-own with the PM what gets built and in what order

What We're Looking For

  • 2–5 years' experience with a strong academic or professional track record (consulting, marketplace, or high-growth startup)
  • You quantify a problem before proposing a fix and are comfortable with messy ops data (SQL is a plus)
  • You build mechanisms, not workarounds
  • You love getting your hands dirty and shipping a scrappy v1 fast
  • You can hold a team accountable, including one you don't directly employ
  • You've grown fast: early promotions or ownership beyond your level

If you're excited by 0→1 problems, building from scratch and working with lean, high-calibre teams, this role is for you.

job.name: Compensation Manager
job.description:
Location: Any location in the United States

Work Arrangement: Remote

A Day in the Life The Compensation Manager manages the Firm’s compensation programs and processes to support competitive, equitable, and compliant pay practices. This position is responsible for compensation strategy, market benchmarking, pay structure development, annual compensation and bonus cycles, and compensation governance. The Compensation Manager serves as a trusted advisor to Firm leaders, HR partners, and Talent Acquisition while managing and developing compensation team members.

A typical day as a Compensation Manager might include the following:

  • Manages the administration and continuous improvement of the Firm’s compensation programs, policies, practices, and related tools.
  • Oversees annual and exception compensation, promotion, and bonus processes, including planning, system preparation, data review, leadership guidance, approvals, and implementation.
  • Interprets and applies the Firm’s compensation philosophy to support consistent, market-aligned, and performance-driven pay decisions.
  • Develops compensation recommendations that balance market competitiveness, internal equity, employee experience, performance, geographic considerations, and Firm practices.
  • Leads participation in industry compensation surveys and oversees the collection, validation, submission, and analysis of survey data.
  • Maintains relationships with survey providers and evaluates market data sources to support reliable benchmarking and informed decision-making.
  • Oversees the development and maintenance of compensation ranges, structures, and guidelines across positions, service lines, locations, and geographic markets.
  • Consults with Firm leaders, HR business partners, and Talent Acquisition on hiring ranges, promotions, compensation adjustments, retention concerns, and other pay decisions.
  • Advises on job leveling, position evaluations, organizational structure, and role alignment to support workforce planning and career progression.
  • Partners with HR and business leaders to identify compensation risks, evaluate internal equity concerns, and recommend appropriate actions.
  • Takes a total rewards perspective when developing compensation recommendations, considering base pay, incentives, benefits, and career growth opportunities.
  • Leverages compensation, workforce, and market data to identify trends, evaluate program effectiveness, model potential outcomes, and provide actionable insights to leadership.
  • Utilizes emerging technologies, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve compensation analysis, streamline processes, enhance reporting, and support data-driven decision-making.
  • Establishes and maintains compensation governance processes, decision-making frameworks, and leader guidance to promote consistency across the Firm.
  • Monitors compensation-related regulatory requirements and supports compliance with applicable federal, state, and local law

job.description:
No Responses to Applications??

Get Hired with a Process which Works!

Many job seekers assume their skills have expired simply because they’ve been out of the workforce or recently laid off. But the truth is, your foundation is still valuable — it just needs sharpening. Despite layoffs and market shifts, the tech industry still needs skilled developers. The challenge is proving you’re ready to contribute. Rejections can be discouraging, but they don’t reflect your true potential — they reflect your preparation.

Re‑entering the tech industry can feel overwhelming, especially after a layoff or career gap. But you don’t have to do it alone. SynergisticIT’s JOPP gives you a fast, structured path back into the field.

If your applications disappear into a black hole, you’re experiencing the modern hiring funnel. Most resumes never reach a hiring manager. Recruiters are looking for job-ready signals—specific stacks, strong project depth, relevant certifications, and clear experience narratives. That’s why “I applied a lot” often leads to silence. The fix is not more applications. The fix is improving what your application communicates in the first 10 seconds.

If you’ve been unemployed for 3–6+ months—or longer—you’ve probably seen how quickly the market can change. A career gap or an outdated tech stack can reduce callbacks, even when you have talent. Recruiters may assume your skills are outdated or your confidence is lower. But gaps don’t define ability. They simply require a strategy: refresh your stack, rebuild proof of work, and re-enter with structure.

Since 2010 , SynergisticIT has helped candidates return to the workforce and land full-time jobs at major employers—companies like Google, Apple, PayPal, Visa, Western Union, Wells Fargo, Intel, Citi, JPMC, Walmart Labs, Deloitte , and more—often with offers between $90,000 and $154,000 depending on role and expertise.

Why gaps hurt—and how to neutralize them

Employers worry about currency: are your tools current? Can you still perform? The solution is demonstrating recent, relevant work: projects, certifications, and interview readiness. JOPP helps you rebuild that proof and confidence systematically.

SynergisticIT commonly supports hiring pipelines for roles such as junior software programmer , Java full stack engineer , Python/Java developer , DevOps/cloud engineer , plus data-track roles like data analyst , BI analyst , data engineer , data scientist , and ML/AI engineer . Today, real-time data is buried in legacy tools that weren't designed for constant disruption. By the time an issue surfaces, it has already snowballed, sending everyone into firefighting mode. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. This expert team of engineers is responsible for building new analytics capabilities in Elasticsearch’s completely new compute engine, and accessed via our new piped query language called ES|QL. This role includes providing technical vision and direction for the customer/user interfaces and for the underlying language syntax and compute infrastructure. This role requires related past technical experience in addition to the ability to work cross-organization.

Our company is distributed by intention. We hire the best engineers we can find wherever they are, whoever they are. We collaborate across continents every day over email, GitHub, Zoom, and Slack. At our best, we write fast, scalable, and intuitive software. We believe that the best way to do that is to empower individual engineers, code review every change, decide big things by consensus, and strive for incremental improvements.

What You Will Be Doing: As a full-time Elasticsearch contributor, you will define, lead, and contribute to the development of data-intensive enhancements. You’ll research the latest features, data structures, and algorithms in the industry to ensure we’re building the right capabilities for our users. You’ll work directly with our partners and product teams to understand their needs and build out a strategic vision for the longer term. You’ll bring your past experience in analytics systems to help build and drive an innovative roadmap for ES|QL and the compute engine. As an authority in several areas of Elasticsearch, everyone will turn to you when they have a question about that area. You'll improve those areas based on your questions and your instincts.

Our globally distributed team of expert engineers is focused on the search and query (ES|QL) analytics capabilities of Elasticsearch. Nos solutions d’imagerie médicale rationalisent le flux d’informations, simplifient les processus complexes, maximisent l’efficacité et mettent en lumière l’inconnu. Nous permettons aux médecins d'apporter aux patients les réponses dont ils ont besoin plus rapidement et d'améliorer les résultats pour tous. Grâce à une imagerie plus accessible, on sort les patients de l’obscurité.

Basée à Raleigh, en Caroline du Nord, et à Montréal, Intelerad compte près de 800 employés dans des bureaux répartis dans quatre pays. L'entreprise offre à près de 2 000 organisations de soins de santé à travers le monde la rapidité, l'évolutivité et la simplicité nécessaires pour augmenter les performances de l'entreprise tout en, surtout, en améliorant les résultats des patients. L’équipe évolue vers une approche de travail axée sur l’intelligence artificielle, où les outils de programmation assistée par agents intelligents occupent une place centrale dans le processus de développement. job.name: Senior Software Developer - Ad Tech
job.description:
Remote - Canada

Position Overview:

You have deep experience in programmatic advertising – enough to own the architecture of the systems inside our advertising organization and help set our technical direction, not just execute it. You’ll influence the foundational decisions about how our ad systems are built and how they scale, step into complex implementations to stabilize and simplify them, and turn early client relationships into trusted partnerships through technical work that holds up.

Our teams build the systems behind more than 10 billion ad requests a day for high-traffic media & entertainment and news publishers – this is a demanding, hands-on role. You should have enough range across the advertising domain to architect across it, the depth to be the person other developers come to when performance and reliability are on the line, and the ability to move fluidly between a deep technical conversation with developers and a strategic one with product, bringing everyone along.

Scope of Impact & Autonomy:

  • Your solutions are designed to have a positive impact on the entire advertising organization and the broader developer group, not just a single project.
  • You own architecture decisions that are difficult or expensive to reverse, and you’re trusted to make them.
  • You advise Directors and product leadership on technical strategy, privacy and data-handling frameworks, and where we invest.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Own the architecture. Design, build, and evolve the systems behind our ad stack — high-throughput, low-latency services where performance and reliability are the job, not an afterthought.
  • Set technical direction. Influence the foundational decisions about how our ad systems are built and how they scale. Help set the direction, not just deliver against it.
  • Untangle the hard problems. Lead the resolution of the messiest issues — real-time bidding bottlenecks, data synchronization drops, broken platform integrations — and provide the breakthrough on work that has stalled for weeks.
  • Partner with product. Work directly with advertising product owners to shape what gets built. Explain tradeoffs clearly, push back when something doesn’t add up, and propose alternatives — steering product thinking rather than just taking requirements and shipping them.
  • Set the standard. Mentor developers, define what developer excellence looks like in practice, and hold the bar on code review and documentation.
  • Advise leadership. Partner with our leadership team on long-term technical strategy and on the privacy and data-handling frameworks that govern how we work.

Technical Expectations:

job.name: Staff Software Engineer, ML Platform
job.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Staff Software Engineer, ML Platform based in Canada. As a Staff Software Engineer, you will shape the architecture and technical direction of a next-generation machine learning platform supporting large-scale AI and generative AI initiatives. You’ll bridge established MLOps practices with advanced LLM infrastructure, building reliable systems for model serving, intelligent routing, GPU orchestration, and automated evaluation. Working across engineering, data science, infrastructure, and risk teams, you’ll enable developers to deploy and operate models efficiently in production. You’ll also lead complex technical initiatives, influence platform-wide decisions, and mentor senior engineers. This remote opportunity is ideal for a highly experienced technical leader passionate about scalable AI infrastructure, performance optimization, and building platforms that empower other teams.

Accountabilities

  • Define and own the long-term technical architecture and multi-year roadmap for ML model serving, routing, and evaluation infrastructure.
  • Establish platform-wide engineering standards and produce technical design documents that guide implementation across multiple teams.
  • Align product engineering, data science, risk, and infrastructure stakeholders on shared architectural decisions, including GPU capacity management and Kubernetes resource allocation.
  • Lead the evolution of traditional MLOps systems into advanced generative AI infrastructure, integrating modern LLM inference engines and GPU orchestration capabilities.
  • Design and implement low-latency model-routing frameworks that intelligently direct requests between managed cloud services, such as AWS Bedrock, and self-hosted open-source models.
  • Architect, provision, and scale GPU-based serving environments on Kubernetes using technologies such as vLLM, Ray, and Triton.
  • Develop automated model evaluation, benchmarking, and observability frameworks to assess quality, latency, reliability, and model drift in production.
  • Build self-service ML platform capabilities that abstract infrastructure complexity and allow engineering and data science teams to deploy models efficiently across different frameworks.
  • Optimize inference performance and cost through improved GPU utilization, capacity planning, batching strategies, request routing, and model selection.
  • Ensure platform services meet enterprise-grade requirements for availability, scalability, security, and low-latency performance.
  • Lead complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives through influence and collaboration, while mentoring senior engineers and supporting their professional development.
  • Maintain and continuously improve platform systems to support the organization's expanding machine learning and AI requirements.

We've built proprietary tech that uses computer vision to watch live TV and improve the content with contextually-aware commercials, content, and games. Our tech also automates the manual AV tasks that venues have to do every day, to make bar management easier, standardized, and more profitable. We're venture-capital backed and graduated from Y Combinator, the world's top tech accelerator, in winter 2020. Program alumni include Airbnb, Instacart, DoorDash, etc. (www.ycombinator.com/topcompanies).

We are looking for an AI-native Staff Developer to join our growing team!

What We're Looking For This is a senior technical leadership role on the individual contributor track, working across teams. You'll own the technical direction of the systems other systems depend on, and take on the hardest, highest-risk problems until they're solved. You won't manage people, but you'll make the senior developers around you better.

AI is how we build at Taiv. Our developers work in Claude Code every day, and we're making Claude Code review a standard step in CI. We expect you to use AI across your whole workflow and to review its output as critically as a teammate's pull request, because our software runs on devices in thousands of venues. You can delegate work to AI, but you own the result. At staff level, you'll also set the AI patterns the rest of the team follows. Our technical interviews include an AI-assisted round where you use your usual tools, plus technical questions you'll answer without AI. When you apply, tell us about the last thing you built or shipped with AI tools, end to end: what you used, what the AI got wrong, and how you caught it.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the architecture of critical cross-team systems so they hold up at scale.
  • Set the patterns for how our teams build with AI: shared skills and prompts, Claude Code review in CI, and guardrails for AI-written code in critical systems.
  • Use AI agents to take on large changes (migrations, refactors, test coverage) that used to be too expensive to attempt.
  • Work the hardest problems leadership flags, from design through to delivery.
  • Help set standards for design reviews and architecture decisions across teams.

job.name: Software Architect - Containers / Virtualisation
job.description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in more than 80 countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

We are hiring a software architect for Canonical LXD and MicroCloud.

Our goal is to make clusters of compute, with system containers or virtual machines, "just work". It should be trivial to stand up a small cloud using one, two or twenty servers. This is a challenging exercise in distributed systems, virtualisation, container technology, networking and storage. As with the Ubuntu desktop, our goal is to make it easy and to make it reliable for people to focus on the things that really matter to them rather than the OS and infrastructure.

LXD is a modern Golang system container and virtual machine orchestrator widely used on Ubuntu, ChromeOS and other Linux platforms. LXD engineering spans the entire software stack from low-level kernel work on namespaces, confinement, security, filesystems, VMMs and networking, to the high level management REST API and CLI. As a software architect, you will drive the architecture, design and evolution of LXD, and also Canonical MicroCloud which combines LXD with Ceph and OVN to make a lean, easy to use and resilient cluster-scale cloud infrastructure.

We are looking for an outstanding software architect and engineer with experience in Golang and C, with the leadership qualities needed to rally a team to ship outstanding products. Knowledge of modern cloud infrastructure offerings, their APIs and their underlying technologies is a must.

This is an opportunity for someone who wants to have a meaningful impact on modern cloud computing technologies. Canonical offers a fun, fast-paced team environment and a career full of learning and development.

Location : This is a home-based position available in EMEA and the Americas.

The role entails

  • Leadership of the LXD and MicroCloud architecture
  • Mentor, develop and advise colleagues in their career progression
  • Develop in Golang and C
  • Review code produced by other engineers
  • Ensure the product is secure and performant
  • Display technical leadership in Canonical and our communities
  • Work from home with global travel twice annually for company events

What We Are Looking For In You

Opportunity Information Management Group (IMG) is seeking a highly motivated Senior Linux Systems Administrator to join our team in Albany, NY area. This on-site position requires a professional who brings strong technical expertise, exceptional attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to problem-solving.

The successful candidate will support and administer an evolving infrastructure and data storage environment. The ideal candidate will have solid Linux System Administration experience and hands-on experience managing Linux servers, Cisco-based infrastructure, and NetApp storage environments.

Linux Systems Administration

Salary $110,000 to $145,000

Position Expectations

job.name: Agentic AI Architect - Intelligence Engineering (East)
job.description:
Who You’ll Work With

At Slalom, we co-create modern technology and software products with clients who are ready to accelerate their digital product development. We imagine how things can be made better, then set out to realize what’s possible — driving innovation with quality, resilience, and purpose. By blending design, product engineering, analytics, and automation, we build the custom-built software and data products of tomorrow. As a member of Intelligence Engineering, you’ll design and deliver innovative AI/ML and agentic AI solutions as part of intelligent products and automating / re-envisioning human workflows on Amazon Web Services, Azure, and Google Cloud. This includes architecting multi-agent systems, LLM-powered autonomous workflows, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and enterprise-grade AI governance frameworks using cutting-edge orchestration frameworks, tool-use protocols, and cloud-native AI services. You’ll help clients move from isolated proofs of concept to secure, scalable, observable systems that create real business value, while helping craft projects in their initial phases and delivering them with a team. What You’ll Do

job.name: Software Engineer, Developer Productivity
job.description:
About The Role Codex lets engineers work on many changes in parallel. That changes the demands on the systems around the code: source control needs to handle more concurrent work, builds and tests need to provide fast, trustworthy feedback, and releases need to stay safe. Engineering Acceleration builds and operates those systems for the teams developing ChatGPT, the API, Codex, and OpenAI’s infrastructure.

Our work spans source control, code review, development environments, builds, CI, and delivery. One example is Pando, our Git-compatible backend built with Codex, which now powers development in OpenAI’s monorepo and serves nearly a petabyte of Git data a day. We’re also evolving Bazel build and test infrastructure, scaling CI, and making it easier for teams to ship reliable software.

You’ll own projects within one or more of these areas, from technical design through adoption and operation. The work combines distributed systems engineering with a product mindset: understand where developers lose time or confidence, build a better default, and measure whether it actually helps. You’ll also use our models and coding agents to build the platform itself and explore what engineering workflows can become.

In This Role, You Will

Depending On Your Focus, You Could

  • Scale source control and our in-house code review and merge platform for large repositories and concurrent work by engineers and coding agents.
  • Make Bazel builds reproducible and fast, improve test selection and failure diagnosis, and design efficient CI scheduling, remote execution, and caching systems.
  • Build development environments and self-service workflows that make it easy to get started, reproduce CI failures, and use reliable infrastructure by default.
  • Evolve deployment platforms with progressive rollouts, automated health evaluation, and rollback mechanisms that help teams release safely.
  • Use AI to improve engineering workflows, from diagnosing failures and debugging flaky tests to helping validate and remediate changes.

Across these areas, you will work directly with engineers to identify high-impact problems, use telemetry and feedback to evaluate results, and own your systems in production, including an on-call rotation.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have 7+ years of software engineering experience, including building infrastructure, developer tools, or distributed systems.
  • Have designed, shipped, and operated production software in at least one relevant area, such as source control, build systems, CI/CD, or developer platforms.
  • Enjoy debugging across system boundaries and making thoughtful tradeoffs among performance, reliability, correctness, and cost.
  • Care about developer experience and can turn user feedback and ambiguous problems into tools people choose to use.
  • Are excited to build with coding agents and to design systems that support both human and agent workflows.

job.name: Software Development Engineer III, Machine Learning Annapurna - System Integration
job.description:
Description Do you want to build AI-powered tooling that keeps custom silicon running reliably at scale? In Annapurna Labs at Amazon Web Services (AWS), we sit at the intersection of software and hardware, designing the systems that detect failures, generate repair instructions, and automate qualification for Trainium products. As a Software Development Engineer III, you will lead the technical design and delivery of this tooling platform — combining generative AI techniques with deep hardware knowledge to solve problems that few teams in the industry encounter. With hardware complexity and scope expanding rapidly, this is a rare opportunity to shape how we bring the next generation of custom chips to operational stability.

Key job responsibilities

  • Design and deliver generative AI-based tools that identify complex hardware failures, dynamically create repair instructions from hardware system designs, and automate the qualification framework for post-new-product-introduction hardware changes on Trainium systems.
  • Own system design decisions across the tooling software stack, evaluating tradeoffs in scalability, maintainability, and performance while partnering with silicon design and operations teams on cross-functional technical discussions.
  • Collaborate with hardware design and sustaining teams to align tooling updates with upcoming silicon changes, creating the right integration checkpoints to ensure successful delivery.
  • Drive adoption of engineering best practices across the team through code reviews, design reviews, and mentorship — raising the quality bar and helping fellow engineers grow.
  • Evaluate and refine generative AI model outputs used in the tooling platform, applying responsible AI practices to ensure accuracy and reliability at production scale.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing system health metrics for the tooling platform, then join a design review where a teammate walks through a new generative AI model for automated failure diagnosis on Trainium hardware. You ask probing questions that sharpen the approach. After lunch, you pair with an engineer to work through a tricky data-modeling problem, then shift to a cross-team sync with hardware design engineers to align on upcoming silicon changes that will require updates to your qualification automation. Later, you write a technical document outlining how the tooling will scale to support the next generation of Trainium products.

Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role We are looking for a Principal Software Development Engineer (Service Platform & Orchestration) to join our team. This is a Hybrid (3 days in office) role, reporting to the Director, Software Engineering in the Zero Trust Exchange department. In this high-ownership position, you will engineer the management plane and reliability systems that govern ZIA’s fleet lifecycle at massive scale.

This is a hands-on building role where you will lead the transformation of our infrastructure from legacy automation into a stateful, durable management plane (built on Temporal) to achieve deterministic “one-touch” provisioning and lifecycle operations. You will treat “infrastructure as a distributed system,” developing self-healing capabilities and AI-driven SRE practices for a global fleet of 100k+ instances.

What You’ll Do (Role Expectations)

  • Develop framework-level services and internal APIs that ensure all new products are delivered “orchestration-ready” with reliability hooks built directly into the code

job.name: Software Engineer, Infrastructure
job.description:
About Cape Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected and have privacy.

We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.

Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information.

The Team At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what's possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve "impossible" problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day.

The Role

To join our team, you should be excited to:

  • Dive into a well-funded but early-stage startup. We’re in a scrappy phase, be comfortable getting a little uncomfortable.
  • Reclaim some of the personal privacy we have all sacrificed as smartphone adoption has grown.
  • Flex your technical skills on hard, important problems with serious implications for consumer privacy and national security.

job.name: Platform Engineer, Kubernetes Infrastructure (GroqMetal)
job.description:
Mission GroqMetal is building the infrastructure platform that turns large-scale physical compute into a reliable, isolated, customer-consumable product. As a Platform Engineer, Kubernetes Infrastructure you will build and operate production software within the GroqMetal platform, helping deliver Kubernetes as a commercial product for customers running large-scale AI training and inference workloads.

You will own meaningful platform components, work alongside experienced infrastructure engineers, and develop deep expertise in Kubernetes, distributed systems, and large-scale AI infrastructure.

Location: This role will be based in one of our three hiring hubs: the Dallas, San Francisco, or New York City area . The person hired for this role must be based in one of these three areas. You’ll have the flexibility to work remotely while we establish our local Groq office, with the expectation that this role will transition to onsite once the office opens.

Responsibilities & Opportunities In This Role

  • Build production Kubernetes platform capabilities: Implement APIs, controllers, operators, automation, and platform services that support the GroqMetal product by extending Kubernetes.
  • Own components end to end: Take responsibility for well-defined platform capabilities from design and implementation through testing, deployment, operation, and continuous improvement.
  • Operate what you build: Improve reliability, observability, performance, and operational efficiency, and participate in diagnosing and resolving production issues.
  • Build a Kubernetes platform as a commercial platform: Develop capabilities used by dedicated customers running large-scale AI training and inference workloads.
  • Develop distributed systems expertise: Build software that handles retries, failures, concurrency, reconciliation, and changing infrastructure state correctly.
  • Improve the platform: Identify reliability, scalability, and usability problems and work with the team to deliver durable solutions.
  • Collaboration is a core skill: Work within a team of experts to elevate the collective efforts of our team. Collaborate with engineers across infrastructure, inference, networking, infosec, and related teams to integrate platform capabilities holistically.

job.name: Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure
job.description:
Company Overview Promise modernizes how government agencies and utilities support people in financial difficulty. We build technology that makes it simple for residents to receive benefits, engage with assistance programs, set up flexible payment plans, and stay on track—while helping agencies increase efficiency, recover revenue, and deliver services with dignity. Our mission is to transform public systems so they work better for everyone, especially the most vulnerable.

Our team includes experts from companies like Palantir, Google, Stripe , and esteemed government leaders. We work hard and believe deeply in what we do. We're looking for excellent people to build innovative, resilient technology.

Backed by over $50 million in funding from top investors – such as Reid Hoffman, Howard Schultz, Michael Seibel, Y Combinator, 8VC, The General Partnership, First Round Capital, Kapor Capital, XYZ Ventures, and Bronze Investments – Promise has been recognized as one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies of 2022,” “Forbes Next Billion-Dollar Startups 2024,” and Y Combinator’s #1 GovTech startup.

About The Role Promise is looking for a Platform & Infrastructure Engineer to help shape how we deliver and run software — with automation at the center of everything you do.

You'll build the systems that let us ship faster, smarter, safer, and better. Working closely with our Product and Forward Deployed Engineers, you'll give them the foundation they need to solve real customer problems — so they can stay focused on exactly that.

The through line of this role: fewer humans in the loop for the things that don't need them. That means owning deployments, environment setup, security, on-call triage, policy checks, cost reviews, and compliance evidence — and systematically taking humans out of those flows wherever it makes sense.

What You'll Do

  • Build and own our GCP infrastructure, Kubernetes clusters, and Terraform IaC
  • Own CI/CD across all services — end to end
  • Build internal platforms and tooling that help product engineers ship with less friction
  • Use AI to automate platform work that used to require a human
  • Respond to incidents, own the postmortem, and close the loop so they don't repeat
  • Partner with Engineering, IT, and Security to build the pipelines our products run on

What Will Help You Succeed

  • 5+ years in software or infrastructure, with meaningful time in a platform, infra, or SRE role
  • Kubernetes experience in production
  • Solid Terraform or equivalent IaC experience
  • A track record of building internal systems other teams depend on and trust
  • You've been on-call for things you built, and you have real opinions about what that taught you
  • You use AI tools in your own work and can speak to how and why

Nice to Have

  • Google Cloud Platform (our primary cloud)
  • ArgoCD experience
  • TypeScript or Go
  • Fintech, Payments, or GovTech background
  • SOC 2, FedRAMP, or PCI experience

job.name: Senior Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer
job.description:
We’re seeking a Senior Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to join us in our mission to transform the discovery of therapeutics and materials.

As a member of the Machine Learning team, you’ll play a key role in building and maintaining the systems that put ML models and AI agents to work in drug discovery. LiveDesign ML trains and serves models on live project data, both in our own clusters and in customers' LiveDesign environments. Bunsen is an agentic platform where every session runs an AI agent in its own isolated Kubernetes pod. We also run locked-down environments for federated-learning collaborations with pharma partners.

You'll own the infrastructure behind these products, across our own clusters and customer clouds on GCP and AWS. Today, ML engineers handle it alongside feature work. You'll make it your focus: repeatable customer deployments, strong isolation for AI-generated code, and reliable, cost-efficient GPU systems.

Who Will Love This Job

  • A Terraform or OpenTofu and Helm writer who has shipped with GitOps
  • A solid Python and shell scripter
  • A security-minded engineer who defaults to least privilege, managed secrets, and segmented networks
  • A clear communicator who enjoys working closely with ML engineers and scientists

What You’ll Do

  • Turn customer installs and upgrades into versioned, GitOps-driven releases (Helm, OpenTofu, Argo CD) with automated verification
  • Design isolation for multi-tenant agent sandboxes: network policy, workload identity, runtime sandboxing, and egress control
  • Secure CI/CD and the software supply chain with keyless auth, ephemeral runners, and pinned, signed images
  • Build and operate locked-down partner environments with private networking, default-deny egress, just-in-time access, and audit logging
  • Keep GPU-heavy training and inference reliable and cost-efficient, backed by observability, SLOs, and on-call

What You Should Have

  • At least six years of infrastructure, platform, or SRE experience
  • In-depth understanding of Kubernetes operation (not just deployment)
  • Robust background with GCP (and some familiarity with AWS)

We’d prefer to hire someone who has experience with:

  • Running GPU workloads and model serving (vLLM, Knative) on Kubernetes
  • Sandboxing untrusted code (gVisor, Kata Containers, Cilium)
  • Shipping software into customer-owned or restricted-egress clouds
  • Argo Workflows or batch/HPC scheduling
  • Regulated environments (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GxP)
  • Operating LLM or agent platforms

job.name: Platform Engineer (Kubernetes)
job.description:
Senior Platform Engineer

We are an established global financial firm adding an experienced platform engineer to help develop and expand its internal computing platform. The environment combines physical servers, virtualization, and Kubernetes to support demanding research and investment workloads.

This position blends software engineering with infrastructure ownership. You’ll develop tools that coordinate compute resources, improve platform reliability, and make it easier for development teams to deploy and run their applications.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop distributed services and automation for provisioning and managing compute infrastructure.
  • Create consistent, repeatable environments through automated configuration and policy enforcement.
  • Identify capacity, availability, and performance limitations, then implement improvements.
  • Strengthen failure recovery and reduce operational dependencies through resilient system design.
  • Evaluate and integrate commercial products and open-source technologies.
  • Collaborate with developers and internal users to translate workload requirements into infrastructure capabilities.
  • Share responsibility for production support, scheduled maintenance, and incident response.

What You’ll Bring

  • At least six years of hands-on experience supporting substantial compute infrastructure.
  • Strong Kubernetes knowledge, including cluster operations and the needs of applications running on the platform.
  • Experience administering Linux and managing physical server fleets at scale.
  • Python programming skills for infrastructure tooling and automation.
  • Familiarity with server virtualization and its operation in production environments.
  • Experience diagnosing latency issues and tuning system and network performance.
  • Working knowledge of IP routing and network troubleshooting.
  • Experience developing recovery procedures and maintaining continuity for critical services.

How You Work

You take ownership of complex technical problems, communicate clearly across teams, and balance immediate operational needs with lasting engineering improvements. You’re comfortable working independently while partnering closely with the people who depend on your platform.

job.name: Confluent - Staff Software Engineer - Infrastructure
job.description:
Introduction At IBM Software, we transform client challenges into solutions. Building the world’s leading AI-powered, cloud-native products that shape the future of business and society. Our legacy of innovation creates endless opportunities for IBMers to learn, grow, and make an impact on a global scale. Working in Software means joining a team fueled by curiosity and collaboration. You’ll work with diverse technologies, partners, and industries to design, develop, and deliver solutions that power digital transformation. With a culture that values innovation, growth, and continuous learning, IBM Software places you at the heart of IBM’s product and technology landscape. Here, you’ll have the tools and opportunities to advance your career while creating software that changes the world. With Confluent, data doesn’t sit still. We put information in motion, streaming in near real time so organizations can react faster, build smarter, and deliver experiences as dynamic as the world around them.

Your Role And Responsibilities About the Team

The Secure Compute Team builds and operates the foundational infrastructure layer that powers Confluent Cloud. Our mission is to enable the secure execution of code and data processing in multi-tenant environments across AWS, Azure, and GCP at scale. We provide the essential building blocks, including isolation, identity, and networking, that empower both our customers and internal product teams to innovate without compromising security.

As Confluent's product portfolio continues to expand, our team sits at the center of the company's growth strategy. We own a polyglot, container-based runtime that operates across thousands of clusters globally, solving some of the most complex challenges in distributed systems and cloud-native architecture. By balancing world-class security with operational efficiency, we ensure Confluent Cloud remains the trusted platform for mission-critical workloads, even in the most highly regulated industries.

About The Role As a Staff Software Engineer on the Secure Compute Platform team, you will be a key technical leader responsible for building and evolving a next-generation, multi-tenant, cloud-native compute platform that safely runs both trusted and untrusted workloads at scale. Our platform is built on Kubernetes and operates across a large fleet of clusters spanning multiple public clouds, providing a unified abstraction layer for workload execution, lifecycle management, security, and operational excellence.

job.name: Software Engineer, Frontend
job.description:
About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Check out our Engineering Blog for more on our tech stack, mission and values!

  • Foster a culture of upholding industry-leading UX
  • Continuously improve our engineering processes, tools, and systems that allow us to scale the code base, productivity, and the team
  • Recruit, interview and develop your own interview questions, while fostering the culture of excellence, velocity and humility
  • Inspire and mentor less experienced engineers and interns

What You'll Need

  • Minimum of 5 years of frontend engineering experience preferred
  • Proficiency in JavaScript and React
  • Knack for getting the visuals right
  • Track record of shipping high-quality products and developing projects at scale
  • Ability to turn business and product ideas into engineering solutions
  • Desire to work in a fast-paced environment, continuously grow, and master your craft
  • Alignment with Ramp’s core values of enabling businesses to grow more by spending less

job.description:
Software Engineer at Wert Group, a Boston management consultancy. Remote from anywhere in the United States, full-time. A few small internal tools keep our projects running: a staffing planner, a client data room and scripts that turn client exports into tables our consultants can analyze.

You maintain them and build the next ones. Features and bug fixes in our TypeScript and Python web apps, data-cleaning scripts, tests, pull requests reviewed with our senior developer, deployments through CI to Azure. Before building anything you talk to the consultants who will use it.

You work with our senior developer and the analytics consultants. React or AWS would help.

You need:

  • A computer science degree, or a bootcamp plus a portfolio
  • Python, JavaScript or TypeScript
  • Git and pull requests
  • Basic SQL

Benefits: medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(k) with a company match, paid time off and holidays, a yearly professional development budget, and a laptop and home office setup.

Wert Group is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

job.name: Member of Technical Staff (Frontend)
job.description:
Astrocade is an AI technology company building super-intelligence for the interactive world, delivered through a breakout consumer platform.

Today's frontier models can write, reason, and generate video. None can build a world you can step into and act on. Interactive world models are one of the defining problems on the path to ASI, and the foundation of the next great consumer platform. Interactivity is the holy grail of content: not something you watch, but something that responds to you. We're further ahead than anyone: the only team building the intelligence and the platform together, and both are already live.

Our social UGC platform lets anyone create and play interactive experiences through natural language. And it's one of the fastest-growing consumer products in the world, with over 30 million users in just months since launch. Creators bring to life games, companions that remember and grow with them, learning experiences that adapt like a great tutor, and social worlds built with friends. The platform also powers our research with data no video dataset contains: millions of creators prompting and refining gives us paired data of human intent and the worlds that fulfill it, and every play session produces ground-truth, action-labeled interaction data at scale. All of it flows back into our models, and research ships to real players in days, spinning a flywheel no one else can build.

We are a small team from Google Research, Meta, FAIR, Character.ai, and Stanford, led alongside Fei-Fei Li, with frontier-scale compute and direct ownership of core model problems. We are backed by Sequoia Capital, Google, NVIDIA, and luminaries including Eric Schmidt and Jerry Yang.

The next foundational AI company will be built where world models meet a billion players. We're the rare place where frontier research and a breakout consumer platform are one company, and where your work ships to millions, not to a paper. Come build it with us.

About The Role Games are more engaging, more meaningful, and more fun than passive content - and we think everyone should be able to make them. As a Frontend Member of Technical Staff (MTS), you’ll help make that a reality. You’ll own the creation and play experiences that millions of users touch every day, working at the intersection of product intuition, AI-generated content, and consumer-grade polish. This is a small, dense team: you won’t be maintaining someone else’s system - you will be shaping how the platform feels.

What You’ll Do

Do you love building and pioneering in the technology space? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive and iterative delivery environment? job.description:
Location: Anywhere in Country

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

At EY, our purpose is to shape the future. The insights and quality services we provide help build trust and confidence in the capital markets and economies all over the world. We develop outstanding leaders who are teamed to deliver our promises to all our stakeholders. In so doing, we play a critical role in building a better working world for our people, for our clients and for our communities.

The opportunity The Platforms Practice specializes in mission-critical, intelligent platforms for the world’s most ambitious organizations. Using our product-driven, AI-centric approach, we empower organizations to build for the intelligent digital future. Our elite team of product leaders, data scientists, designers, and software engineers enable our clients to solve their most complex product challenges and positively impact people and the world. Software engineers are problem solvers. While most have deep expertise in specific areas of the technology stack (front end, back end, data, security etc.), all are comfortable swimming across lanes.   • Writing clean, maintainable code and creating specifications that support business objectives.

Regular travel may be required to meet with clients, providing you with the opportunity to engage directly with stakeholders.
