job.name: R&D Control and HIL Test Engineer
job.description:
The opportunity

Join our R&D Product Development team and help validate the next generation of power conversion and control systems. You will work in a cross-functional environment alongside design, control, embedded software, system engineering, and quality teams to ensure our products meet performance, reliability, and certification expectations.

In this role, you will validate hardware and control functions for power converters and energy storage applications. You will study system behavior under transient and fault conditions, support grid code compliance, and drive end-to-end traceability from requirements through to final validation reports. Your work directly shapes the robustness and certification readiness of products deployed in industrial and renewable energy applications.

To excel, you bring strong testing fundamentals, hands-on experience with HIL systems and lab benches, and the analytical mindset needed to debug signals, logs, and waveforms. You are structured in your documentation, curious about new technologies, and motivated to automate what others would repeat manually.

You will grow by working on real prototypes and productized systems, contributing to test automation frameworks, and collaborating with global engineering teams. You will deepen your expertise across power electronics, control algorithms, and grid compliance while building a strong foundation in certification and quality processes.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Define, execute, and maintain validation and verification activities for power electronic products, prototypes, and systems under development.
  • Analyze specifications and technical requirements and translate them into structured validation plans, test procedures, and acceptance criteria.
  • Execute validation tests in both factory and field environments for prototype and productized power conversion systems.
  • Study system stability and response to electrical transients including symmetrical and asymmetrical faults, voltage dips, frequency disturbances, and power oscillation damping scenarios.
  • Simulate, validate, and debug control algorithms and assess compliance with applicable grid codes.
  • Conduct technical analysis of logs, signals, errors, waveforms, and performance metrics, and generate clear, reusable validation reports.
  • Develop and implement test automation frameworks and scripts for lab and HIL-based validation activities.
  • Support product certification activities, component approval, and quality assurance processes, ensuring traceability from requirements to final reports.
  • Responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable external and internal regulations, procedures, and guidelines.
  • Living Hitachi Energy’s core values of safety and integrity, which means taking responsibility for your own actions while caring for your colleagues and the business.

That same technology-first mindset applies internally. Our people are highly technical, they build their own tools, and they expect our systems to be fast, well designed and secure by default.

Who you are

We are hiring an IT Manager to run internal technology operations and lead our help desk function. You will report to the CISO and work alongside a small team, with room to grow into more as the function develops.

This is a hands-on role, not a purely managerial one. You will be in the tenant, on the tickets, and close to the work.

To be considered for this role, you must reside in the greater Seattle area. This is a full-time, hybrid role working from the Prowess office two days per week. No third-party agencies, please .

What you will do

  • Run the help desk for a distributed workforce across two primary sites (Washington, USA and Ahmedabad, India) and remote colleagues worldwide, with service expectations the business can hold us to.
  • Microsoft 365 administration: Entra ID, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, Intune, Purview and Defender.
  • Identity and access administration: on and offboarding, access changes, group and role design, privileged access.
  • Endpoint fleet: procurement, build standards, configuration, patching, recovery and disposal.
  • Vendors, licensing and assets: renewals and a clear picture of what we own and what it costs.
  • Business continuity for internal systems: backup, restore testing, documented recovery expectations.
  • Security operations: vulnerability monitoring and remediation, logging, and incident response.
  • Documentation and improvement: upgrades, small projects, and standards that let someone else run this without you.

What makes this role different

We expect IT to accelerate AI adoption, not slow it down. Using AI well is central to Prowess's strategy. Where most organizations let risk-averse IT throttle adoption, we want internal technology to be an enabler: helping colleagues build and run their own tools quickly and safely, and taking on a growing share of how that tooling is supported. You do not need to have governed an AI platform before. You do need to have used these tools yourself, to be following where they are going, and to meet a risky request by describing what safe would look like rather than refusing it or waving it through.

Onsite Opportunity

Senior IT Support Engineer

Job Description (Primary Responsibilities) Daily IT & Network Operations

Maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize office network infrastructure (routers, switches, firewalls, Wi-Fi, VPNs, and network security devices) to ensure high availability and performance.

Administer Windows server environments, Azure AD, Microsoft 365, Exchange Online, Intune, and other enterprise collaboration platforms.

Perform advanced system administration, configuration, monitoring, and preventive maintenance across office IT infrastructure.

Employee Technical Support (L1/L2/L3)

Data Backup, Security & Operational Excellence

Manage and monitor backup systems and disaster recovery processes to ensure business continuity.

Administer endpoint security, operating system patching, antivirus solutions, identity management, and access control.

Support security incident response, vulnerability remediation, and compliance with corporate IT security policies.

Identify opportunities to improve IT support processes, automate repetitive tasks, and enhance operational efficiency.

5+ years of hands-on experience in IT Support, Systems Administration, or Enterprise Desktop Support, including experience providing L3 technical support in a corporate environment.

Technical Skills:

Expert-level troubleshooting of Windows and macOS operating systems.

job.name: Principal Software Development Engineer
job.description:
Description Amazon S3 holds the world's data. Customers of every size build on it because it gives them durability, scale, and control they can rely on, and because the controls around their data are as much a part of the product as the storage itself. Every request to S3 carries an authorization decision, made in line, at S3's request rate, within a latency budget measured in a small fraction of the request. That combination of scale, precision, and speed makes security in S3 one of the most interesting distributed systems problems at AWS.

We are building S3 for the next kind of usage. AI agents are becoming primary consumers of enterprise data, and they reach for data in patterns, at volumes, and on behalf of identities that look different from the applications and people S3 serves today. We want customers to find the security model simpler and more capable as that shift happens, and to be able to say yes to new uses of their data with confidence. Leading that work is what this role is for.

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to lead the technical direction for security in the Amazon S3 API and Request Processing organization. This organization owns the S3 API surface and the front end of the request path, which makes it the place where every access decision is made. This is a customer-facing security role: you will shape how access to S3 data is expressed by customers, evaluated on the request path, and understood by the people who are accountable for it. You will work across S3 and with partner teams in identity, analytics, and AI, and your designs will be adopted by teams broadly.

The same request path carries S3's performance, availability, and the simplicity of the API itself, and these properties are designed together rather than separately: an access decision that is elegant but slow is not a good design, and an API that is fast but hard to reason about is not either. A Principal Engineer in this organization is expected to shape the request path as a whole and to grow their scope over time, in S3 and beyond it.

Key job responsibilities

Authorization on the request path. Lead the architecture of how access decisions are modeled and evaluated in line with every S3 request. This spans the policy surfaces customers work with, the evaluation and caching that keep those decisions fast at S3 scale, and a model that stays clear and predictable for customers as S3 continues to grow.

A security model customers find easy to reason about. Make the secure path the straightforward one: fewer independent things for a customer to get right, a clear relationship between access to data and access to keys, and controls a customer can explain to their auditors with confidence.

Read the full description

We're looking for software developers in the Vancouver area to bring their own projects and build them using an AI-powered coding assistant. You write real code on real projects you care about. What's Not Eligible

job.name: Software Development Engineer II, Silicon Scan & Fleet Diagnostics, Machine Learning Accelerator Technology Team
job.description:
Description Annapurna Labs designs silicon and software that accelerates innovation. Customers choose us to create cloud solutions that solve challenges that were unimaginable a short time ago—even yesterday. Our custom chips, accelerators, and software stacks enable us to take on technical challenges that have never been seen before, and deliver results that help our customers change the world.

In Annapurna Labs we are at the forefront of hardware/software co-design not just in Amazon Web Services (AWS) but across the industry. The MLA Technology team is looking for candidates who are excited to write software that tests silicon itself—running structural scan (DFT) tests across a huge fleet of machine learning accelerator servers, and turning the results into insights about some of the largest chips ever built.

Do you like the idea of testing billions of transistors and finding the one that’s misbehaving? Great! Ever talked to a chip over JTAG just to see what it would say? Great! Do you read data sheets like others read the news? Great! Written a script to automate something tedious, then kept improving it just because you could? Great! Enjoy turning a mountain of raw data into a dashboard that tells a story? Great! Did this make you smile? Awesome.

Our team writes software that tests the most advanced machine learning chips in the world, at a scale and speed few systems anywhere can match. If that interests you, come join our team!

Key job responsibilities

  • Own and evolve the software that speeds up structural scan (DFT) test execution across a large fleet of ML accelerator servers
  • Design and deliver improvements to the tools and workflows used to bring new scan test patterns to production, from architecture through deployment
  • Build data analytics and dashboards that track test pattern execution across the fleet
  • Automate silicon debug and large-scale investigation workflows
  • Partner with the teams that run and validate scan testing at scale, turning their needs into maintainable, tested, reusable software
  • Mentor early-career engineers and raise the bar through design discussions and thorough, but kind, code reviews

A day in the life

As an SDE II on the team, you’ll own problems end to end—designing the solution, writing the code, testing it against real hardware, and shipping it to a fleet. One day you might be profiling scan execution to shave seconds off a test that runs across thousands of machines; another day you might be building a dashboard that shows how a new test pattern is behaving across the fleet, or automating complex silicon investigations. No software is too low level for us. No software is too high level for us. You’ll work alongside senior engineers deep in silicon test, and help early-career engineers on the team grow through your designs and code reviews.

job.name: Data Engineer, Application Software
job.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

DATA ENGINEER, APPLICATION SOFTWARE The application software team is the central nervous system of SpaceX – we create mission critical applications that are used throughout SpaceX to accelerate launch vehicle production and flight as well as systems that allow Starlink to grow into a worldwide fast, reliable Internet service. We are looking for engineers who treat fellow teammates with fairness, respect, and support.

Our team is currently creating and evolving systems to enable rapid build and reuse of Starship as well as designing the next generation manufacturing software that will be used in high throughput factories for Starlink. Other applications range from platforms that support concurrent streams of data from many always-on assets to manage the world’s largest satellite constellation to public facing systems where customers can join our Starlink network globally. We work closely with engineers throughout the company to create and update our systems with respect to crewed launches, Starship flights, changes to the Starlink network and much more.

Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, respectful, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission. You will have full ownership of challenging problems, working with a team of enthusiastic engineers with diverse perspectives to design and produce solutions that enable SpaceX to move towards our goals at a rapid pace. The success of the missions at SpaceX depends on the software that you and your team produce.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain mission-critical infrastructure, tools, processes, and custom software to objectively assess growth areas for manufacturing software
  • Automate the aggregation of metrics and detection of widespread application issues
  • Establish and maintain relationships with key third-party application/content owners
  • Lead technical investigations about chronic application-level issues
  • Build ground-based software systems that ingest, transform, and store data
  • Apply data analytics, models, and techniques to data products created by space vehicles
  • Create catalogs of data and tools that can be used by you and other teams to perform analytics
  • Fuse data from multiple sources to create usable information

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, physics, mathematics, or a STEM discipline OR 1+ years of data/software engineering experience
  • Experience in analytics, data science, or machine learning

job.description:
Description Senior Manager - Firmware and Hardware Engineering Austin, TX

  • On-site, Monday–Friday

As Sr Manager - Firmware and Hardware Engineering, you'll provide unified technical leadership across firmware, electronics, and mechanical engineering for a small, senior team building rugged, field-deployed embedded systems. You'll be the integration point between disciplines — setting the firmware architecture and system-level design standards, catching issues on the bench before they reach the field, and driving AI-first practices into how the team designs, tests, and documents its work. This is a player-coach role: you'll balance strategic, system-level leadership with hands-on technical direction, without becoming the critical path yourself.

What You'll Do

  • Provide strategic leadership across firmware, electronics, and mechanical engineering so the team ships one integrated customer-facing system — not three disciplines that only come together at the end
  • Champion an AI-first design framework across hardware, firmware, and mechanical work, embedding AI into how the team designs, reviews, and documents
  • Set and hold the firmware standard — architecture, coding practice, and field-release hygiene — while staying electronics-literate and mechanically fluent enough to direct schematic, bring-up, packaging, DFM, and contract-manufacturer decisions as system decisions
  • Require co-design and early system validation across disciplines, catching issues on the bench/HIL while designs can still change
  • Oversee execution of firmware, electronics, and mechanical programs from concept through production and field performance, as a player-coach rather than the critical-path implementer
  • Foster system-level ownership, holding engineers accountable for how their work performs in the finished product, not just their own discipline's output
  • Establish and monitor KPIs for schedule, quality, field issues, and firmware release health
  • Make and document the system-level trade-off calls between firmware, electronics, and mechanical work, guided by customer outcomes like accuracy, battery life, survivability, and installability
  • Enable your senior Firmware Test Automation engineer to own embedded test architecture (HIL, automation, CI) as a first-class system used from early bring-up onward
  • Oversee resource allocation, priorities, and budget across firmware, electronics, and mechanical work, including lab/HIL needs, contractors, and manufacturing partners
  • Maintain living system documentation — pin maps, power/thermal budgets, antenna/mechanical keep-outs, and test interfaces — visible across all disciplines
  • Lead a small multi-discipline engineering team spanning firmware, electronics, and mechanical, including a senior Firmware Test Automation engineer
  • Grow firmware and system capability through hiring, mentoring, and a high review bar; coach engineers across all disciplines to think and validate at the system level

job.name: Design Verification Engineer, Amazon Leo
job.description:
Description Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Role Be part of Amazon Leo’s sub-team responsible for defining and implementing the digital chip SOCs for communications via Low Earth Orbit satellites and Amazon gateways. This is a unique opportunity to define a groundbreaking wireless solution with few legacy constraints. The team works with customer requirements and wireless system teams to define modems, high-speed interfaces, embedded processors, and DSP solutions in latest CMOS generation technologies.

In This Role You Will

  • Implement a state of the art verification environment for IP, subsystem and SOC to facilitate testing of the DUT against reference models.
  • Develop detailed test plans and write tests, run regressions, collect coverage matrices and report progress to the program
  • Understand and debug system level communication scenarios on pre silicon and post silicon environments.
  • Work with the design and communication systems team and participate in system level verification using test benches constructed using UVM, SystemC and DPI-C
  • Develop a highly automated environment to triage regression fails and report issues to stake holders.

Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
  • 1+ year of UVM, C, System C, and scripting experience
  • 2+ years in verification preferably in communication systems

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's or Ph.D degree in Electrical / Communications Engineering
  • 2+ years in digital verification, preferably in communication systems
  • Proficiency in leveraging AI/LLM tools to accelerate verification workflows including AI-assisted test plan, test case generation, debug, human in loop coverage sign off review.
  • Familiarity with Matlab
  • Modem design verification experience
  • System C or Matlab model : development or DV integration experience
  • Familiarity with formal verification techniques
  • Strong written and verbal skills

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

job.name: Software Engineer, Starlink Network
job.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOFTWARE ENGINEER, STARLINK NETWORK At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

As a Software Engineer on the Starlink program, you will be solving challenges that improve our ability to fully utilize the hardware we have deployed. Our goal is to provide customers with the best possible satellite internet experience, often providing under-served communities with affordable, life-changing broadband internet access.

Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support. We expect our engineers to close the feedback loop between software design and real-world performance. In this role, your software will have a meaningful and measurable impact on the world.

Responsibilities

  • Develop highly reliable, real-time software designed to run on the gateways, satellites, user terminals, and switches that make up our low latency, high capacity satellite-based global network.
  • Participate in and lead architecture, design, and code reviews.
  • Develop prototypes and manage experiments to prove out key design concepts.
  • Develop tools for software development and deployment, data analysis and visualization, and test execution across multiple environments, including virtualized hardware environments, real hardware-in-the-loop simulations, and on-orbit testing.
  • Deploy reliable software, test execution, and data analysis as part of a continuous integration and release system.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, math, or science discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in software development in lieu of a degree (internship experience is applicable).
  • Development experience in C, C++, or assembly.

Preferred Skills And Experience

job.name: Software Infrastructure Engineer, Flight Software (Starlink)
job.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOFTWARE INFASTRUCTURE ENGINEER, FLIGHT SOFTWARE (STARLINK) As an infrastructure engineer on the Starlink flight software team, you will be responsible for the software that enables rapid iteration and deployment of both ground and satellite software. You will look for slowdowns in developer iteration, inefficiencies in the build system, and unnecessary interface complexity, and fix them. You will engage closely with other Starlink engineers to identify the biggest challenges they are facing and resolve them. You will be responsible for the full lifecycle of the software that you write, from conception to test to maintenance. Your relentless commitment to streamlining the flight software ecosystem will be critical to the team’s ability to rapidly deliver high quality software.

Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on an inspiring mission.

Responsibilities

  • Maintain flight code generation tooling for flight software and GNC engineers
  • Maintain core flight software features that are shared across various satellite products
  • Work closely with flight software developers to understand slow / error prone aspects of embedded software development and fix them
  • Invent tools and processes that enable fast, accurate, and easy-to-use development and operational systems
  • Engage ground software teams to understand where flight systems should be changed to simplify constellation operations

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, math, or STEM discipline OR 2+ years of experience in software development
  • Development experience in C/C++, Python, or other similar programming languages

Preferred Skills And Experience

  • Knowledge of Bazel, C++, Python, Bash
  • Experience identifying and improving performance bottlenecks, both in build systems and in embedded environments
  • Experience designing aesthetic and easy-to-use user interfaces targeted at software engineers
  • Experience designing fault tolerant, distributed, or real-time embedded systems
  • Experience with version control, continuous integration, and continuous delivery systems
  • Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements
  • Ability to communicate effectively across teams in a solution-oriented manner
  • Ability to work independently or in a team

Additional Requirements

  • Willing to work extended hours and weekends when needed

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: Pay Range Level 1: $125,000.00 - $165,000.00

Level 2: $145,000.00 - $200,000.00

job.name: Senior Software Engineer
job.description:
Overview Microsoft is a company where passionate innovators come to collaborate, envision what can be and take their careers further. This is a world of more possibilities, more innovation, more openness, and the sky is the limit thinking in a cloud-enabled world.

Microsoft’s Azure Data engineering team is leading the transformation of analytics in the world of data with products like databases, data integration, big data analytics, messaging & real-time analytics, and business intelligence. The products our portfolio include Microsoft Fabric, Azure SQL DB, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure PostgreSQL, Azure Data Factory, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure Service Bus, Azure Event Grid, and Power BI. Our mission is to build the data platform of AI, powering a new class of data-first applications and driving a data culture.

Within Microsoft Fabric, the Platform team builds and operates the unified foundation that brings together all Fabric workloads into a single, cohesive experience. The platform provides shared infrastructure, governance, security, and a unified data model that enables customers to manage their entire data estate in one place. This team is central to delivering Fabric as a complete, end-to-end intelligence platform.

Every AI agent is only as good as the data it can reach. As a Software Engineer on the OneLake team, you'll design and lead the highly scalable systems that connect AI to data across clouds, platforms and formats.

OneLake is the open data lake at the heart of Microsoft Fabric and the data foundation for the AI agents built on it. Enterprise data rarely lives in one place. Our team brings it together without copying it: with shortcuts, mirroring and catalog federation, data in Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, Databricks and on-premises systems shows up in OneLake as a single copy, ready for Spark, SQL, Power BI and AI. And the scale is real: OneLake handles over 110 billion interactions a day, more than 15 million shortcuts are in active use, and storage has grown over 300% in a year.

That creates some of the hardest distributed systems problems in the industry. How do you make data in another cloud feel local, fast and secure? How do you keep metadata in sync with many external catalogs, bridge open table formats like Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg, and enforce one consistent security model across all of it? As a Engineer, you'll drive the architecture for these answers, own critical services end to end, work directly with our largest enterprise customers, and mentor engineers around you.

If you have deep distributed systems experience and want to shape how the world's data connects to AI, join us.

We do not just value differences or different perspectives. We seek them out and invite them in so we can tap into the collective power of everyone in the company. As a result, our customers are better served.

job.name: Principal Software Engineer
job.description:
Overview What would it take for a cloud fleet to recover from failures, adapt to changing demand, and continuously improve—with engineers setting direction instead of driving every action? We are building toward that future for Microsoft 365: autonomous fleet management that turns operational intent into safe, reliable action at scale.Our team builds the compute infrastructure that makes this possible—from provisioning and resource management to deployment, recovery, and optimization. The challenge is more than adding AI to existing workflows. It is evolving the distributed systems at the heart of the fleet so that engineers and agents can understand what is happening, decide what to do, and act safely—even when systems fail and conditions change.

We are bringing together resilient infrastructure, agent-ready capabilities, and agents that put those capabilities to work: provisioning capacity, responding to events, guiding service teams, and driving hands-free recovery and optimization where safe. Our ambition is to change how M365 operates its compute fleet—with greater autonomy, higher efficiency, and resiliency built in. As a Principal Software Engineer, you will help define that future and build the foundations that make it real.

We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to provide hands-on technical leadership for compute provisioning and fleet-management infrastructure, and guide its evolution toward safe, agent-led operations.You will shape the distributed systems, control planes, and operational capabilities that manage the compute lifecycle—from provisioning and deployment to recovery and optimization. This is a core infrastructure role: success depends on sound architecture, production-quality engineering, and systems that remain reliable under scale, failures, and changing demand.You will set technical direction for modernizing these foundations and exposing them through agent-ready APIs and tools, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces and a shared fleet knowledge and action layer. You will also lead the development of long-running, event-driven, and customer-concierge agents that use these capabilities to investigate issues, coordinate work, and manage the fleet within clear safety boundaries.You will turn ambiguous infrastructure problems into durable platform capabilities, lead investments across system and team boundaries, and balance near-term delivery with long-term architectural direction. Through hands-on design and implementation, cross-team alignment, and mentorship, you will raise the bar for provisioning reliability, recovery, compute efficiency, and safe automation.

job.name: Software Development Engineer - Amazon MSK, Managed Streaming for Kafka
job.description:
Description Come build the future of data streaming with the Amazon Managed Streaming for Kafka (MSK) team!

We are seeking builders for our Amazon MSK service, a fully managed service that makes it easy for customers to build and run applications that use Apache Kafka to process streaming data. We are looking for engineers who are enthusiastic about data streaming, and are as passionate about contributing to open source as they are about solving real customers' business needs, at AWS scale.

As a member of the Amazon MSK team, you will be making contributions to the entire core data plane stack that make up the MSK service, the core Kafka platform, and stand-alone tools that make it easier for Kafka community to operate Kafka better. Upstream compatibility is a core tenet of MSK. Your code changes to the Kafka platform will be released back to open source. As a member of an AWS service that builds on top of a popular open source technology, this is a unique opportunity to work on a team that straddles both worlds – open source and Amazon-internal software. You will design and build new features, make performance improvements, identify and investigate new technologies, prototype solutions, build scalable services, and test and review changes, to deliver an exceptional customer experience.

The ideal candidate has experience designing large-scale systems supporting millions of transactions per second, enjoys solving complex software problems, and possesses analytical, design and problem-solving skills. Ideally you have an in-depth understanding of streaming data technologies like Amazon Kinesis or Apache Kafka, and experience with open-source data processing frameworks like Apache Spark, Apache Flink, or Apache Storm. Your responsibilities will include collaborating with other engineers to build a large scale AWS service, and work with senior leaders to define your team's roadmap, including identifying design and code changes needed in the underlying open source platforms.

job.name: Software Development Engineer, Provisioning - Amazon Leo
job.description:
Description Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Join our dynamic team developing satellite technology that will revolutionize provisioning software for satellite vehicles. In this critical role, you will design and implement robust software solutions that directly impact the proper functioning of satellite systems. Your expertise in problem solving and coding will be essential as you tackle complex challenges in a high-stakes environment where precision and reliability are paramount.

This position offers the unique opportunity to work with sophisticated satellite technology while developing features that ensure seamless operation of these advanced systems. You'll collaborate with a technically strong team to solve challenging problems, implement innovative solutions, and maintain critical software infrastructure that powers our satellite fleet. This role provides significant growth potential for someone with the technical aptitude and drive to advance into a Sr. Engineer position.

Key job responsibilities

Design and develop software solutions for satellite vehicle systems, implementing best practices in code organization, clarity, and error handling while balancing short and long-term technical needs.

Contribute to technical architecture decisions and software development for satellite over-the-air update capabilities, ensuring high reliability, performance, and security in a mission-critical environment.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot complex support issues, triage bugs, and implement solutions that maintain operational excellence of satellite systems.

Identify and resolve root causes of persistent problems in satellite software, making existing systems simpler while maintaining robust development practices.

Export Control Requirement Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

A day in the life

Your day begins with a team standup where you'll discuss ongoing projects and address any blockers. You'll spend time in design and implementation discussions for new satellite features, working collaboratively with your team to solve complex technical challenges. Throughout the day, you'll write and review code, triage critical bugs, and provide expert support for over-the-air update issues that require immediate attention. You'll balance proactive feature development with responsive troubleshooting, ensuring the satellite software vehicle maintains optimal performance.

job.name: Senior Performance Engineer, Efficiency Red Team
job.description:
Description Are you the kind of engineer who obsesses over performance? Does the idea of hunting for hidden waste across the world's largest infrastructure and turning those findings into hundreds of millions of dollars in freed capacity sound like the most exciting job you can imagine? If so, keep reading.

This role offers something rare. Deep technical research freedom, immediate access to the largest compute infrastructure in the world, and direct line of sight to impact that reshapes how Amazon builds and operates its infrastructure. The Efficiency Red Team has already driven billions in cumulative capacity savings, reclaimed petabytes of DRAM through automated profiling, and built GPU efficiency frameworks adopted across Amazon. And we are just getting started. The surface area of opportunity grows with every new workload, every new chip generation, and every new AI model Amazon deploys. You would be joining a team with a proven foundation and an expanding frontier.

Compute demand is rising with no sign of slowing down. The explosive growth of Generative AI has created unprecedented demand for GPUs, and the shock-waves are now constraining DRAM availability for traditional compute across the entire industry. Silicon, power, and physical space are not infinite. When capacity is constrained, efficiency becomes the new capacity. At Amazon's scale, a single efficiency pattern discovered and applied can unlock resources equivalent to building entirely new data centers. A modest reduction in memory footprint across a widely deployed library translates into millions of dollars in freed capacity. An optimization that improves response latency by milliseconds across billions of requests directly improves the experience of hundreds of millions of customers and drives business growth.

We are looking for experienced performance engineers to join a focused group whose mission is discovering and eliminating waste across every layer of the compute stack. You will work at the intersection of hardware and software, from GPU memory management in generative AI inference pipelines to DRAM allocation patterns deep inside language runtime, from storage subsystem inefficiencies to CPU scheduling behaviors at hyper-scale.

Key job responsibilities

job.name: Senior AI Model Security Researcher
job.description:

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. job.name: Sr. Software Engineer (Starlink Ground Network)
job.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK GROUND NETWORK) At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Ground Network team, you will set the technical direction for the software that plans capacity across Starlink’s global ground infrastructure for broadband and mobile: thousands of ground stations, points of presence, data centers, fiber, and associated hardware. You will own the architecture of the tools, models, and services used to forecast demand, choose deployments, and quantifying the cost to serve tens of millions of users while maintaining high reliability.

Responsibilities

  • Own the architecture of the capacity-planning process for broadband and mobile Ground Network.
  • Design and operate the forecasting and optimization engines that predict network demand, find bottlenecks, and recommend where to deploy capacity.
  • Collaborate with network engineers, operators, software teams, and external partners to close the loop between planning models and real-world performance.
  • Develop scalable data pipelines, and backend services that ingest telemetry, inventory, cost, and usage data to produce actionable capacity models and KPIs.
  • Turn network constraints (power, fiber, spectrum, site, latency, cost, etc.) into software requirements with network engineering and operations.
  • Lead design and code review. Break ambiguous problems into scoped work, set the technical bar, and raise the quality of the engineers around you.
  • Apply first-principles thinking thinking to deep-dive into capacity, cost, and scaling problems. Prototype, quantify, and make the tradeoff explicit (model fidelity vs operability vs time-to-decision).

job.name: Senior Data Performance Engineer (Oracle, dbt, Airflow)
job.description:
About The Role This role focuses on making data workflows built on dbt and Apache Airflow on Oracle run fast and reliably. Workflows migrated from Informatica must produce accurate data and perform as well as or better than the process they replace .

As a member of the performance engineering team, you will:

  • Troubleshoot. Find the root cause of slow data workflows across the database, transformation and orchestration layers.
  • Tune. Fix the bottleneck and prove the improvement with measurements, without affecting data accuracy.
  • Templatize. Turn each fix into a reusable pattern, template or guideline that other developers can apply on their own.

This is a hands-on role for an engineer who enjoys tracking down where time is lost and building solutions that keep the same problem from coming back.

What You'll Do Troubleshoot performance end to end

  • Profile slow workflows across the full execution path: scheduler, Airflow, containers, dbt and database.
  • Separate actual database processing time from framework and orchestration overhead.
  • Set performance baselines and compare results against legacy Informatica runtimes.
  • Identify root causes and explain them clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

Tune across every layer

  • Oracle: Tune SQL and PL/SQL using execution plans, SQL Monitor, AWR/ASH and wait-event analysis. Resolve optimizer, cardinality, memory and parallelism issues. Tune distributed queries across database links so processing happens where the data lives.
  • dbt: Design efficient models and materializations. Reduce parsing, compilation and run overhead, and keep large projects fast.
  • Airflow: Design efficient DAGs and tasks. Reduce scheduling and start-up delays, and make workflows reliable through sound retry, restart and failure handling.
  • Find and fix data accuracy and reliability issues uncovered during tuning.

Build reusable templates and standards

  • Turn proven fixes into reusable templates, macros, utilities and shared components.
  • Design shared changes so they can be adopted gradually and rolled back safely.
  • Create tuning playbooks, troubleshooting checklists and automated performance checks that catch regressions before release.
  • Mentor developers and review designs so new workflows perform well from the start.

Collaborate and influence

  • Present findings, options, trade-offs and measured results to developers, architects, DBAs and leadership.
  • Work with architecture and database teams to get approval for platform-level improvements.

What You Bring Required qualifications

We are seeking an experienced Data Architect/Engineer to help lead the design, implementation, and maintenance of cloud data platforms for US healthcare clients. You will own the architecture from ingestion through the Gold layer, feeding Power BI semantic models and making the data ready for Power BI Dashboards, Data Agents and AI-driven workflows.

You will work closely with our existing solution leaders and architects to oversee and guide our data engineers, BI developers, analysts and business stakeholders, and will communicate technical trade-offs clearly. This is a team lead role that requires demonstrable experience of leading/managing technical teams of varying levels of experience.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture and Data Modelling

  • Design data models including star/constellation/ snowflake schemas, and choose the right approach for each subject area based on performance, maintainability and reporting needs.
  • Design scalable, medallion-layered (Bronze / Silver / Gold) platforms on Microsoft Fabric using

OneLake, Lakehouse and Warehouse.

  • Translate business requirements into robust, well-documented data models, conformed dimensions and fact grains.

Data Engineering and Transformation

  • Review and guide ingestion and transformation built with Fabric Pipelines / Azure Data Factory, T-SQL and PySpark notebooks.
  • Implement transformation logic to meet business objectives and regulatory requirements, with

schema mapping, reconciliation and data validation to preserve data integrity and security.

  • Write and review production-grade SQL for incremental loads, slowly changing dimensions (Type 1 / Type 2), data quality checks and source-to-target reconciliation, and set SQL coding standards and code-review practices for the team.
  • Design Power BI semantic models (DAX, RLS, certified datasets) that serve dashboards and Fabric Data Agents, using Direct Lake / Import / Direct Query over Gold-layer Delta tables where appropriate.

Performance, Compliance and Documentation

  • Analyze performance and optimize across SQL, Spark and Fabric capacity (indexing, partitioning, Delta table design, capacity cost).
  • Enforce HIPAA / HITECH controls: PHI minimization, row-level security, auditing and de-identification patterns, aligned with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 practices.
  • Maintain documentation of architecture, lineage, data models and data dictionaries.

Required Skills and Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field (Master's

preferred).

• 8+ years in data architecture / database design, with 2+ years on a modern cloud data platform (Microsoft Fabric, Synapse or Databricks).

  • Expert-level SQL / T-SQL (complex query design, query optimization, stored procedures) plus advanced knowledge of Python / PySpark.

As the semiconductor industry continues its rapid growth, there is a critical demand for high-fidelity modeling and high-throughput numerical simulations to support the production of stable, high-volume chips at advanced technology nodes.

In this pivotal role, you will collaborate with industry leaders to develop groundbreaking tools that accelerate semiconductor manufacturing and device performance study at the most advanced technologies (logic 2/1.4/1.0/0.7nm and beyond, 3D NAND, 6/4F2/3D DRAM, CIS, and 3DIC packaging). Our solutions will deliver significant performance gains over conventional approaches, essential for supporting high-volume manufacturing and the agile turnaround times our customers demand.

Qualifications The ideal candidate should possess the following education and experience in one or more of following areas:

Education & Background

  • PhD (or MS + 5+ years of research/industry experience) in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, or Other Engineering (Material Science, Mechanical, etc.), with expertise in:
  • Physics-based Modeling Experience: has good intuitive to build physics-based models to solve real-world problems, capable to derive simplified models for complex systems.
  • Semiconductor Fabrication Process: unit process modules such as plasma-based dry etch, wet etch/cleaning, CVD, PVD, ALD, CMP, Epitaxy, Ion Implantation, Annealing, etc. Integration flow for advanced logic transistors (FinFET, NSFET, CFET), DRAM (COB, vertical PassGates, 3D), 3D NAND and 3DIC (TSV, RDL), CIS, LED, etc.
  • Semiconductor Device and Multi-Physics: semiconductor band-structure and carrier transport, reliability issues (BTI, TDDB, SHE, EM/IR drop), etc.
  • Semiconductor Metrology: Optical (scatterometry, ellipsometry), eBeam (SEM) based.

The Team Join the next science revolution at AWS Life Sciences Applied AI Solutions where you'll work alongside world-class scientists to build AI that transforms how therapeutics are discovered, developed, and brought to patients.

We're out to revolutionize how medicines are discovered, developed, and brought to patients powered by a new generation of AI. Our team tackles some of the hardest open problems at the intersection of frontier AI and life sciences. We apply biological foundation models large language models and agentic reasoning systems to life sciences problems then put them into the hands of customers as applications and managed services they can fine-tune tailor and deploy on their own data. The science challenges are deep: how do you design agentic systems that reason correctly over complex biological regulatory and clinical logic? How do you enable customers to tailor foundation models to their proprietary data and get better outputs with less effort? How do you adapt models to reason faithfully in high-stakes scientific and regulatory domains?

Today we're focused on two areas. In clinical trials we're building AI that automates and optimizes regulatory and clinical development workflows. In drug design our products (including Amazon Bio Discovery) accelerate discovery by giving bench scientists AI-guided protein engineering and antibody design capabilities. We combine frontier research with production-scale delivery to put breakthrough science into the hands of customers solving humanity's hardest problems.

We value scientific rigor encourage publication and support conference participation. If you want to do research that ships this is the team.

The Role We are seeking an Applied Scientist to build the models and methods behind our life sciences AI products with a primary focus on clinical trial operations and agentic reasoning. You will design train and evaluate systems that reason over complex clinical and operational logic and ship them into products customers use directly. job.description:
NVIDIA is at the forefront of the AI and robotics revolution, and NVIDIA’s robotics teams are on a mission to build the essential technology that can enable any company to become a robotics company. The Seattle Robotics Lab is uniquely positioned at the intersection of open academic research and real-world industry impact, pursuing fundamental and applied robotics research across the full robotics stack, including perception, planning, control, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, simulation, and robotics foundation models. This research aims to transform research paradigms, transfer into NVIDIA’s robotics and simulation products, and create new robotics markets for the world.

The Seattle Robotics Lab has published over 500 research papers, including many influential works that have been presented at top robotics, AI, and computer vision conferences. These works include BayesSim, cuRobo, DeXtreme, DiSECT, Factory, GraspNet, IndustReal, ITPS, LAPA, MimicGen, NeRD, RoboLab, RVT, ScheduleStream, and SHAC. (See our publications page for a complete list.) The work has deeply impacted the research community and NVIDIA products, including Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Isaac Manipulator, Isaac Lab-Arena, Cosmos, and Newton amongst others.

We are looking for PhD-candidate interns to play a pivotal role in our research efforts, providing deep, hands-on technical contributions. Our interns must have exceptional research and engineering skills, a strong research track record, and a team-first mindset. You will have the opportunity to achieve real impact, while working with some of the most creative, brilliant, and motivated researchers in the world. Interns can either be working on their own projects typically aligned with one of our internal efforts, or in some cases directly contribute to one of our efforts. Our former interns have gone on to become full-time researchers and engineers at NVIDIA and other world-leading tech companies, started academic careers at top universities, and launched frontier robotics and AI companies.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Developing algorithms, foundation models, and methods for robotic manipulation and/or loco-manipulation, for industrial, scientific, and household applications;
  • Integrating these methods into real-world robotic manipulation systems, including those consisting of collaborative robot arms, industrial robot arms, mobile manipulators, humanoids, and dexterous hands;
  • Contributing to multi-person research projects that require a diverse set of skills across the robotics and machine learning stack;

Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description: Arcadis is seeking a Digital Engineering Information Manager to lead and support the implementation of ISO 19650-compliant Information Management workflows on infrastructure and capital projects. This role involves managing the setup and governance of Common Data Environments (CDEs), ensuring control over structured data and documentation across multidisciplinary teams. Additionally, the manager will act as the Information Manager on active projects, coordinating project information requirements and digital deliverables to align with client expectations, Arcadis standards, and contractual obligations.

Role accountabilities: In this role, you will lead project-level information management activities in alignment with ISO 19650 standards, focusing on the setup and maintenance of Common Data Environments (CDEs), metadata standards, and structured data delivery processes. You will be responsible for developing project workflows, data management plans, and information architecture documentation in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams. This involves establishing, configuring, and maintaining the CDE, including managing user permissions, folder structures, naming conventions, status codes, and document lifecycle controls.

You will coordinate with project teams to define and manage Employer’s Information Requirements (EIR), Project Information Requirements (PIR), and the associated Master Information Delivery Plan (MIDP) and Task Information Delivery Plan (TIDP). Supporting BIM coordination activities is also crucial, including model federation, clash detection readiness, data validation, and COBie/asset data structuring as needed. Leading the creation of Information Management Plans, Data Management Plans, Workflow Diagrams, and Delivery Protocols will guide teams through consistent and efficient information handling.

Facilitating internal and external reviews, approvals, and information exchanges in alignment with agreed-upon workflows and project milestones will be part of your responsibilities. Monitoring CDE usage and compliance through regular audits and reporting, you will identify issues and coordinate resolutions with technical teams. You will liaise with digital leads, BIM managers, design coordinators, and client Information Management representatives to ensure data interoperability and alignment across platforms like ProjectWise, ACC, and Aconex.

job.name: GIS Data Technician
job.description:
GIS Data Technician (Temp)

Encepta | Burnaby or Victoria, BC | Temporary | Full-time

Why This Role

Before a fibre network is designed, someone has to count every home, business and unit it needs to reach. This work ensures service coverage for all properties across the network footprint. With several active projects scheduled, additional support is needed on the data processing side. For those familiar with ArcGIS Pro who enjoy refining complex address datasets, this provides a solid opportunity for short-term technical involvement.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Reviewing address points in ArcGIS Pro against municipal address data, parcel maps, satellite imagery and Street View
  • Analyzing public infrastructure (aerial, buried and conduit cable routes, poles and pedestals) to record how each building is served
  • Updating records in batches and flagging anything unclear for a field visit
  • Cleaning and analyzing address data so our field team starts every project with accurate base data
  • Running quality checks before data is delivered to our clients

Some days are a lot of careful, repetitive clicking. We won't pretend otherwise. It matters, because a missed data point can mean a home doesn't get fibre.

Who You'll Learn From

You'll work side by side with our Data team: they built the workflows, scripts and documentation you'll use, and they'll train you from day one.

Who This Is For

  • GIS students looking for winter work experience, or GIS grads and temp workers available for a short-term contract
  • Comfortable in ArcGIS Pro (QGIS experience is a plus)
  • You notice when an address on the map doesn't match the city's records, and you can't let it go
  • You can work through a large, repetitive dataset at a steady pace without losing accuracy
  • Comfortable with Excel or Google Sheets
  • Bonus: Python, SQL, or experience with municipal GIS data

Who This Isn't For

  • Anyone looking mainly for cartography, design or creative mapping work
  • Anyone who needs a lot of variety day to day

What We Offer

  • A December to February contract, with the possibility of extension
  • Hands-on training from an experienced GIS and data team
  • Real telecom infrastructure work on your resume, in a field that keeps growing

About Encepta

Founded in Victoria, headquartered in Burnaby, more than 150 people across BC, Alberta and remote locations nationally. We work with Canada's largest telecommunications carriers and are expanding into the utility and municipal infrastructure market.

Safety is fundamental to how we work. Our people are in the field, on the road and around live infrastructure every day, and our safety programme is built for that reality, not for a binder.

We are an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applications from everyone.

How to Apply

*🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot!* Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. *💻 Role* Risk Strategists at Whatnot combine data analysis, hands-on investigation, and technical problem-solving to protect our marketplace. You’ll dig into how fraud works, translate those insights into durable defenses, and help shape our risk strategy and Product and Engineering roadmap. This role requires both attention to detail and the ability to turn individual findings into broader action.

  • Investigate fraud at its source. Examine suspicious accounts, transactions, and connected activity to understand fraudsters’ modus operandi, the methods, behavioral patterns, coordination tactics, and product or process gaps they exploit.
  • Build durable defenses. Translate investigative findings into repeatable detection signals, rules, controls, and product improvements that address underlying vulnerabilities rather than individual incidents.
  • Shape strategy and priorities. Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, and Operations to define strategic direction, prioritize opportunities, and develop a roadmap that balances immediate threats with long-term protection.
  • Drive cross-functional execution. Turn complex findings into clear recommendations, build alignment on tradeoffs, and carry initiatives from problem definition through implementation and iteration.
  • Stay hands-on and technical. Use SQL, scripting, automation, and AI-assisted development tools to investigate problems and prototype solutions. Where appropriate, contribute lightweight tools and small, well-scoped application features in partnership with Engineering.
  • Measure and improve outcomes. Monitor emerging fraud trends and defense performance, balancing fraud prevention with false positives, customer experience, and operational efficiency.
  • Embed protection into new experiences. Evaluate abuse risks in new products, markets, and customer journeys, and help design safeguards before and after launch.

NeoCloud is building an AI-operated GPU cloud spanning 4 US DCs, APAC sites, and Iceland. In this role you own the IP/Ethernet infrastructure that connects that fleet — DCI, WAN, internet edge, tenant-facing networks — and you build the automation that lets the AIOps substrate express network intent as code, not as change tickets.

What You'll Own

  • EVPN-VxLAN data center fabrics for multi-tenant network isolation and workload mobility.

  • Network health, capacity, and SLA monitoring across all sites.

Feed the AIOps substrate

  • Every route policy, ACL, VRF, and peering session lives as code in the platform's config-management substrate — no config drift, no snowflakes.
  • Every BGP flap, every DCI degradation feeds the network-stability predictor.
  • Every routine change becomes a workflow the remediation actuator can execute under a maintenance window.

Why join us Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Engineering at Brex

Engineering at Brex is about building systems that scale with speed and intention. Our teams span Software, Data, Security, and IT, and operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration. We tackle hard technical problems, own our outcomes, and push for excellence at every level — from architecture to deployment. It's an environment where engineering is a craft, and builders become leaders.

What you'll do

We're building a new team within Brex's Travel group to own a defined part of our next-generation travel experience, and we're looking for the Engineering Manager to build and lead it. This is a rare from-scratch opportunity: a large strategic investment, a clean slate on team shape and roadmap, and high autonomy to define how the team works.

Part of your job is deciding what the job is. The broader Travel group covers a lot of ground, and one of your first and most important tasks is to help shape this team's mandate within that bigger picture — what it owns, where its boundaries sit, and where it should focus to have the most impact. You'll start with a small existing group and grow it through hiring into the team that carries this part of travel forward.

You'll set the technical and product direction for the team, ship a competitive customer-facing product, and build the culture from day one. Because the domain is new and the roadmap is yours to shape, product judgment matters as much as technical judgment here — you'll be making real calls about what to build and why, not just executing a handed-down plan.

Description Everyday Essentials (EE) is a $100B+ business and one of the fastest-growing categories at Amazon — the household staples, health and personal care, grocery, and beauty products hundreds of millions of customers reorder. We're reinventing how customers discover, buy, and get more value from them, and we're looking for Software Development Engineers who want to build that future.

The EE Experiences organization builds the shopping experience for the products customers come back for most. Our charter is Progressive Discovery and Monetization: helping customers find better products for their needs, complete their baskets, and improve EE business economics — and giving the world's largest consumer brands new and effective ways to reach those customers and grow with Amazon. We build a durable, profitable business at the intersection of the two, on the surfaces customers use every day.

This is a space where the hardest problems don't have off-the-shelf answers. We're not polishing a solved product — we're inventing experiences that don't exist yet, and the decisions we make now shape a business with room to grow for years. You'll build discovery and recommendation features, brand-facing advertising surfaces, and the backend services that power them. Your work moves from whiteboard to production in front of a very large customer base, with visibility all the way to senior leadership.

We're an AI-first team, and that shows up in two ways. We use AI throughout how we build software, and we expect our engineers to keep learning and applying the latest tools to move faster and raise the quality bar. AI is also at the core of what we build — the intelligence that helps customers find the right product is a modeling and engineering problem we work on hand in hand with scientists. If you're curious about AI, learn quickly, and like using it to solve real customer problems while keeping a clear head about where it helps and where it doesn't, you'll fit right in.

Key job responsibilities

Design, build, and own software end to end — from customer research through design, code, testing, deployment, and production operations.

Take on ambiguous problems where the goal is clear but the path is not, bring clarity, and deliver simple solutions that improve how customers find and buy everyday essentials.

Partner closely with scientists, product managers, and designers to turn customer and brand problems into products that ship worldwide.

Use generative AI tools and modern engineering practices to raise quality and velocity, and coach teammates on getting the most from them.

Own operational health for your services — monitor metrics, drive root-cause fixes, and keep improving the experience for customers and brand partners.

Raise the technical bar through code reviews, mentoring, and hiring for the best talent.

job.name: Sr. Software Engineer
job.description:
Job Purpose and Impact

The Senior Software Engineer - Pricefx Configuration Engineer will design, configure, develop and support scalable Pricefx solutions within Cargill's commercial technology ecosystem. In this role, you will translate pricing strategies and complex business requirements into maintainable calculation logic, data structures, workflows, integrations and user experiences that enable Cargill's go-to-market strategy. You will apply deep Pricefx and software engineering knowledge to deliver secure, resilient and high-performing solutions, bring clarity to ambiguous scenarios, and raise engineering standards across the pricing technology community.

Key Accountabilities

Pricefx Solution Configuration and Development

  • Configure and extend Pricefx capabilities using Groovy, the Pricefx Groovy API and reusable calculation logic libraries.
  • Translate commercial pricing requirements into deterministic solutions for price setting, quoting, agreements and promotions, rebates, analytics or optimization, based on the assigned product scope.
  • Design pricing calculations including cost-plus, margin and markup, discounts, price floors and ceilings, segmentation, overrides, effective dating, currency and unit-of-measure conversion, and price waterfalls.
  • Configure Pricefx data objects, including Products, Customers, extension tables, Company Parameters, Data Sources, Data Feeds, Datamarts and Rollups, using the appropriate object for each data and performance need.
  • Build user-friendly configurators, input builders, result matrices, dashboards and approval workflows with clear validation and role-appropriate access.

Architecture, Integration and Performance

  • Design scalable, flexible and maintainable Pricefx solutions and create clear architecture, data mapping, interface and solution design documentation.
  • Define integrations and workflows between Pricefx and enterprise platforms such as SAP, Salesforce and other master-data, ERP, CRM or analytics systems.
  • Develop and troubleshoot REST API and event-driven integrations using JSON, authentication, pagination, retries, idempotency and reliable error handling; collaborate with Integration Engineers on IntegrationManager solutions when required.
  • Optimize large-volume calculations and queries through sound SQL, QueryAPI and DatamartContext usage, efficient joins and filters, batching, caching and avoidance of row-by-row or repetitive data access.
  • Apply security-by-design practices, including least-privilege access, user groups, roles, data entitlements, secure configuration and appropriate handling of sensitive information.

Engineering Delivery and Technical Leadership

job.name: Lead Agentic Security Engineer
job.description:
SECURITY ENGINEERING AT INVESTCLOUD At InvestCloud, we are building an intelligent security response capability that determines what to fix first based on the actual risk to our clients and business, not a scanner's native severity.

Traditional vulnerability management produces disconnected findings and long backlogs. It often misses whether vulnerable code is deployed, reachable by an attacker, connected to a critical service, capable of lateral movement, or already being exploited. We are solving that problem by combining threat intelligence, runtime and deployment evidence, configuration management data, attack path analysis, business criticality, and validation results.

The platform will ingest findings from infrastructure, cloud, application, software supply chain, secrets, containers, infrastructure as code, and adversarial testing. It will reconcile them to a canonical asset and service model, deduplicate them into unique exposures, and rank the remediation actions that remove the most risk.

The product is being built in Python on AWS with source-controlled connectors, deterministic policy code, an AI reasoning layer, human approval gates, complete audit evidence, and closed-loop validation. Large language models (LLMs) can correlate evidence, recommend remediation, and explain decisions. They do not calculate the authoritative priority score.

This is not another scanner or dashboard. It is a security decision and remediation platform that must answer one question reliably: what is the single next action that will remove the most material risk, why is it first, who owns it, and how will we verify the risk is gone? Every engineer on this team will build production software, operate what they build, and own the product after the initial consultant implementation.

THE ROLE As our Agentic Security Engineer, you will serve as the principal software architect for the harness and own the AI reasoning layer that turns prioritized exposures into evidence-grounded remediation options, residual risk analysis, and clear explanations.

You will ensure the product operates as a reliable system, not an AI demonstration. The deterministic policy engine owns the authoritative score. The LLM layer retrieves evidence, correlates likely root causes, evaluates mitigation choices, produces structured recommendations, and knows when to abstain or require a human. You will also set engineering standards across Python services, APIs, data contracts, the evaluation framework, observability, and the operator experience.

What You Will Own

Building on the original Alexa, it uses generative AI to deliver a more conversational, personalised, and effective experience. Build AI safety systems that protect millions of Alexa customers every day. Your innovations won't just improve Alexa+; they'll fundamentally shape how it learns, evolves, and earns customer trust. As Alexa+ continues to delight customers, your work ensures it becomes more trustworthy, safer, and deeply aligned with customer needs and expectations.

Your work directly protects customer trust at Amazon's scale. Every innovation you create—from novel safety mechanisms to sophisticated evaluation techniques—shapes how millions of people interact with AI confidently. You're not just building products; you're defining industry standards for responsible AI.

This is frontier research with immediate real-world impact. You'll tackle problems that require innovative solutions: training models that remain truthful and grounded across diverse contexts, building reward models that capture the nuanced spectrum of human values across cultures and languages, and creating automated systems that continuously discover and address potential issues before customers encounter them. What We're Looking For

job.name: SENIOR, DATA SCIENTIST
job.description:
About The Role Merchandising Data Science builds the systems — both automated decision engines and decision support systems — that drive high-stakes merchandising decisions: how we select and curate items, manage space, plan and allocate inventory, flow inventory through the network, decide what and how much to buy, read the competitive landscape, and price. As a Staff Data Scientist, you own a single, hard problem end-to-end — not an abstract domain, but a specific question like "how do we estimate price elasticities better?", "how do we reduce forecast error for seasonal items a year out?", or "how do we incorporate all constraints at DC outbound so the planned flow can actually be executed, exceptions and all?" Depending on the problem, the answer is a system that decides automatically, or one that gives a merchant or planner the right recommendation, tradeoff, and evidence to decide well. You take the problem from a rough business question to a precise formulation to a production system, and you make sure it keeps getting better even on the days you're not in the room. You are an individual contributor with no direct reports — your leverage comes from raising the judgment and standards of the people working alongside you on that problem, not from personal output alone.

What you'll do

Own one hard, well-defined problem end-to-end — e.g., "how do we estimate price elasticities better?" or "how do we reduce forecast error for seasonal items a year out?" — from rough business question to precise formulation to production system.

Define what a good answer looks like: decision variables or recommendation logic, objective function, constraints, fallback behavior, and measurable success criteria.

Decide whether the problem calls for a fully automated decision engine or a decision support system that augments a human decision-maker, and design accordingly.

Choose and implement the right solution approach — optimization, heuristics, simulation, forecasting, causal/statistical inference, or a hybrid — and defend the choice on evidence.

Build the production system, not a prototype, integrating with the merchandising, planning, and platform systems it depends on.

Establish patterns, methods, and quality standards on this problem that other people working on it (Senior DS, engineers) adopt and extend.

Define the metrics and run the experiments that prove the answer is actually better — this may be estimation accuracy, forecast error, executability of a plan, margin, sell-through, or trust/adoption of a recommendation, depending on the problem.

Create mechanisms — documentation, reusable components, decision frameworks — so continued progress on the problem does not depend on you personally.

Proactively surface the next-most-important version of the problem before being asked (e.g., once elasticity estimation improves for core items, is the next gap seasonal or new items?).

Read the full description

Description The Annapurna Labs team at Amazon builds AWS Neuron, the software development kit used to accelerate deep learning and GenAI workloads on Amazon’s custom machine learning accelerators, Inferentia and Trainium.

The AWS Neuron SDK, developed by the Annapurna Labs team at AWS, is the backbone for accelerating deep learning and GenAI workloads on Amazon's Inferentia and Trainium ML accelerators. This comprehensive toolkit includes an ML compiler, runtime, and application framework that seamlessly integrates with popular ML frameworks like PyTorch and JAX enabling unparalleled ML inference and training performance.
