Working across the stack from PyTorch till the hardware-software boundary, our engineers build systematic infrastructure, innovate new methods and create high-performance kernels for ML functions, ensuring every compute unit is fine tuned for optimal performance for our customers' demanding workloads. We combine deep hardware knowledge with ML expertise to push the boundaries of what's possible in AI acceleration.

As part of the broader Neuron organization, our team works across multiple technology layers - from frameworks and kernels and collaborate with compiler to runtime and collectives. We not only optimize current performance but also contribute to future architecture designs, working closely with customers to enable their models and ensure optimal performance. This role offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of machine learning, high-performance computing, and distributed architectures, where you'll help shape the future of AI acceleration technology

You will architect and implement business critical features, and mentor a brilliant team of experienced engineers. We operate in spaces that are very large, yet our teams remain small and agile. There is no blueprint. We're inventing. We're experimenting. It is a very unique learning culture. The team works closely with customers on their model enablement, providing direct support and optimization expertise to ensure their machine learning workloads achieve optimal performance on AWS ML accelerators. The team collaborates with open source ecosystems to provide seamless integration and bring peak performance at scale for customers and developers.

job.name: Applied Scientist, AVM Builder Enablement
job.description:
Description Applied Scientists on the AWS Vulnerability Management (AVM) Builder Enablement team use program analysis, machine learning and generative AI for managing vulnerabilities and securing the software supply chain across AWS. Our scope covers the third-party open-source packages, language ecosystems, operating systems and kernels that AWS services are built on. Our goal is to take builders out of the remediation loop. When a vulnerability is disclosed or a package is compromised, our systems work out whether it actually affects AWS, generate the fix, check that it's safe and ship it at AWS scale, with one click or no clicks at all.

New vulnerabilities are disclosed every day in the software AWS depends on, and finding and fixing them by hand doesn't scale. We build systems that detect vulnerabilities and work out whether the vulnerable code can actually be reached and exploited in a given service. They rank issues by real risk rather than raw severity scores, then fix them automatically. That can mean upgrading dependencies across ecosystems like Java, Python, JavaScript, Go and Rust, fixing breaking API changes, backporting patches, or patching operating systems and kernels across the fleet. Just as important, we check that each fix is correct and safe, so it can merge with little or no human review.

Beyond known vulnerabilities, we protect the integrity of the software supply chain itself. Modern software is assembled more than it is written, and every dependency is a potential way in for attackers. Securing it means knowing what's in our software, where it came from and whether it can be trusted. Our work here includes building and analyzing software bills of materials (SBOMs), verifying package provenance and build integrity, and detecting malicious or compromised packages before they reach production.

Our methods range from static and dynamic program analysis to LLM-based agents for code repair and upgrades. This is a chance to shape a fast-growing area that directly affects the security of AWS and its customers. You'll apply your technical depth in a fast-moving environment, and your work will reach thousands of AWS builders and services.

A Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDEs write production-grade software and own outcomes end-to-end, from prototype through enterprise-scale deployment, combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes. job.name: Sr. Staff IAM Architect
job.description:
About OpenLoop OpenLoop was co-founded by CEO, Dr. Jon Lensing, and COO, Christian Williams, with the vision to bring care anywhere. Our telehealth support solutions are thoughtfully designed to streamline and simplify go-to-market care delivery for companies offering meaningful virtual support to patients across an expansive array of specialties, in all 50 states.

About The Role OpenLoop’s mission is to bring care anywhere by powering telehealth solutions at scale. Our Identity and Access Management team governs how every person, partner, and system proves who they are and what they can reach.

We are hiring a Sr. Staff IAM Architect to be the design authority for identity across the company: workforce, non-employee, customer, partner, non-human, and AI agent.

That last one is not filler. Service accounts and AI agents are on track to outnumber the people we govern, and very few companies have a real architecture for them yet. You would own ours.

The platforms are chosen and in flight. Okta is our workforce IdP. SailPoint ISC and NERM are deploying for identity governance and non-employee records. Britive is deploying for privileged just-in-time access. Auth0 is our customer identity platform, procured with machine-to-machine flows in production and the interactive login experience in active build. iam-ops-hub, our identity posture and remediation platform, is built in house and deployed. What we do not have is a single design authority tying them together. Architecture currently gets decided project by project, under delivery pressure. This role exists to change that.

This is a hands-on architecture role, and we mean that concretely. Expect to write Auth0 Actions, Okta Workflows, and Terraform, and to query the posture warehouse yourself. Identity controls here carry HIPAA, HITRUST, and SOC 2 weight. The person who does well in this role is comfortable in ambiguity, writes decisions down, and can explain a design tradeoff to a staff engineer and to a CISO in the same week.

What You’ll Do

job.name: AWS Architect
job.description:
AWS Architect

Workplace type: Toronto, ON

Fulltime – Onsite

Requirement: Immediate

Key Responsibilities

1. AWS Architecture Design & Implementation

  • Design & Support: Architect and amend cloud infrastructure with a focus on high availability, fault tolerance, and workload optimization.
  • Core Networking: Administer and optimize advanced AWS networking, including VPCs, Transit Gateway (TGW), VPNs, VPC Endpoints, PrivateLink, Peering, Route Tables, and NACLs.
  • Traffic Management: Configure and manage Application Load Balancers (ALB) and Network Load Balancers (NLB)
  • IP Management: Handle VPC subnetting and CIDR block/mask administration.

2. Disaster Recovery (DR) & Business Continuity

  • DR Strategy: Design and implement robust DR solutions utilizing AWS native services to meet strict business RTO and RPO objectives.
  • Replication & Backup: Leverage AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (EDR), AWS Backup, S3 Multi-Region Access Points (MRAP), and RDS/Redshift cross-region replication.
  • Cross-Region Operations: Lead upcoming DR testing initiatives to ensure infrastructure and applications seamlessly restore in us-east-1 within established RTOs.

3. Security, Governance & Identity Management

  • Access Control: Manage IAM, AWS Identity Center, Control Tower, and AWS Landing Zone environments.
  • Data Protection: Utilize multi-region AWS Custom KMS keys for data encryption.
  • Compliance & Auditing: Analyze AWS Security Hub findings, drive remediation efforts, and enforce compliance using AWS Config and strict resource tagging policies.

4. DevOps, Automation & CI/CD

  • Infrastructure as Code (IaaC): Provision and manage infrastructure using Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Pipeline Management: Set up and maintain CI/CD pipelines using GitLab (or similar Git tools) and configure GitLab Runners.
  • Configuration Management: Utilize Ansible for automated configuration and deployment.
  • Repository Governance: Administer Git branching strategies, including permissions, code promotion, and pull request reviews.

5. System Administration & Operations

  • OS Support: Perform system administration, troubleshooting, and resource provisioning across both Windows and Linux environments.
  • Patching & Vulnerability: Conduct routine vulnerability assessments and manage monthly system patching cycles.
  • Data & AI Provisioning: Spin up and manage Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and standard compute instances.
  • L1 Troubleshooting: Support basic troubleshooting for AWS Lambda functions and AWS Glue data jobs.

6. Financial & Performance Optimization

  • Cost Optimization: Analyze AWS Cost Optimizer data to identify savings opportunities.
  • Executive Reporting: Deliver weekly and monthly billing and utilization reports for HCCA management.
  • Monitoring & Observability: Build custom CloudWatch Dashboards.

job.name: Information Technology Auditor
job.description:
Job Description

Position Title: Auditor – IT Security (Staff Accountant / Staff Consultant), Contract

Location: North York, Canada

Category: Mid- Senior, Contract - 3 months

Industry: Chartered Professional Accountants / IT Security & Audit

About the Opportunity

We are a Canada-based Chartered Professional Accounting and Advisory firm, expanding our operations globally. We are seeking talented professionals to join our team . This is an exciting opportunity to work with a fast-growing firm, gain exposure to international clients, and develop expertise across multiple areas of IT security, audit, and advisory.

Key Responsibilities

IT Security Assessment

  • Analyze and assess client IT infrastructure to evaluate the design and operational effectiveness of controls.
  • Conduct or support risk assessments to identify information security vulnerabilities.
  • Perform vulnerability assessments and penetration testing using tools such as Kali, Nessus, Parrot, etc.
  • Evaluate antivirus programs, firewalls, password protection, and network security controls.
  • Inspect networks and hardware for security gaps and recommend remediation measures.
  • Provide expert input on security architecture concepts and requirements.
  • Draft IT security policies, procedures, and guidelines for clients.
  • Deliver security awareness training sessions as required.

IT Audit

  • Execute IT audits in the areas of infrastructure, processes, applications, operations, security, and emerging technologies.
  • Apply IT audit and control frameworks (COBIT, NIST, ISO 27001, PCI, SOC1, SOC2, CSAE 3416, etc.).
  • Prepare risk and control matrices, perform walkthroughs, and document processes and controls.
  • Identify compliance gaps, process inefficiencies, and operational issues.
  • Develop clear and comprehensive audit work papers, memos, and reports.
  • Conduct assurance engagements including planning, scoping, risk assessments, and audit program execution.
  • Finalize audit files and reports independently with minimal supervision.
  • Provide advisory services to clients on IT risk, controls, and governance.

Internal Control Testing

  • Design and perform tests of controls (manual and automated) to evaluate adequacy and effectiveness.
  • Conduct walkthroughs of business and IT processes to identify control gaps.
  • Prepare and maintain risk & control matrices (RCM).
  • Identify non-compliance with internal control requirements and highlight weaknesses.
  • Document internal control frameworks, policies, and processes for clients.
  • Test the design and operating effectiveness of entity-level, application, and IT general controls (ITGC).
  • Prepare working papers clearly linking test results to audit findings.
  • Recommend remediation plans to strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with regulatory

SOC 1, SOC 2, and SOX Audits

Position Overview

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Microsoft Purview & SharePoint Specialist to play a key role in managing, optimizing and supporting the organization's Microsoft 365 environment, with a primary focus on Microsoft Purview, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), information protection and SharePoint Online governance. The successful candidate will bring strong hands-on technical expertise in administering and troubleshooting Microsoft Purview, configuring and tuning DLP policies, managing sensitivity labels and data classifications, and improving SharePoint Online site health and governance. Microsoft Purview & Information Protection

  • Manage, administer and troubleshoot the Microsoft Purview platform, ensuring effective data protection and compliance controls.
  • Configure, maintain and optimize Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies across the Microsoft 365 environment.
  • Support Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) and broader Microsoft 365 data-security initiatives.
  • Configure and manage sensitivity labels, information protection policies and data classification rules.
  • Work directly with business data stewards and data owners to review, refine and tune policies and classification requirements.
  • Investigate DLP alerts, false positives, policy conflicts and security control gaps, implementing appropriate corrective actions.
  • Improve the accuracy, effectiveness and operational performance of data protection policies.
  • Support auditing, alerting, reporting and ongoing policy monitoring.
  • Document configurations, policy changes, procedures and information governance standards.

job.description:
Required As a Public Key Infrastructure and Cryptography Expert, you play a key role in the implementation, administration, operation, and evolution of a new internal public key infrastructure (PKI) at Desjardins. You contribute to the ongoing development of cryptographic services by deploying and managing a robust, resilient and secure PKI that supports the organization’s certification authorities, cryptographic keys and digital certificates. You leverage your experience in deploying and administering enterprise PKIs to ensure their availability, security and integration into technology environments, while supporting the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). We’re looking for someone who excels at diagnosing and resolving complex technical incidents affecting PKI services. You’re analytical, autonomous and diligent, and collaborate effectively with a range of technology teams. More specifically, you will be required to :

  • Participate in the technical design, installation, configuration and release to production of a new internal PKI
  • Ensure the daily administration, operation, maintenance and development of the internal PKI, including its hardware, software and cryptographic components
  • Deploy, configure and administer root and issuing certification authorities, registration authorities, and certificate validation and revocation services (CRL and OCSP)
  • Administer the hardware security modules (HSMs) and protect, back up and manage the certification authorities’ cryptographic keys
  • Ensure the availability, monitoring, performance and resilience of PKI services, including through incident, patch, upgrade and recovery management
  • Integrate and maintain PKI services in Windows, Linux, Active Directory, cloud environments and certificate management (CMS/CLM) platforms
  • Support the migration of existing certification authorities and certificates to the new infrastructure while maintaining the required chains of trust
  • Work with architecture, infrastructure, cybersecurity and development teams to ensure the integration and evolution of PKI services
  • Contribute to preparing the infrastructure for new cryptographic technologies, including post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility

What we offer\*

  • Competitive salary and annual bonus
  • 4 weeks of flexible vacation starting in the first year
  • Defined benefit pension plan that provides predictable, stable income throughout retirement
  • Group insurance including telemedicine
  • Reimbursement of health and wellness expenses and telework equipment
  • Benefits apply based on eligibility criteria.

À titre d’expert(e) en infrastructure à clés publiques (PKI), Cryptographie, vous jouez un rôle clé dans la mise en place, l’administration, l’exploitation et l’évolution d’une nouvelle infrastructure PKI interne au sein du Mouvement Desjardins. Vous contribuez à la modernisation des services cryptographiques en assurant le déploiement et la gestion opérationnels d’une infrastructure PKI robuste, résiliente et sécuritaire, permettant de gérer les autorités de certification, les clés cryptographiques et les certificats numériques de l’organisation. Vous mettez à profit votre expérience dans le déploiement et l’administration d’infrastructures PKI d’entreprise afin d’assurer leur disponibilité, leur sécurité, leur intégration aux environnements technologiques et leur évolution vers la cryptographie post-quantique (PQC). Nous sommes à la recherche d’une personne possédant une forte capacité à diagnostiquer et à résoudre des incidents techniques complexes affectant les services PKI, reconnue pour son esprit d’analyse, son autonomie, sa rigueur et sa capacité à collaborer efficacement avec diverses équipes technologiques. Plus spécifiquement, vous serez amené(e) à :

  • Participer à la conception technique, à l’installation, à la configuration et à la mise en production d’une nouvelle infrastructure PKI interne.
  • Assurer l’administration quotidienne, l’exploitation, la maintenance et l’évolution de l’infrastructure PKI interne, incluant ses composantes matérielles, logicielles et cryptographiques.
  • Déployer, configurer et administrer les autorités de certification racines et émettrices (Root CA, Issuing CA), les autorités d’enregistrement (RA) et les services de validation et de révocation (CRL, OCSP).
  • Administrer les HSM et assurer la protection, la sauvegarde et la gestion des clés cryptographiques des autorités de certification.
  • Assurer la disponibilité, la surveillance, la performance et la résilience des services PKI, notamment par la gestion des incidents, des correctifs, des mises à niveau et des mécanismes de reprise.
  • Intégrer et maintenir les services PKI dans les environnements Windows, Linux, Active Directory, infonuagiques et les plateformes de gestion des certificats (CMS/CLM).
  • Participer à la migration des autorités de certification, des certificats et des chaînes de confiance existantes vers la nouvelle infrastructure.
  • Collaborer avec les équipes d’architecture, d’infrastructure, de cybersécurité et de développement afin d’assurer l’intégration et l’évolution des services PKI.

job.name: Security Specialist
job.description:
Company Description Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. We believe diverse perspectives help both players and teams thrive. If you’re passionate about innovation and pushing entertainment boundaries, join our journey and help create the unknown!

Job Description As an Application Security Specialist at Ubisoft Montréal, you will join our Application and Platform Security team within the Security Risk Management (SRM) department.

Working within engineering teams across Ubisoft, you’ll partner with developers, infrastructure specialists, and technical stakeholders to strengthen the security of applications, services, platforms, and development environments. You’ll address systemic security weaknesses, improve existing technical architecture, and help teams adopt secure-by-default practices.

This hands-on role combines technical expertise with self-directed work and collaboration. You’ll help shape engineering priorities and deliver lasting security improvements across teams without direct organizational authority.

What You’ll Do

  • Partner with engineering teams as an embedded security specialist, trusted technical partner, and primary security contact for assigned environments and services.
  • Identify, investigate, and remediate systemic security weaknesses across applications, services, infrastructure, and development environments.
  • Implement structural security improvements to address recurring vulnerabilities, reduce technical risks, and strengthen existing systems by design.
  • Improve secure development and delivery workflows, including continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD) pipelines, build processes, authentication, authorization, secrets management, and infrastructure configurations.

Dentsply Sirona is the world’s largest manufacturer of professional dental products and technologies, with over a century of innovation and service to the dental industry and patients worldwide. Dentsply Sirona develops, manufactures, and markets a comprehensive solutions offering including dental and oral health products as well as other consumable medical devices under a strong portfolio of world class brands.

Dentsply Sirona is looking for a Senior Security Engineer, PKI & Network Edge professional to join our team This is a senior-level individual contributer position within Dentsply Sirona's Security Architecture and Engineering organization.

This role is the enterprise technical owner for the security of three foundational internet-facing services: Domain Name System (DNS), digital certificates and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and Web Application Firewall (WAF). These services define and protect the boundary between Dentsply Sirona and the public internet, and this engineer is accountable for keeping that boundary trustworthy, available, and resilient.

As the build-and-govern owner, the role designs, selects, and stands up these capabilities, then sets the standards and guardrails by which they run. It owns the design, engineering, and continuous improvement of controls across DNS resolution and domain governance, the full certificate lifecycle and enterprise PKI, and web application and edge protection. Day-to-day operation transitions to a partner Infrastructure run-and-maintain function, while this role retains design authority, standards, and risk governance. The engineer partners closely with Infrastructure and Operations, Network Engineering, Cloud Engineering, Product Security, Application Development, and Security Operations to reduce attack surface, prevent outages caused by expired or misissued certificates, and ensure web-facing assets are protected against modern application-layer threats.

Operating with minimal direction, the Senior Engineer leads complex initiatives end to end, acts as the senior escalation point for DNS, certificate, and WAF issues, and serves as a trusted advisor to both engineering teams and security leadership. The role also provides senior-level support to Security Operations by ensuring high-quality telemetry and detection coverage across DNS, certificate, and WAF data sources.

job.description:
We are seeking an experienced Cyber Security Engineer to support a highly secure cloud and network infrastructure environment. This role focuses on security, reliability, automation, observability, and operational excellence for mission-critical services.

Important Requirements

  • Canadian Citizenship is mandatory due to the security requirements of the end client.
  • Candidates must be eligible to obtain a Government of Canada Top Secret Security Clearance.

Key Responsibilities

As a Cyber Security Engineer, you will:

  • Maintain and enhance the reliability, scalability, performance, and security of cloud infrastructure and services.

  • Automate infrastructure and operational processes using scripting and Infrastructure as Code (IaC).

  • Assist with the implementation and operation of Zero Trust architectures, secure access solutions, and other cybersecurity technologies.

Required Qualifications

  • Routing and Switching
  • Hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as:
  • AWS

  • Experience supporting large-scale production environments.

  • Experience with Zero Trust architectures , secure access technologies, and modern cybersecurity frameworks.
  • Experience working in highly regulated or government environments.

job.name: Senior Security Engineer, Detection Engineering
job.description:
NVIDIA Security is seeking a Senior Detection Engineer to join the Detection and Automation Engineering team. On this team, we build reliable detection coverage that helps responders identify real threats quickly, reduce unnecessary noise, and protect NVIDIA's enterprise, cloud, developer, AI, and production environments. Do you enjoy turning sophisticated security signals into detections responders can trust? Can you read an incident write-up, a red-team result, or an unusual authentication pattern and decide what is worth alerting on? We want someone who can move from hypothesis to tested production content and explain the tradeoffs clearly.

We work closely with incident response, threat intelligence, security operations, cloud security, and engineering teams. We protect enterprise, cloud, identity, endpoint, collaboration, developer, AI, and production environments. We care about detections that are explainable, measured, maintainable, and useful during real investigations.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build and tune high-confidence detections across platforms such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel / Defender, CrowdStrike, cloud-native logs, identity telemetry, endpoint data, SaaS platforms, and developer systems.
  • Translate incidents, hunts, threat intelligence, red-team findings, and vulnerability context into detection logic we can test and operate.
  • Investigate real telemetry before we alert on it, including field behavior, timing, joins, baselines, and the false positives a responder will actually see.
  • Drive the full detection lifecycle: design, query development, validation, peer review, documentation, deployment, tuning, monitoring, and retirement.
  • Strengthen detection-as-code workflows, including test data, quality checks, metadata, rollout safety, coverage tracking, and detection health reporting.
  • Partner with responders to cut noise, add useful context, improve severity decisions, and build follow-up detections after investigations.
  • Shape logging, normalization, enrichment, and retention requirements when the telemetry we need is missing or hard to use.
  • Coach analysts and engineers through design reviews, query reviews, and clear guidance on what makes a detection credible.

What We Need To See

job.name: Software Engineer, S3 Discovery
job.description:
Description Managing trillions of objects in storage, retrieving them in sub-x ms, building software that deploys to tens of thousands of hosts, achieving 99.999999999% (you didn’t read that wrong, that’s 11 nines!) durability. These are just a few of the numbers that give you a sense of the scale of the exciting problems you will find every day working in Simple Storage Service (S3). Amazon S3 powers businesses across e globe that make the lives of consumers better daily. Whether its electronic content delivered to your home, technology that betters your remote working experience, allows you to plan travel to exotic places or simply get stuff delivered to your home.

As a Software Development Engineer in the S3 Distribution Plane team, you will deliver services at scale to delight our customers and support the routing of billions of requests per minute to S3’s globally distributed server fleet. You will have the opportunity to design and develop systems and services in the domains of DNS, IP and Network Connectivity, TLS Certificates, VPC Endpoints and Private Connectivity. You will work alongside engineers and leaders who obsess about operations, performance, availability, scalability, and durability of customer data. Our services run at scale worldwide and as a member of this team, you will have the opportunity to ship code often, and see the impact your code has on a wide range of S3 customers.

Day to day you will be responsible for designing, delivering and maintaining the operational health of our services, maintaining our build & release systems, and ensuring maximum up-time for our developers and customers. You will provide coaching and mentoring for junior engineers and participate in design reviews, operations meetings and leadership discussions. You will partner with service teams across AWS to build ground-breaking DNS, networking and security solutions in code for S3. You will work closely with the likes of Amazon Route 53, AWS EC2 and AWS Networking to achieve the combined goals of AWS and S3. You will transcend a single organization in order to deliver solutions that require broader integration across AWS. For this reason, thinking big and thinking outside of S3 is one of the key tenets you will have to practise on a daily basis.

Responsibilities As a Software Development Engineer in our team, you are constantly striving to raise our operational bar and improve our infrastructure, enabling our teams to move faster. Your responsibilities will include:

Developing tools to streamline operations as we scale to reduce operational load and improve our overall operational posture. Influencing & driving operational excellence and best practices within the organization.

Identifying ways to increase the automate and improve our test infrastructure and make our CI/CD more robust and flexible.

job.name: Software Development Engineer — Storage
job.description:
Description We're seeking a Sr.Software Development Engineer with deep storage expertise to architect, build, and operate the high-performance storage infrastructure that accelerates silicon development at Annapurna Labs. In this role, you'll own the storage platforms—spanning Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, FSx for Lustre, and S3—that enable chip design teams to iterate faster, run regressions more efficiently, and bring transformative custom silicon to market.

Key job responsibilities

You will design, deploy, and operate high-performance storage platforms—Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP (Gen1/Gen2) and FSx for Lustre—optimized for EDA and HPC workloads. This includes managing NFS exports, ONTAP SVMs, intelligent tiering (FabricPool), snapshot policies, SnapMirror replication, and quota enforcement across multi-tenant environments. You'll deploy all storage infrastructure using AWS CDK, architect cross-VPC and multi-account solutions via Transit Gateway and Route 53 private hosted zones, enable EFA for high-throughput Lustre access, and manage data synchronization using DataSync and S3 integrations. You'll build a Storage as a Service platform with self-service provisioning, defined SLOs, cost attribution, and automated lifecycle management that enables teams to consume storage without deep specialization.

You will build monitoring and observability for storage health, utilization, and cost trends, and establish incident response processes for storage-related failures. You'll continuously evaluate and adopt new AWS storage features—Gen2 scale-out, NVMe-over-TCP, enhanced backup performance—to keep the platform at the leading edge. You'll profile I/O patterns across EDA workloads, tune file system configurations for optimal performance, and partner with silicon design and verification teams to proactively scale capacity and mentor others on storage best practices.

A day in the life

You might start your day reviewing storage utilization dashboards and tiering efficiency reports, identifying file systems approaching capacity thresholds or workloads that would benefit from tier migration. Mid-morning, you could be collaborating with a verification team to provision a new FSx for Lustre file system optimized for their regression suite—sizing it based on their I/O profiles, enabling EFA access, and deploying it through your CDK pipeline.

In the afternoon, you might be building the next iteration of your Storage as a Service platform—adding automated quota enforcement for a new team onboarding, implementing a snapshot policy that aligns with their project milestones, or extending cross-VPC access to a new account. You'll review pull requests for CDK constructs, investigate a DataSync job that stalled, and discuss FSx ONTAP Gen2 migration plans with your team.

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Overview: A chip isn't a product until it's a working system. These teams cover both ends of that: getting silicon to boot and validate correctly,building the board, power, mechanical, thermal, packaging and IO around it. You submit one application, you have one recruiter screen - then we match you to the specific team below and location that fits best.

  • Systems & Silicon Validation: Post-silicon testing of physical chips and integrated systems to ensure they meet all functional, electrical, and performance specs.
  • System Software: Development of foundational software, including firmware, drivers, and operating systems, that directly controls and interfaces with hardware.
  • System Design: The process of defining, integrating, and mapping out hardware components such as PCBs, software modules, and interfaces into a complete product blueprint.
  • System Architecture: Define the high-level structural framework, interfaces, and data-flow pathways between the CPU, memory, and peripherals.
  • Packaging: A package is what is placed between the silicon and the board; and its design requires detailed electrical, electromagnetic, and mechanical simulations and analysis.

This role is on-site based out of Toronto, Ontario or Vancouver, British Columbia.

Who You Are

  • Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in EE, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Mechanical Engineering
  • Coursework or projects in embedded systems, microwave and signal integrity, board-level design, or thermal/mechanical engineering using low-level programming (C/C++, Python) or hardware design and/or simulation tools (e.g., CAD, FEA, Verilog).
  • Problem solver with strong foundational knowledge in one of these areas: electrical engineering, digital logic, computer architecture, or thermal/mechanical.
  • Curious learner who is passionate about the intersection of software, silicon architecture, and the physical constraints of chip packaging and printed circuit boards (PCBs).

Your work will help lab leadership make faster priority calls and keep our design-team customers supported on the most urgent, actionable work.

We do this through the delivery of secure cloud, AI, software and digital workplace solutions that enable agility, innovation and growth.

With a highly engaged, high-performing team, we are certified as a Great Place to Work® in both Canada and the United States, and have been recognized as a Best Workplace in Canada for more than 20 years. As part of WWT, we connect customers to the global scale, advanced innovation, world-class partnerships, and deep expertise of a leader in AI and digital transformation. The Engineer, Low-Code guides clients on employing Power Platform tools — Copilot Studio, Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Power Pages, and AI Builder, Azure AI — to solve business needs, develops enterprise-grade solutions following best practices, and participates in the full client delivery lifecycle from discovery through deployment. This role contributes to both commercial and government enterprise clients, helping them improve business results through modernization of processes, applications, and approaches to real-world business problems. This role reports to a Sr Engineer, Low-Code, Supervisor, AI and Apps, or Manager, AI and Apps.

job.name: Sharepoint Developer
job.description:
Role: SharePoint Developer

Location: Vancouver, BC

Type: Fulltime

"Role Overview

The person will work with business analysts, architects, technical leads and end users to understand requirements, design SharePoint based solutions, implement customizations and support delivery across the application lifecycle. The role requires strong hands-on development experience in SharePoint Online, Office 365, SPFx and modern web technologies, along with the ability to troubleshoot, document and support collaboration platform solutions.

Key Accountabilities

  • Understand business requirements as per the BRD and translate them into technical design and implementation tasks.
  • Design, develop and enhance enterprise collaboration solutions using SharePoint Online, Office 365 and Microsoft 365 services.
  • Build custom SharePoint Framework (SPFx) web parts, extensions and reusable components using TypeScript, React and modern development practices.
  • Develop SharePoint lists, libraries, pages, content types, permission models, workflows and integration components as per project standards.
  • Configure and customize SharePoint Online using out-of-the-box features, Power Platform and approved scripting approaches.
  • Integrate SharePoint solutions with Power Apps, Power Automate, REST APIs, Microsoft Graph and other enterprise systems where required.
  • Participate in solution design, development, unit testing, quality assurance, deployment and post-production support activities.
  • Troubleshoot production issues, analyze root causes and implement fixes or enhancements within agreed timelines.
  • Prepare technical documentation such as Solution Design Document, deployment guide, configuration notes, SOPs and support handover documents.
  • Follow secure coding, coding standards, version control, release management and client delivery processes.
  • Collaborate with onsite and offshore teams, support task estimation and provide technical inputs during sprint planning or project execution.
  • Keep up to date with Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, SPFx and Power Platform features and recommend improvements where applicable.

Experience Required

  • Good communication skills and ability to interact with business users, analysts and technical stakeholders.
  • Minimum 7-10 years of IT development experience with strong hands-on exposure to SharePoint development and Microsoft 365 collaboration solutions.
  • Strong experience in SharePoint Online, Office 365, SharePoint Framework (SPFx), Power Platform and modern SharePoint development.
  • Experience developing SPFx web parts/extensions using React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3 and REST API based integrations.
  • Working experience with SharePoint site architecture, lists, libraries, metadata, search, permissions, page templates and reusable components.
  • Experience with Power Apps and Power Automate for business process automation and workflow enablement.

job.name: Full Stack Developer
job.description:
Saltworks Technologies is a leading Canadian cleantech company solving two of the world's most pressing challenges: water sustainability and critical minerals supply. We design and build advanced industrial water treatment and lithium refining systems for global leaders in semiconductors, mining, automotive, and industrial processing.

Saltworks is a Technology Fast 50 company and EY Entrepreneur of the Year award winner. We lead our industry in adopting and developing automation, autonomy, and AI across our products, projects, and operations. Join us and build skills defining the next era of engineering and industrial systems.

The Role We have an exciting opportunity for a Full-Stack Developer to join our Data Systems team. This team builds the applications, integrations, and data infrastructure that support engineering, manufacturing, and operations across the company. In this role, you will work across the full stack, from front-end interfaces to back-end services and infrastructure, while building AI-powered tools that work with real company systems and data. This is a hands-on position for someone who enjoys working directly with end users and seeing the impact of their work firsthand.

Based onsite at our office in Richmond, BC, this opportunity is open to candidates who live in the Lower Mainland or are willing to relocate. Key Responsibilities

  • Design and build full-stack tools for engineering and corporate teams, such as an interactive plant layout viewer that links each piece of equipment to its documents, tasks, and schedule.
  • Build and deploy AI agents and AI-powered applications that securely interact with company systems and data, such as allowing staff to search and act on engineering and project information using natural language.
  • Connect our ERP, PLM, project management, and data warehouse systems by consuming application APIs, developing secure endpoints, and creating data pipelines that move information where it is needed.
  • Contribute to the infrastructure that supports our internal systems, with attention to how applications, data, and integrations work together.
  • Use AI tools to speed up and improve your own development work.
  • Work directly with system owners and non-technical users to translate business requirements into practical solutions.
  • Write maintainable, well-documented code, handle data responsibly, and participate in code reviews.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve issues across the full stack.
  • Identify opportunities to improve existing workflows through automation and better tooling.

You Will Be a Great Fit If You Have

job.name: Senior Full Stack Engineer
job.description:
We're Optix, and we're building a future where flexible spaces run themselves. Optix (optixapp.com) automates the work behind a flexible space: bookings, billing, access and member communication. Operators in 25+ countries use it to keep their spaces running around the clock, so the people behind them can spend their time where it matters most: welcoming members, elevating the customer experience, and building communities worth belonging to.

Our roots are in coworking, and the idea is already reaching further. Le Birdie, a 24/7 self-service golf venue, runs on Optix. Operators like them show that the old limits on a physical space are changing: the hours it can open, the experiences it can offer and the business it can become.

Our ambition is fully autonomous, human-centred spaces, powered by AI and automation. If you want to shape how people run and experience physical places, this is where you'll do it.

We're looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer to help build the platform operators rely on to run their spaces every day. You'll work across four areas:

  • Product features: shipping full-stack features end to end on our Laravel and Vue stack, with room to build your mobile skills on our native iOS and Android apps
  • AI-powered features: helping Optix evolve from a rules-based platform into a conversational, agentic workspace management system that brings AI to life for operators
  • Platform and security: designing and evolving APIs, resolving security vulnerabilities and helping move a proven product to a cleaner, API-first architecture
  • Reliability: owning priority bug fixes and taking part in on-call

You'll use AI tools daily and work closely with our Engineering Lead, Product and Design, with real influence over technical design and direction.

You'll get hands-on experience building agentic AI into a product people use every day, at a profitable SaaS company where your work ships quickly and makes a visible difference.

Location: Hybrid, for someone based in Vancouver, BC. You'll spend 60% of your time in our waterfront Gastown office and 40% working from home.

What You'll Do

  • Work AI-first: AI writes the majority of our code. You direct Claude and other tools, then steer, review and raise the bar on what ships
  • Design and evolve the REST and GraphQL APIs our iOS and Android apps depend on, with care for backward compatibility across releases
  • Modernize our established Laravel and Vue codebase: migrate from legacy frameworks, reduce technical debt and grow test coverage
  • Resolve security and risk tickets by remediating vulnerabilities and upgrading to current framework, language and dependency versions
  • Build agentic AI features with an intuitive UI, and partner with our Engineering Lead and Product Manager on evaluation and monitoring in LangSmith
  • Investigate and fix complex escalated bugs, including rare edge cases across a large client base, and take part in our on-call rotation

job.name: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
job.description:
SentiLink helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role As a Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack you will be responsible for the development and maintenance of our web application and platform that is used for Fraud analysis. You will be working closely with Product & Design, Solutions Engineering, Data Science, Infrastructure and the Data Platform teams to build new products and enhance our existing suite of products.

This is a remote, US-based role.

Technologies React, Golang, Python, PostgreSQL (RDS), Docker, AWS technologies (Lambda, Cognito and other standard technologies)

job.name: Software Engineer
job.description:
Craftbridge Digital builds web apps, API integrations and automation scripts for businesses, and keeps their older software running. We're based in Austin.

We're hiring a Software Engineer. Full-time, remote from anywhere in the United States.

A typical ticket: a client's order form has to push data into their accounting system, and nobody wrote down how the old sync worked.

You read the code that's there, write the new piece, test it against a copy of their data and ship it with a short note on what changed.

Most of our work is TypeScript and Node on the back end, React on the front and Postgres or SQL Server underneath. Some clients still run PHP or C#. You'll touch those too.

Every change goes through code review. You review other people's pull requests and they review yours.

You've shipped code in at least one of those languages, at work, in an internship or in a project we can look at.

You use Git and can write a SQL query with a join.

You've called a REST API from code and handled what comes back when it fails.

Nice if you've written tests, used Docker or worked with the Stripe, QuickBooks or Salesforce APIs.

Benefits: medical, dental and vision for you and your family, a 401(k) with a company match, paid time off and sick days, a yearly learning budget, plus a laptop and home office gear.

What we read first: your CV, then a repo or something you built. A few lines on the hardest bug you fixed are plenty.

Craftbridge Digital is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

job.name: Software Development Engineer Intern - Summer 2027 (USA)
job.description:
Description Application deadline: Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis

Shape what comes next | Discover careers in Tech

At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. This is an environment where you learn by building. Whether you're creating cloud-native solutions, optimizing machine learning models, or building products that drive experiences for millions of customers around the globe, your work reaches the world, fast. You'll take ownership early, collaborate across teams and disciplines, and grow your skills as you tackle new problems. There's no single path forward here, with a chance to explore different directions and shape your journey as you go. This is where ambition meets opportunity and, where the impact of what you build helps define what comes next, for customers and for you.

What's in it for you? An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You'll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? Do you enjoy working on scalable services in a collaborative team environment? Do you want to see your code directly impact millions of customers worldwide?

At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Customer obsession is part of our company DNA, which has made us one of the world's most beloved brands.

Our SDE interns use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. The challenges SDE interns solve at Amazon are meaningful and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products globally. We seek individuals passionate about creating new products, features, and services while managing ambiguity in an environment where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years.

At Amazon, we believe in ownership at every level. As a SDE intern, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code - from design through deployment and ongoing operations. This ownership mindset, combined with our commitment to operational excellence, ensures we deliver the highest quality solutions for our customers.

We're looking for curious minds who think big and want to define tomorrow's technology. At Amazon, you'll grow into the high-impact engineer you know you can be, supported by a culture of learning and mentorship. Every day brings exciting new challenges and opportunities for personal growth.

job.name: Senior Product Engineer, Full Stack
job.description:
SentiLink helps institutions and protects customers by accurately resolving identities and flagging fraud risk. Each day, we verify more than 3 million identities, flagging 150k+ fraud attempts in the process. The problems we work on are challenging, and solving them takes deep domain expertise, rigorous analysis, and a willingness to dig into the details.

At SentiLink, you'll work alongside smart, highly collaborative colleagues who respect each other's time and judgment, take ownership, and follow through on their commitments. Together, we do truly meaningful work protecting the identities of innocent consumers and flagging the fraudsters attempting to exploit them.

We're well capitalized and growing quickly. We already serve 13 of the top 15 U.S. banks, we're expanding into new markets, and we're backed by Craft Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, NYCA, and Max Levchin. We've been named to the Forbes Fintech 50 and as a 2026 FICO Industry Vanguard Decision Award Winner. We were also the first company to go live with the electronic Consent Based Social Security Number Verification (eCBSV) service, and we've testified before the U.S. Congress on the future of identity.

We want SentiLink to be the best place you've ever worked. We offer generous benefits and support a range of working arrangements, from fully remote to in-office. We are a digital-first company with strong collaboration across the U.S. and India, and we meet in person regularly to build relationships. We have offices in Austin, San Francisco, New York City, Seattle (Bellevue), Los Angeles, and Chicago in the U.S., and in Gurugram (Delhi) and Bengaluru in India.

Role As a Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack you will be responsible for the development and maintenance of our web application and platform that is used for Fraud analysis. You will be working closely with Product & Design, Solutions Engineering, Data Science, Infrastructure and the Data Platform teams to build new products and enhance our existing suite of products.

This is a remote, US-based role.

Technologies React, Golang, Python, PostgreSQL (RDS), Docker, AWS technologies (Lambda, Cognito and other standard technologies)

With a team of over 500 professionals across various specialties, we've built scalable pharmacy, telemedicine, and e-commerce platforms using cutting-edge technology. job.description:
About Leo Berwick *Who we are:* Leo Berwick is an innovative mergers and acquisitions consulting firm. We are comprised of top tier, experienced advisors from global law and accounting firms that add value to transactions as trusted partners throughout the deal life cycle. At Leo Berwick, we hire the best and the brightest. Our teams deliver a dedicated and customized service to every client.

As a growth-stage company, we move quickly, work collaboratively, and value people who take initiative and thrive in a fast-paced environment. Our culture is grounded in high performance, continuous learning, and the shared ambition to build something exceptional, together.

What We’re Looking For Leo Berwick is looking for a Head of Engineering to join our technology team, reporting to the Chief Technology Officer. This role is based in the Greater Toronto Area, Ontario, with a hybrid work arrangement of 2 days per week in office.

We’re looking for a deeply technical engineering leader who has built and scaled products in fast-moving SaaS environments and personally led the architecture and delivery of production agentic AI solutions. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can move comfortably between architecture, engineering delivery, and team leadership, and who has the technical credibility to coach and develop experienced Staff and senior engineers.

The Head of Engineering will own end-to-end software development and lead the architecture, delivery, and scaling of our technology platforms. Working closely with senior leadership, engineers, and internal subject matter experts, this individual will lead a small, experienced engineering team across onshore and offshore locations. With an established platform foundation, direct access to internal users, and subject matter expertise already available, the team can build and test products immediately. As the business evolves, the role may expand into leadership of distinct SaaS product areas, with scope to grow into leadership of distinct SaaS product areas.

*You’re the right fit for this role if you –*

  • Take ownership, make sound decisions, and turn ambitious product goals into delivered solutions.
  • Thrive in a fast-moving, evolving environment while maintaining strong engineering discipline.
  • Communicate openly and clearly with technical teams, business leaders, and other stakeholders.
  • Invest in coaching others and building a collaborative, accountable, high-performing team.

What You'll Do *Engineering strategy and architecture*

  • Own end-to-end engineering execution across the platform, from technical planning through development, release, and continuous improvement.
  • Lead architecture decisions and governance across scalable, reliable systems, including oversight of data engineering capabilities.
  • Partner with business leaders and subject matter experts to translate complex needs into achievable product and technical roadmaps.

job.name: Manager, Performance Engineering
job.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA is looking for a Performance Engineering Manager to manage a team responsible for understanding, measuring, and improving performance across some of our most important computing platforms and workloads. Our Performance Engineering organization works across Consumer and Enterprise products, AI workloads, and emerging areas including Physical AI and Robotics. In this role, you will lead experienced performance engineers working at the intersection of hardware, software, applications, and system performance. You will help establish performance priorities and methodologies, guide complex technical investigations, and ensure our performance results provide clear and actionable insights to engineering, product, and business teams. This is an opportunity to develop a strong technical team while influencing the performance and direction of current and future NVIDIA products.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Lead, develop, and grow a team of performance engineers responsible for benchmarking, performance characterization, data analysis, automation, and product readiness!
  • Define performance priorities, methodologies, and execution plans while building strong working relationships with engineering, product, and business teams across NVIDIA's global sites and time zones.
  • Guide the development of benchmarks, workloads, test methodologies, and automation used to evaluate current and future NVIDIA platforms.
  • Provide technical direction for complex performance investigations spanning GPUs, CPUs, memory, storage, networking, operating systems, drivers, applications, and AI workloads.
  • Review performance data and methodology to ensure results are accurate, reproducible, and supported by rigorous analysis.
  • Drive investigations of performance regressions and opportunities, partnering across hardware and software teams to identify root causes and potential solutions.
  • Translate complex performance results into clear conclusions and recommendations that influence product development, software optimization, competitive analysis, and future performance requirements.
  • Coach and develop engineers while evolving Performance Engineering capabilities across Consumer, Enterprise, Physical AI, Robotics, and other emerging platforms and workloads.

What We Need To See

Our technologically advanced warehouses are at the center. They form the invisible back half of Amazon that magically turns your click of a button into a product at your door. Amazon Sortation Technologies are a key part of that solution, enabling the flow of inventory into and out of warehouses and the consolidation of items for a shipment.

Are you ready for a challenge? Would you like to use your engineering or computer science background to optimize and solve complex problem's in Amazon Fulfillment Technologies? The candidate in this role will have an opportunity to own design and development of distributed systems on AWS platform. You will influence system design and implementation to ensure the best user experience for maximum adoption. You will contribute to a wide range of projects in a highly collaborative and fast-paced environment. You will become part of a world-class engineering team solving challenging problems at scale.

A commitment to teamwork, hustle, and strong communication skills are absolute requirements. Creating reliable, scalable, and high-performance services and architectures require exceptional technical expertise. job.name: Security Engineer - Product Security
job.description:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

Security engineers at Spotify help protect our environment and more than 700 million users. Within Platform, our Product Security team evaluates and communicates Spotify's security posture, helping developers and leadership make informed decisions about security risks. We own the vulnerability management platform, supporting the full lifecycle of identifying, attributing, remediating, and reporting security vulnerabilities.

As AI changes how vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited, we're evolving how Spotify responds. We're looking for a Security Engineer to help transform vulnerability findings into reliable, actionable code improvements using agentic AI. You'll build the tools, workflows, and evaluation frameworks that make automated remediation more effective, scalable, and safe, while helping developers focus on building great experiences for our users.

What You'll Do

  • Build and improve agentic AI workflows that turn security vulnerability findings into tested, review-ready code changes for engineering teams across Spotify.
  • Design and implement evaluation frameworks to measure the quality of automated fixes, including correctness, completeness, safety, build and test success, and pull request merge rates.
  • Develop tools and processes to compare remediation approaches, evaluate AI models, and continuously improve the reliability and effectiveness of generated fixes.
  • Research and apply emerging practices in AI-assisted vulnerability remediation, including prompt engineering, context engineering, and vulnerability-specific fix guidance.
  • Identify which vulnerability types are suitable for automated remediation, balancing security impact, technical feasibility, and developer experience.
  • Collaborate with developers and security stakeholders to collect feedback through code reviews, pull requests, support channels, and interactive sessions, using these insights to improve remediation quality.
  • Help shape how Spotify approaches security posture management by building scalable solutions that reduce security risks and make it easier for teams to address vulnerabilities.

Who You Are

job.name: Compiler Engineer for AI Tile-based DSL
job.description:
Job Details Job Description:

The Role and Impact As a Compiler Engineer at Intel, you will design, develop, test, and optimize cutting-edge compiler technologies tailored to Intel architectures, with a focus on compiler middle-end and backend development.

You'll contribute directly to our LLVM- and TileIR-based DSL compiler stack, supporting innovative tile-based programming models and AI workloads running on Intel CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators.

This role offers an opportunity to work with emerging technologies such as TileLang and cuTile, collaborate with experienced compiler engineers, and contribute to software solutions that enable advances in artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.

Business Group The Compiler Technology Innovation team, part of Intel's Data Center Group (DCG), focuses on creating and enhancing software tools for domain-specific programming languages.

The team is expanding its work on tile-based AI DSL compilers and programming models, a strategic area supporting AI workloads across Intel CPU and GPU architectures.

Through collaboration across engineering teams and the compiler community, we develop innovative solutions that advance heterogeneous computing, AI performance, and Intel's broader technology initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, and optimize compiler middle-end and backend features for Intel CPU and GPU architectures.
  • Contribute to the development and optimization of LLVM- and TileIR-based compiler technologies and domain-specific programming languages.
  • Support tile-based AI programming models and compiler development initiatives, including technologies such as TileLang and cuTile.
  • Collaborate with hardware engineering teams to support new processor features, architectures, and AI workloads.
  • Develop, maintain, and enhance compiler technologies and related tools, including Clang, DPC++, and SYCL.
  • Write comprehensive test cases to ensure code coverage, functionality, and reliability.
  • Contribute to compiler optimizations involving parallelization, vectorization, and emerging programming models.
  • Research, identify, and resolve software bugs through debugging, performance analysis, and analytical techniques.
  • Collaborate with internal engineering teams and open-source communities, including Clang and LLVM, to support compiler development and innovation.
  • Support technical discussions and collaboration with external partners and standards groups to contribute to language evolution and industry best practices.

This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship.

Join a team advancing AI compiler technologies and programming models for next-generation computing. You'll have the opportunity to develop your technical expertise while contributing to meaningful projects that support Intel's AI and data center technology strategy.

This role reports into the Corporate IT Security leadership and will work within the IT function and the business to ensure that we meet and exceed the security requirements from Celestica customers. This role will also have to coordinate with external vendors and internal IT teams to ensure that the cybersecurity requirements are met and exceeded.

Detailed Description

Performs tasks such as, but not limited to, the following:

  • Architects, designs, and secures Ai Solutions in multi-cloud environments, specifically focusing on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, and AWS to enable secure deployment of enterprise AI solutions.
  • Setup, maintenance and ongoing governance of various subscriptions to Ai Vendors such as Anthropic and OpenAI, (including AI Fin Ops)
  • Architects, builds, and enforces security guardrails for AI Agents, establishing robust governance frameworks to monitor and control agentic behaviors.
  • Participates in the security review of new applications with Ai Features.
  • Leads the product selection or review for new cloud and AI security technologies, conducting Proof of Concepts (POCs) and technical evaluations
  • Establishes and maintains effective relationships with process owners/sites to proactively assess business risks and develop risk mitigation.
  • Design and Participation in the continued management and maintenance of AI security policies, Standards, guardrails and roadmaps.
  • consumption of internal teams, namely Vertex Ai and Azure AI Foundry.
  • Design AI Guardrails and rules to Secure AI Agents and data.
  • Establishes and maintains effective relationships with process owners to proactively assess AI-related business risks, threats, and mitigation strategies.
  • Designs and implements security controls for SaaS and PaaS AI integrations to ensure continuous data protection, DLP, and regulatory compliance.
  • Communicates governance and compliance objectives, fostering a compliant and risk-aware security culture across internal engineering and product teams.

job.name: Product Engineer - Ads
job.description:
About Faire Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About This Role Faire's Ads team helps brands succeed by putting them in charge of their own growth. We own the brand-facing side of the Ads business: the ads manager, campaign setup, performance reporting, budget retention and expansion, and the trust that keeps advertisers investing with us.

As a product engineer on the team, you'll own features end-to-end: dig into the advertiser's problem, weigh the options, ship, and measure whether it worked. You'll partner with Product, Design, Data Science, and our Go-to-Market team to shape what we build, not just how it gets built.

This is an ideal role for engineers who combine strong product intuition with genuine excitement about AI. You'll go deep on how ads work in a wholesale marketplace, where the advertisers are independent brands and the buyers are the retailers who stock them.

What You'll Do

  • Product ownership: Take advertiser-facing features from problem to launch, including ads manager workflows, campaign controls, and performance reporting.
  • Product judgment: Partner closely with Product, Design, Data Science, Analytics, and Marketing to identify business opportunities and execute on them. Bring customer empathy for brand advertisers, a clear point of view, and a bias for delivering over waiting for a perfect spec.
  • Technical craft: Build scalable systems and product experiences that stay fast and reliable as our advertiser base grows, and contribute to the technical strategy that gets us there.
  • AI fluency: Use AI tooling as a core part of how you deliver impact, from prototyping and coding to reviewing and exploring ideas faster.
  • Data fluency: Instrument what you ship, then use the data to understand advertiser behavior, evaluate experiment results, and guide where we invest next.

Qualifications Must-haves

job.name: Scientifique de données
job.description:
Voici un bref aperçu des tâches et des responsabilités qui vous incomberont :

  • Analyser des ensembles de données complexes et volumineux afin d’identifier des tendances, des occasions et des informations permettant de soutenir les décisions stratégiques et opérationnelles;
  • Concevoir, développer et valider des modèles statistiques et des algorithmes d’apprentissage automatique pour des analyses prédictives, descriptives et prescriptives;

  • Réaliser des expérimentations, notamment des tests A/B, des analyses causales et des mesures d’impact afin de soutenir la prise de décision fondée sur les données;

job.name: Senior Software Engineer
job.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana The Engineering team is responsible for building out the product for bringing this vision to life. We are creating a platform fundamentally driven by AI, which scales to a massive trove of data, and a diverse customer base; it is a complex system that will stretch engineering in many directions.

Shipping products that customers actually adopt, not just products that ship, takes a particular kind of engineering practice. It means starting inside the customer’s workflow rather than at the ticket. It means treating every release as a hypothesis you can prove or disprove. It means reaching for AI as a primary building block, not a feature you bolt on at the end. And it means owning a product end‑to‑end, from the first conversation through the telemetry six months later.

As a Senior Engineer at Altana, that’s the work and you’ll lead others doing it. You’ll embed with product and design, get on calls with users, form hypotheses about where the real pain is, and lead a small team turning those hypotheses into shipped, adopted products. You’ll measure your work in customer outcomes, not commits.

You Will

  • Spend real time with customers. Sit alongside them in their workflows, watch where they get stuck, and translate what you learn into product bets your team is willing to ship behind.
  • Partner with the product team to decide what to build, not just how. Form hypotheses about customer value, design the smallest experiment that could prove them out, and learn fast. Push back on briefs that aren’t grounded in evidence.
  • Take new product surfaces from 0 to 1. Pitch, prototype, ship, and drive adoption with real users. You are as fluent in “did this land?” as you are in “is this maintainable?”
  • Build AI‑native by default. LLMs, agents, evals, retrieval, and modern AI tooling are first‑class building blocks in your stack, not bolt‑ons. You make principled choices about where AI changes the product equation and where it doesn’t.
  • Own end‑to‑end outcomes. From the first customer conversation to telemetry on the dashboard six months later — including the architecture and instrumentation choices that make that telemetry meaningful.
  • Set the technical bar for your team. Review designs and code with a high standard for quality, simplicity, and customer impact, and a low tolerance for engineering work that can't be traced back to a customer outcome.
  • Mentor engineers in customer‑centric, hypothesis‑driven product development. Help them build the instincts to talk to users, run experiments, and tell when a feature is done because it's loved, not because the ticket is closed.
  • Drive technical decision‑making with a bias toward shipping. Choose practical, iterative designs that get a working version in front of customers fast

job.name: Staff Software Engineer
job.description:
Altana is the network for trusted trade. Our AI-powered product network empowers governments and businesses to build a more resilient and secure global economy while keeping trade flowing.

The Opportunity at Altana The Engineering team is responsible for building out the product for bringing this vision to life. We are creating a platform fundamentally driven by AI, which scales to a massive trove of data, and a diverse customer base; it is a complex system that will stretch engineering in many directions.

Shipping products that customers actually adopt, not just products that ship, takes a particular kind of engineering practice. It means starting inside the customer’s workflow rather than at the ticket. It means treating every release as a hypothesis you can prove or disprove. It means reaching for AI as a primary building block, not a feature you bolt on at the end. And it means owning a product end‑to‑end, from the first conversation through the telemetry six months later.

As a Staff Engineer at Altana, that’s the work and you’ll lead others doing it. You’ll embed with product and design, get on calls with users, form hypotheses about where the real pain is, and lead a small team turning those hypotheses into shipped, adopted products. You’ll measure your work in customer outcomes, not commits.

You Will

  • Spend real time with customers. Sit alongside them in their workflows, watch where they get stuck, and translate what you learn into product bets your team is willing to ship behind.
  • Partner with the product team to decide what to build, not just how. Form hypotheses about customer value, design the smallest experiment that could prove them out, and learn fast. Push back on briefs that aren’t grounded in evidence.
  • Take new product surfaces from 0 to 1. Pitch, prototype, ship, and drive adoption with real users. You are as fluent in “did this land?” as you are in “is this maintainable?”
  • Build AI‑native by default. LLMs, agents, evals, retrieval, and modern AI tooling are first‑class building blocks in your stack, not bolt‑ons. You make principled choices about where AI changes the product equation and where it doesn’t.
  • Own end‑to‑end outcomes. From the first customer conversation to telemetry on the dashboard six months later — including the architecture and instrumentation choices that make that telemetry meaningful.
  • Set the technical bar for your team. Review designs and code with a high standard for quality, simplicity, and customer impact, and a low tolerance for engineering work that can't be traced back to a customer outcome.
  • Mentor engineers in customer‑centric, hypothesis‑driven product development. Help them build the instincts to talk to users, run experiments, and tell when a feature is done because it's loved, not because the ticket is closed.
  • Drive technical decision‑making with a bias toward shipping. Choose practical, iterative designs that get a working version in front of customers fast,
